God regarded this army as insignificant {compared with his great power}. {He helped} the Israelites{, and so they} were able to humiliate those soldiers {by defeating them}.
I wish that God, whose sanctuary is on Mount Zion, would rescue the Israelite people! When God makes his people prosperous again, the Israelites, those descendants of Jacob, will be very happy.
God, please use your power to save me {from my enemies}! If you do that, people will realize that I have not done anything wrong.
God, please listen to what I say as I pray to you.
I am praying for your help because even my fellow Judeans are treacherously acting against me. These are violent men, and they want to kill me. They do not respect you. Selah
But God is helping me. The Lord is helping the people who are protecting me so that I stay alive.
My enemies want to do harmful things to me, but God will cause those things to happen to them instead. Because you faithfully do what you promise, destroy them {so that they do not kill me}!
I promise that {when you rescue me,} I will publicly offer a sacrifice to honor you. I will praise you, Yahweh, for how good you are.
I will be able to do this because he rescues me from all my troubles and, as a result, I see that he has defeated my enemies.
God, please listen to me as I pray to you. Please do not ignore me as I am pleading with you.
Please pay attention to me and do what I ask. The things I am praying about are agitating me and making me moan {in distress}.

This is because my enemies are saying things {to threaten me}. Wicked people are attacking me. They are causing me to have great troubles. Because they are so hostile to me, they never stop trying to harm me.
My heart is pounding inside me because I am so upset. I strongly feel many fears because I know that my enemies are trying to kill me.
I am shaking because I am so afraid. The only thing I feel is fear.
I have been thinking, “How good it would be if I had wings like a dove! I would fly away and find a place to rest.
If I could, I would go far away and stay in a desolate area. Selah
I would quickly find a safe place where my enemies could not harm me in the way that a powerful storm causes damage.”

Lord, please destroy my enemies! Make them disagree about what to do {so that they cannot make successful plans against me}. I ask this because I know that they are fighting with people in the city and hurting them.
The fighting is constant, and the people in the city cannot get away from it. Bad people are causing much trouble right in the middle of the city.
These bad people harm others right in the middle of the city. Dishonest people continually deceive and cheat others in the marketplace.
If it were an enemy who was saying bad things about me, I could endure it. If it were someone who hated me who was powerfully opposing me, I could hide from him.
But the person who is doing those things to me is someone I treated not as a subject but as an equal. I knew him well, and we were together often.
We used to talk together in a wonderful way. We also used to go to the temple courtyard together {to worship God} with the other Israelites who gathered there.

My enemies are so wicked in their inner beings that it is as if wickedness lives in their homes {and influences what they do}. So I hope that bad things happen to them that destroy them! I wish that {the earth would open up under them so that} they would go down alive to the place where dead people are.
But I will ask Yahweh, my God, to help me, and he will rescue me.
I will continually pray to him, whether I can express my concerns in words or whether I am only able to moan {as a plea to him}. He will answer my prayer by helping me.
My enemies are coming with many soldiers to fight against me, but God will keep me safe and save my life when we fight a battle.
My enemies have no difficulties in life, so they do not respect God. Selah But God, who has ruled forever, will answer my prayer and punish them as they deserve.
The man I knew well is attacking me even though I was his friend. He should have remained loyal to me, but he has not.

What he said was as easy to believe as butter is easy to swallow, but secretly he hated me. The words he spoke were as soothing as olive oil, but all along he intended to use words to hurt people as sharp swords do.
Depend on Yahweh to help you when you are in trouble, and he will take care of you. He will never allow anyone to destroy people who are righteous.
God, you will cause people who deceive and kill others to die before they have lived half as long as most people do. But as for me, I will trust you {to protect me}.
O God, men are attacking me, so please help me! They keep fighting me and making me suffer.
Many proud enemies are fighting against me, so there is continually someone attacking me.
But whenever I am afraid, I trust you {to help me}.
I praise you, God, because you have promised {to take care of me}. I trust you to do that, so I am not afraid. I know that mere humans will not be able to harm me!
My enemies are continually trying to interfere in my activities. They keep planning ways to harm me.
Together they secretly watch where I am going because they are looking for an opportunity to kill me.
They should not be able to avoid punishment for the wicked things they are doing. O God, in your anger, please defeat all of our foreign enemies!
You have watched me carefully as I have wandered to this place. Please stay close to me as I have sad experiences here. I know that you have watched me closely as I have had these experiences.
When I cry to God for help, my enemies will stop attacking me. I know that will happen because God favors me.
I praise you, Yahweh my God, because you have promised {to take care of me}.
I trust you to do that, so I am not afraid. I know that mere humans will not be able to harm me!
God, I have vowed {that I will thank you publicly when you help me}, so I will offer a sacrifice to thank you.
I will be able to do that because you will have rescued me. No one will have killed me. Because you protect me, I will be able to live in your presence here in this world where people are alive.

O God, please help me! I ask you to do that because I depend on you to protect me. I pray that you will protect me just as a mother bird protects her chicks under her wings. I ask you to do that until the troubles I am having are over.
I am crying {for help} to God, who is greater than all other spirit beings. God will complete what he has begun to do for me.
May he act from where he is in heaven to rescue me. Someone is trying to harm me; may God prevent him from doing that. Selah God is kind and loyal to the people who trust him, so may he help me.
Men who are as dangerous as lions are all around me. I have no safe place to sleep far away from those men who are trying to kill me. They say things about me that make other people want to harm me.
May you have the most glory, God, of anyone in heaven or on earth!

My enemies are trying to capture me, as if they had set out a net to trap me. This has distressed me greatly. Yes, they are trying to capture me, as if they had dug a deep pit along the path where I walk, hoping that I would fall into it. But I believe that God will use what they are doing against them, as if they had fallen into that pit themselves. Selah
God, I trust you completely. So {instead of worrying,} I will sing praises to you.
I will do that enthusiastically. I will begin the day by praising you as I play my harp and lyre.
I will sing songs to praise you, Lord, so that people of other nations can find out about you.
You deserve this praise because your kindness and loyalty are much greater than anything on earth, just as the clouds in the sky are much higher than anything on earth.
May you have the most glory, God, of anyone in heaven or on earth!

You {judges} should not think that you can ensure justice if you do not speak out {to condemn wickedness}. You are not judging cases fairly, and that shows that you are acting only as humans{, not as God’s representatives}.
In fact, you keep thinking about doing things that are wrong. The decisions that you make encourage people to commit violent crimes.
Wicked people do wrong things and tell lies from the time when they are born.
Wicked people harm other people just as poisonous snakes harm people. They do not pay attention to God’s commandments, as if they were cobras that refused to listen
and so did not respond to the music that snake charmers were playing. Even the most skillful charmer could not get them to respond to music.
Yahweh my God, wicked people are as dangerous as young lions, but destroy them as if you were breaking the large teeth of such lions.
Make them disappear like water that flows away. When they try to harm people as if they were shooting arrows at them, keep them from hurting those people, as if those arrows had no heads!
May they be like a snail that dissolves as it moves along. May they be like a baby that never lives on earth because it dies before its mother gives birth to it.

God will punish and destroy them as powerfully as if a whirlwind were carrying them away. He will do that more quickly than thorns can catch fire and heat a pot, even if the thorns are dry, not fresh.

Righteous people will celebrate when they see God punish wicked people. It will be as if wicked people were an army that God destroyed and righteous people were walking triumphantly through the battlefield afterwards.
Then people will say, “It is true that there is a reward for righteous people! It is true that God judges fairly the people who live on the earth!”
My God, please rescue me from my enemies! Protect me from those who want to attack me!
Rescue me from wicked men who are trying to kill me!
Look! They are hiding and waiting for a chance to kill me! Fierce men have gathered to harm me. Yahweh, they are doing that even though I have not done anything that is wrong!
I have not committed any sin, but they are hurrying to get ready to attack me. Please consider my situation and come quickly to help me.

Yahweh, you are the God who commands the heavenly armies. You are the God whom we Israelites worship. So I ask you to take action and punish all the people who do not honor you. Do not act mercifully toward those wicked people who have acted treacherously toward me. Selah
They are like wild dogs that come out in {the cool of} the evening and growl as they roam around this city {looking for scraps of food}.
They make violent threats so loudly that it is as if they are belching. They think, “No one who hears us {will stop us}!”
But you mock them, Yahweh. You scoff at people who do not honor you.
Because you, God, are the one who protects me and makes me strong, I will depend on you.
You, God, are faithfully loving to me, and you will come to help me. You will defeat my enemies so that I can look triumphantly at them.

But do not kill them {right away}. Otherwise, the Israelite people might forget how you punished them. Instead, use your power to make them wander around helplessly, and then destroy them. Lord, you are like a shield that protects us.
The things that they say are sinful. They curse people falsely. May their pride be like a trap that catches them {and keeps them from doing what they are planning}.
Become angry with them and destroy them so that they do not exist anymore. That way people will know that you, God, rule over the Israelite people and the entire world. Selah
They are like wild dogs that come out in {the cool of} the evening and growl as they roam around this city {looking for scraps of food}.
They roam around searching for food. If they do not get enough to eat, they keep roaming around all night.
But as for me, I will sing each morning about how powerful you are. I will sing joyfully about how faithfully loving you are to me. I will sing about how you protect me when I am in danger.
I will praise you, who enables me to be strong, because you, God, protect me and faithfully love me as you promised.
God, you have stopped helping us Israelites! Because you have become angry with us, our enemies have been able to break through our ranks. Please enable us to fight victoriously again!
It is as if you have caused a great earthquake that has split open the ground. Our army is struggling, but please make it strong again.
You have caused us Israelites to experience great difficulties. It is as if you have made us drink strong wine that is making us fall down as if we were drunk.
But you have raised a battle flag for those who honor you. They can rally around it when their enemies attack them. Selah
That way you will rescue the people whom you love. Please answer my prayer and use your power to save us.

God is holy {and does not lie}, and he has said, “I delight in the territory that I have measured and divided up for you Israelites to live in. That territory includes land on the east side of the Jordan River, where the Valley of Succoth is, and land on the west side of the Jordan River, where Shechem is.

I own the region of Gilead {east of the Jordan River}, and I own the territory of Manasseh {west of the Jordan River}. The mighty soldiers of the tribe of Ephraim {who fight to protect Israel} are like my helmet, and I have given Israel a ruler from the tribe of Judah.

The Moabites are my servants, like slaves who wash my feet. I own the land of Edom; it is as if I have thrown my sandal onto it to show that it belongs to me. And you Philistines might shout your battle cry against me{, but I will defeat you}.”
But I still need someone to lead my army to the land of Edom and conquer their {capital} city that has strong walls around it.
It seems that you, God, have stopped helping us Israelites. It seems that you do not enable our armies to defeat our enemies when they march out to fight them.
Any help that human beings could give us would not be at all sufficient. So we need you to help us to defeat our enemies.
If you, God, help us defeat our enemies, then we will be able to fight very valiantly.
O God, I am calling to you for help. Please do what I ask.
I am far from home, and I feel sad, so I am calling out to you {for help}. Please keep me safe, as if you had put me on top of a high rock.
You protect me. You are like a strong tower into which I can go so that my enemies cannot harm me.
I wish I could always be a guest in your home! Keep me as safe as a baby bird is under its mother’s wings. Selah
God, you know that I have solemnly promised to offer sacrifices to acknowledge you, so please help me. You have given me the blessings that belong to people who honor you.
Please allow me, the king of Israel, to live and rule for many years. Please allow my descendants to rule also.
May I reign for a long time as you watch over me. You are faithful, and you keep your promises, so please protect me.
If you do that, I will always sing songs to praise you, and each day I will offer the sacrifices that I promised to give you.
God is the one who saves me from my enemies, and I am waiting quietly for him to do that.
He is the only one who can save me. He protects me as if he were a rock I could climb onto in order to be safe. No one would harm me at all.
My enemies are threatening me, but they will not be able to keep doing that. God will destroy all of them, just as a leaning wall falls down and just as people can push a fence onto the ground.

My enemies are plotting together to do one thing. They want to remove me from my important position. They enjoy telling lies. They say things to bless people, but in their inner beings, they are cursing those people. Selah
Because I am expecting God to help me, I will wait quietly for him alone to do that.
He is the only one who can save me. He protects me as if he were a rock I could climb onto in order to be safe. No one would harm me.
God is the one who saves me and honors me. God is like a huge rock to which I can go to be safe. He makes me strong.
You Israelite people should always trust in God. Pray earnestly to him in his presence. He is the one who keeps us safe. Selah
Certainly, ordinary people lack the power to help, and important people are not as powerful as they seem. If you put them all on a scale, it would be as if they weighed less than air.
It is foolish to expect to get rich by cheating other people or by stealing from them. If you become wealthy, do not rely on your money.
God has said very reliably that he is the one who truly has power.
God is also the one who always keeps his promises. He punishes people who do wrong things but rewards people who do good things.
God, you are the God whom I worship. I greatly desire to be with you. It is as if my body aches for you, just as a person in a dry, hot wilderness greatly desires water.
I have worshiped you in your sanctuary and recognized how powerful and glorious you are.
You are always kind to me, as you promised in your covenant. This is worth more to me than even being alive, so I will always praise you.
I will praise you for as long as I am alive. I will lift up my hands and pray to you.
You satisfy me as if I had just eaten a delicious banquet of rich foods. I will praise you very joyfully.
Sometimes I think about you when I am lying in bed. When that happens, I reflect during the night on how wonderful you are.
{I realize that you are wonderful} because you have always helped me. I sing to you joyfully because I am aware that you protect me just as a mother bird protects her chicks under her wings.
I remain completely loyal to you, and you protect me by your power.
Some people are trying to kill me, but they will die and go to the place where dead people are.
They may die in a battle, and then wild dogs will eat their corpses.

But I, the king {of Israel}, will rejoice in what God has done for me. All those who swear oaths in the name of God will praise him because he will have stopped people from saying things that are not true.
God, please listen to me as I tell you about what worries me. I am afraid of my enemies; please save me from them.
Protect me from what wicked men are planning to do to me. Protect me from that group of men who do evil things.
The hostile things they say are like sharp swords; their cruel words are like arrows.
They are not afraid of anyone. They falsely accuse people who have done nothing wrong. They are like a person who suddenly jumps up from a hiding place and shoots an arrow at someone.
They encourage each other to do the evil things they are planning. They boast about how they have deceived people. They say, “No one will realize what we are doing!”
They carefully plan the wicked things they want to do. They brag, “We have planned this out perfectly!” It is very difficult to know what people are thinking privately.
But God will suddenly judge and punish them, as if he were shooting an arrow at them and wounding them.
The deceitful things they say will get them into trouble. Everyone who sees what happens to them will stay away from them.
People will think about how God has punished them, and they will tell others about it. As a result, people will not dare to be wicked.
People who do what is right will be very happy that Yahweh has punished those wicked people. They will trust Yahweh to protect them. Yes, those who really want to do good things will be glad.
God, when you come to your sanctuary on Mount Zion, you will find that we have been waiting quietly to praise you and to do what we promised we would do to honor you.
Because you help people when they pray, people everywhere will pray to you.
When we feel very badly because we have done wrong things, you forgive our sins and make it as if we had not committed them.
When you invite people to come and worship you in your sanctuary, that makes them very happy! When we come to your sanctuary, we realize how good and holy you are, and that satisfies us completely.
When we pray to you, you do good and powerful things to help us. You are the God who saves us. Even people who live in very remote places on the earth, on the other side of the oceans, trust in you.
You are so strong, you were able to use your power to set the mountains in their places.
When there is a storm at sea, you can calm it and stop its waves from crashing on the shore. In the same way, you can keep nations from causing trouble.
People who live in very remote places on the earth deeply respect you because of the miracles that you perform. People who live all over the world celebrate what you do.
You send rain to make the soil fertile so that it will produce good crops. It is as if you bring water to the fields in a stream. That is how you prepare the earth to produce abundant crops.
You send rain on the plowed fields, and you fill their furrows with water. You soften the hard clods of soil with showers, and you help young plants to grow in the fields.
When harvest time comes, the fields are glorious with crops, as if you had put a golden crown on them. You provide food for people in great abundance.
There is plenty of food for sheep and goats to eat in the pastures where they graze. So many crops grow on the hills that it is as if the hills were celebrating.

Flocks of sheep and goats cover the meadows like a garment, and there is so much grain in the valleys that the ground is not visible. It is as if the meadows and valleys are singing and shouting joyfully.
This is a note for the worship leader: This is a song, a psalm. Everyone on earth should shout joyfully to praise God!
They should sing songs that tell how glorious God is and how much he deserves praise for being glorious.
Everyone should tell God, “You do such amazing things! You are so powerful that your enemies come and bow down fearfully in front of you.
Everyone on earth should worship you and sing to praise you for your excellent character.” Selah
Come and consider what God has done! Think about the amazing things that he has done among people.

He made a dry path through the Sea of Reeds so that our ancestors could walk right through it. They also walked across the Jordan River {when he stopped it from flowing}. After they crossed, they celebrated what God had done, and we should still celebrate that today.
He is so powerful that he rules forever. He observes what all the people groups do, so anyone who considers rebelling against him should not think that he will be able to do that. Selah
People from every nation, praise our God! Praise him loudly so that others will hear you as you praise him.
He has kept us alive, and he has not allowed anyone to destroy us.
God, you have allowed us to experience great difficulties {in order to make us pure}, just as people put silver in a hot fire so they can purify it.
It is as if you allowed someone to catch us in a trap or made us carry a load that was almost too heavy for us.

It is as if you allowed our enemies to trample on us. We experienced troubles that were like walking through fires and floods. But now you have brought us to a place where we are safe and have plenty of food.
God, I have come to your temple bringing offerings for the priests to burn completely on the altar. I am doing what I promised to do for you.
When I was experiencing great trouble, I said that I would bring these offerings to you {if you rescued me}.
So I have brought fat sheep to burn on the altar, and I have also brought bulls and goats. When they are burning, you will enjoy the smell of the smoke. Selah
All you people who deeply respect God, come and listen as I tell you what he has done for me.
I called out to him to help me, and I praised him as I was praying to him.
If I had secretly intended to commit sins, the Lord would not have done what I asked.
{But I did not do that,} so God has done what I asked.
I praise God because he did what I asked him to do. He has continued to be kind to me, as he promised.
May God always be kind to us and bless us. May he consider us favorably. Selah
God, please do that so that all of the people in the world will know how you want them to live and that you are the one who saves them.
May all the people in the world praise you, God!
You judge those nations fairly and show them what they should do. So may they praise you loudly and joyfully! Selah
May all the people in the world praise you, God!
Good crops have grown on our land. May the God whom we Israelites worship continue to give us good harvests.
May God bless us, and may that cause people throughout the world to respect him greatly.
God, take action and chase away your enemies! Make those who hate you run away from you.
Chase your enemies away just as wind blows smoke away. Make bad people go away, God, just as wax melts when it is near a fire.
But make good people happy. May they rejoice when they are in your presence; may they be very joyful.
Sing praise to God! Sing a song for him who even cares for desolate regions. His name is Yahweh; be glad when you are in his presence.
God, who is present in his sanctuary, is like a father to those who are orphans, and he protects widows.

He provides families for those who have no one to live with. He frees prisoners and enables them to be successful. But those who rebel against him will not be successful. It will be as if they live in a place where it is very hard to grow crops.
God, you led your people out of Egypt, and then you marched with them through the desert. Selah
After you did that, the earth shook at Mount Sinai when you appeared to your people. Rain poured down from the sky, and your people worshiped you.
You caused much rain to fall there in the wilderness, and so you enabled good crops to grow again on that land that you gave to us Israelites.
Your people built homes there. You were kind to poor people and provided food for them.

Kings led their armies to fight against the Israelites, but God defeated them and they ran away. The Lord declared victory over them, and a great crowd of Israelite women sang and danced to celebrate. The men who fought against these enemies captured many valuable possessions and brought them back to the women who were at home.

Some men had to take care of the sheep {instead of fighting}, but the soldiers captured enough valuable possessions to give them some as well. They received treasures such as a dove statue with silver wings and feathers shimmering with fine gold.
Shaddai defeated the enemy kings and their armies by making it snow on Mount Zalmon!
Mount Bashan is a very high mountain. It has many peaks.

Because it is such a great mountain, if it could think, it might think that God should have chosen it as the place for his sanctuary. But Yahweh chose Mount Zion instead, and he will always be present there.

God is so powerful that it is as if he has thousands and thousands of chariots. In fact, it is as if he has ten thousands and ten thousands of them! The same God who appeared to the Israelites on Mount Sinai is now present in his sanctuary on Mount Zion.

{After he defeated his enemies,} he went up to the sacred mountain where his sanctuary is. He led many captured prisoners in a victory procession. He received gifts from the enemies whom he had defeated. He even received gifts from those who had rebelled against him. Now Yahweh, our God, will always be present in his sanctuary.
Praise the Lord, who helps us every day as if he were carrying a heavy load for us. He is the God who saves us. Selah
Our God is the God who saves us; Yahweh our Lord is the one who rescues us from dying.
But God will completely destroy his enemies. If anyone continues to behave sinfully, God will destroy that person.
The Lord said, “Even if my enemies try to climb a high mountain to be safe, or even if they try to hide at the bottom of the ocean, I will bring them back
so that you can trample on their heads. Your dogs will lick up the blood that comes out of their heads.”
And now you are parading triumphantly into your sanctuary, God. You are our king, and you are leading a great crowd the way a king does.
There are singers at the front of the parade. Musicians playing stringed instruments are at the back of the parade. In the middle there are girls playing tambourines.
Praise God, you who have gathered together! Praise Yahweh, you descendants of Israel!

People from the tribe of Benjamin, the smallest tribe, are marching first. Leaders and many other people from the tribe of Judah come next. There are even leaders from the {far northern} tribes of Zebulun and Naphtali in the parade.
Our God has made our Israelite tribes strong. God, continue to help us with your power as you helped us in the past.
Since you have now established your sanctuary on a mountain above Jerusalem, kings will send tribute to you there.

Show the king of Egypt that even though he has a powerful army, he cannot defeat you. Many kings who are strong like bulls may gather together. They may form armies from their subject nations, which are like bulls’ calves, {but they will not be able to defeat you either}. Instead, they will come submissively and pay you tribute in silver. Some nations are eager to fight wars; make their armies run away!
Then envoys will come from Egypt {bringing gifts to you}. The ruler of Cush will hasten to send tribute to God.
People of nations throughout the world, sing praise to God! He is the Lord Selah
who dwells above the sky that he created long ago. When you hear thunder, it is as if he is shouting with his very powerful voice.
Proclaim how powerful God is! He is the king who reigns over Israel as he rules powerfully from the sky.
God, you are in your sanctuary, and you are very powerful. This is the God whom we Israelite people worship. He makes us very strong. Praise God!
Please rescue me, God! I am in great danger, as if I were just about to drown in a flood.
It is as if I am sinking in deep mud where there is no solid ground for me to stand on. It is as if I am in deep water and a flood is swirling around me.
I am tired and my throat is dry because I have been calling to you for help for so long. I have been looking for so long for you to come and help me that I have worn out my eyes.

There are people who hate me for no reason. There are so many of these people, it is as if there are more of them than there are hairs on my head! The enemies who want to harm me are powerful, and they are telling lies about me. They are demanding that I pay back things that I did not steal!
O God, you know that I have foolishly disobeyed your laws; you are aware of the sins that I have committed.

But Yahweh my Lord, commander of the heavenly armies, may the wrong things I have done not disappoint the people who trust you. You are the God whom we Israelite people should worship. Please do not let me embarrass those who do worship you.
People have insulted me because I am loyal to you. They have thoroughly humiliated me.
Even my own family members act as if they do not know me.
I care so much about your temple that people are causing trouble for me. People are speaking disrespectfully of you, and it is as if they are also insulting me.
I wept and fasted very sincerely, but they mocked me for doing that.
I wore rough clothing {to show that I was sad}, but they used me as an example of a foolish person.
Even the elders of the city say bad things about me. The drunkards in the city sing insulting songs about me.
But I will continue praying to you, Yahweh. You are always very kind to me, as you have promised. So at the time that you choose, please answer my prayer by rescuing me, since you love me faithfully.
Rescue me so that it will no longer be as if I were sinking in mud. Rescue me from my enemies so that it will no longer be as if I were drowning.
Make it so that it will no longer be as if a flood were swirling around me and I was about to go down to the bottom of deep water. Rescue me so that I do not go to the place where dead people are.
Yahweh, it is so good that you faithfully love me, so please do what I ask. Because you are very merciful, please help me.
I am experiencing much trouble, so please consider my situation and act quickly to help me.
Come and save me; please rescue me from my enemies.
You know personally how people are insulting, shaming, and dishonoring me. You know who all my enemies are.
Their insults have deeply offended me, and I feel very badly. I wanted someone to feel sorry for me and encourage me, but no one did.
Instead, they put poison in my food, and when I was thirsty, they gave me sour wine to drink.
May their own food be like a trap that they walk into! May it harm their health.
May their eyes become dim so that they cannot see anything. May their bodies keep getting weaker.
Become angry with them and punish them! Angrily pursue them until you catch them.
Make them abandon their towns so that no one lives in them anymore.
Do this because they did things to harm people whom you were already disciplining. They said that people whom you were correcting were suffering {because they had done bad things}.
Punish them for every wrong thing they have done. Do not forgive them!
Remove their names from the book that records the names of people who have everlasting life; do not include them in your list of righteous people.
As for me, I am in bad circumstances, and I am suffering. O God, please protect me and save me.
When God does that, I will sing a song to praise God, and I will honor him by thanking him.
When I do that, it will please Yahweh more than if I had sacrificed oxen, yes, he will like that better than if I had offered him full-grown bulls.
Humble people will be happy when they see {that God has rescued me}. This will encourage people who worship God sincerely.
When needy people pray to Yahweh, he does what they ask. He greatly respects people who suffer for him.
May the entire creation praise God: the birds in the sky, the animals on the land, and the creatures in the sea.
May God protect the people who live in Jerusalem and in other places in Judah. May he strengthen their cities so that they keep living in them as their territory.
May the descendants of the people who are loyal to him inherit that territory, and may those who love him live there safely.
Yahweh my God, please act quickly to rescue me!
Some people are trying to kill me. Embarrass them by making them fail to do that. Some people would be happy to harm me. Humiliate them by making them abandon that plan.
Some people are saying that I am suffering because I am a bad person. Make them ashamed of saying that so that they stop saying it.
{Rescue me so that} everyone who is loyal to you will greatly celebrate. Then the people who depend on you to rescue them will keep saying, “God certainly is great!”
But right now I am in very difficult circumstances, so please act quickly to help me, God! Yahweh, you are the one who helps me and saves me, so please help me right away!
You, Yahweh, are the one who keeps me safe. May it always be clear that I was right to trust you.
Because you always do what is right, take action to help me. Consider my situation and save me!
You declare that I will be safe, since you are the one who keeps me safe and protects me, so please be like a huge rock on top of which I can always go to be safe.
My God, please rescue me from what wicked people want to do to me. Rescue me from the power of violent, evil men.
Yahweh my Lord, you are the one whom I confidently expect to help me. I have trusted in you ever since I was young.
I have depended on you for my entire life; you even made sure that I was born safely, so I will always praise you.
It shocks many people to see me now, but you are my mighty protector.
I praise you lavishly throughout the day for how glorious you are.
Please keep helping me now that I have become an old man. Please help me even though I am not strong anymore.
My enemies are saying that they want to kill me, and they are planning together how to do that.
They are saying, “No one will rescue him, since God is not helping him anymore, so we can pursue him and capture him.”
My God, do not neglect me; hurry to help me!
Embarrass the people who want to kill me by making their plans fail. Yes, completely shame and disgrace those who want to harm me!
But as for me, I will always trust you, and I will praise you even more {now than I have in the past}.
I will tell people how you have saved me because you are good. I will do that continually because there will always be more for me to say about this.
Yahweh my Lord, you are the one who gives me great strength. I will recall {to others} how you do what is right in a way that no one else does.
God, you have taught me many things ever since I was young, and I still tell people today about the wonderful things you do.
God, please keep helping me now that I am old and my hair is gray. That way I will be able to tell my descendants how powerfully you have helped me.
God, you do so many great things because you are good, it is as if they have piled up to the sky. There is no one else like you, God!
You have allowed me to experience many very difficult things, and it has seemed as if I was about to go to the place where dead people are, but now please give me a good life again.
Please make me even greater than I was before, and comfort me rather than allow me to have difficult experiences.
When you do that, then I will play my lute and praise you, my God, for faithfully helping me. I will play my harp as I sing to praise you. You are the holy God whom we Israelites worship.
I will shout joyfully while I sing. Because you will have rescued me, I will sing to you wholeheartedly.
You will have defeated and disgraced the people who wanted to harm me, so throughout the day I will describe how you did what was right.
A psalm of Solomon. O God, please enable the man who is now succeeding his father as king to judge cases rightly, as you would do.
Enable him to judge the cases of Israelite people fairly, especially for people who are vulnerable.
May the people live rightly so that they will be prosperous as crops grow abundantly on the hillsides of the land.
Help the king to defend poor people and rescue needy people and defeat those who are oppressing them.
May each successive generation of the people respect you. May they do that for as long as the sun and the moon are in the sky!
May this king make the nation prosperous, just as heavy rains soak the soil and enable more hay to grow after a first cutting.
May people who live rightly prosper during the time when he reigns, and may the nation be very prosperous for as long as the moon is in the sky.
May he rule over all of the surrounding territory, right up to the shores of the seas. May his realm extend from the Euphrates River to the limits of the lands that people know.
May the leaders of the desert tribes bow down in front of him {to acknowledge him as their ruler}, and may his enemies lie facedown on the ground {in submission to him}.
May the kings who rule the land of Tarshish and other coastal areas pay tribute to him. May the king of Sheba and the king of Seba give him gifts.
In fact, may all the kings in the world acknowledge him as their ruler, and may every nation obey him.
May all these things happen because he rescues needy people when they cry out for help and he helps poor people who have no one else to help them.
May he feel compassion for people who are weak and needy and save their lives.
May their lives be important to him so that he rescues them from people who are oppressing and harming them.
May this king live for a long time! May he receive much fine gold. May people always pray for him and ask God to bless him.

May the fields produce such abundant crops that grain grows all the way up to the tops of the hills and sways in the wind like the branches of the trees in Lebanon. May the cities in Israel be as full of people as the fields are full of grass.
May people always remember what a good king this was, for as long as the sun is in the sky! May he do good things for many people, and may the people of other nations say that he has a good life.
Praise Yahweh, the God whom we Israelites worship; he does amazing things that no one else can do.
Praise him forever for how glorious he is! May his glory fill the whole world! Amen! Yes, amen!
This is the end of the prayers that David, the son of Jesse, wrote.
Asaph wrote this psalm. God truly is good to us Israelite people, to those who want to do what pleases God.
As for me, I almost stopped trusting in God; I was almost guilty of committing a great sin against him
because I envied those who proudly acted as if they did not need God, when I realized that they prospered even though they were wicked.
Those people do not suffer; they always have plenty of food to eat.
They do not experience the difficult things that other people do; they do not experience catastrophes and sicknesses like other people.
So they are proud and violent. Their being prideful is like a necklace that they show off to others, and they openly display their violent actions like people openly display the clothes they wear.
Their eyes protrude because their faces are fat, and they are always thinking about more evil things to do.
They scoff at other people, and wickedly talk about doing unjust things to them; they speak pridefully.
They exalt themselves and talk as if they are God in heaven, and they go about the earth talking boastfully.
The result is that people pay attention to them and listen to everything they say.
Wicked people say to themselves, “God certainly does not care what we do; the Most High certainly will not judge us for what we do!”
Look at how these wicked people live; their lives are so easy that they never have to worry about anything, and they are always becoming richer.
{When I saw this I thought that} certainly it is useless that I have thought about things that are pleasing to you and have not sinned.
Every day I suffer, and every morning you punish me.
If I had said these things out loud in front of others, surely I would have been sinning against your people.
When I tried to think about all this, it was very difficult for me to understand it.
But when I went to the temple where people worship God, then I understood what will happen to wicked people in the future.
I know that you make their future insecure; you will cause them to be ruined.
God will suddenly destroy these wicked people; they will die in terrible ways.
Lord, when you act, you will cause the wicked to quickly vanish; they will vanish like a dream which disappears as soon as a person awakes from their sleep.
When I was grieved in my inner being and felt emotionally hurt,
I was stupid and ignorant; I behaved like an animal toward you.
Nevertheless I am always with you; you constantly stay close to me.
You lead me by instructing me, and when I die, you will take me into your glorious presence.
You are the only one I have in heaven! There is nothing on this earth that I desire more than you.
My body and my spirit may become very weak, but God enables me to feel encouraged; he has granted to me that I would belong to him forever.
People who abandon you will perish; you will ruin every person who is not loyal to you.
But for me, the only thing I need is to be close to God. I trust in the Lord Yahweh to keep me safe so that I may tell others everything you have done for me.

A Levite from the clan of Asaph wrote this song. God, it feels as if you have permanently abandoned us! You care for us Israelites the way a shepherd cares for his flock. So please do not continue to be angry with us.
Think about your people whom you chose long ago. You rescued us from slavery so that we would belong to you. Think about Mount Zion, where you have been present {in your temple}.
Come and walk through the ruins of your temple. It seems that no one will ever rebuild it. Look at all the damage that the enemy soldiers did to your temple.
Your enemies shouted in triumph right there in the place where you met with us Israelites. They set up their battle flags to show that they had conquered it.
They acted like woodsmen who were swinging axes to cut down trees in a forest.
They smashed all the carved wooden panels with their axes and hammers.
Then they burned down your temple completely. They treated the temple where you were present as if it were not a sacred place.
They said to themselves, “We will completely subdue the Israelites.” They burned down every place in the land where people gathered to worship God.
You no longer give us any signs, and there are no prophets anymore. None of us knows how long this will last.
God, do not allow your opponents to continue to insult you! Do not allow your enemies to keep treating you with disrespect anymore!
You should not fail to use your great power. Use your power to destroy your enemies!
God, I acknowledge that you have ruled from ancient times. You have been saving people throughout the earth.
By your great power, you pushed back the sea so that the dry land would appear. You created order out of the watery chaos.
It was as if you smashed the heads of a chaos monster that lived in the sea and left his body in the desert for scavengers to eat.
You are able to make springs and streams flow in dry areas, but you are also able to dry up rivers that usually flow all the time.
You determine when it becomes day and when it becomes night. You make it light during the day when the sun shines.
You are the one who set all the boundaries of the earth. You are the one who created the seasons of summer and winter.
Yahweh, remember that your enemies have insulted you and that foolish people have mocked your reputation.
Do not allow cruel enemies to destroy the people whom you cherish. Save the lives of your vulnerable people before it is too late.
People are committing violent acts in places where they think others will not see them. So we need you to help us. Please do that because of the covenant that you made with us.
We are asking you to help us; please do not disappoint us. Then we poor and needy people will praise you for what you have done.
Take action to defend yourself, God! Do not allow foolish people to keep insulting you!
Do not ignore what your enemies are saying. Your opponents keep shouting things against you.
We thank you, God! We thank you because you are close {to us}. We tell people about the wonderful things that you have done.
{You say,} “I have set a time {to judge people}. At that time, I will judge everyone fairly.
The earth may shake, and everyone who lives on it may tremble. But I am the one who holds it steady.” Selah
I warn those who boast, “Stop boasting!” I tell wicked people, “Do not be proud!
Do not brag about your power! Do not speak arrogantly!”
{The one who judges and} honors people does not come from the east, west, or south.
God is the one who judges people; he shames and punishes some people, and he honors other people.

It is as if Yahweh holds a cup {full of punishment} in his hand. It is full of {punishment that is like} foaming wine mixed with spices. He pours it out {to punish the wicked}, and all the wicked people on earth must drink it. {He punishes them fully like} they were drinking the cup to the last drop.
But as for me, I will never stop saying what the God whom Jacob worshiped has done; I will never stop singing to praise him.
God promises this: “I will destroy the power of wicked people, but I will increase the power of righteous people.”
People in Judah know God. He is famous in Israel.
His home is in Jerusalem. He lives on Mount Zion.
There he shattered the flaming arrows. He destroyed the shields, the swords, and the weapons of war. Selah
You are glorious and excellent. You are more majestic than the mountains where you destroyed your enemies.
Enemy soldiers plundered the brave soldiers. They have fallen into their final sleep. None of the warriors were able to lift their hands {to defend themselves}.
When you, the God whom Jacob worshiped, shouted at them, their war horses and their riders fell down dead.
You are the one whom everyone must fear. No one can survive in your presence when you are angry.
You gave your decision from heaven. The whole world was scared and silent.
This happened when you stood up to judge, O God, to rescue all the oppressed people of the world. Selah
Even human anger will bring you praise. You will use the rest of their anger as a weapon.
Make promises to Yahweh your God and keep them. Let everyone around him bring gifts to the Awesome One.
He humbles the leaders, and terrifies all the kings.
I cried out to God; I cried aloud to him, and he listened to me.
When I was in trouble, I prayed to the Lord; all during the night I lifted up my hands {while I prayed}, and I did not stop {praying}. But nothing could comfort me.
When I thought about God, I despaired; as I thoughtfully considered {him}, I became weak and discouraged. Selah
All during the night he prevented me from sleeping; I was so worried that I did not know what to say.
I thought about days that had passed; I remembered what had happened in previous years.
During the night, I remembered the songs that I used to sing; I thoughtfully considered, and I pondered these things:
{I feared that} the Lord would reject {me} forever and that he would never be kind {to me} again.
{I wondered whether} {the Lord} had completely stopped being faithful and had broken his promise to all future generations.
{I asked myself whether} God had forgotten to be gracious {and whether} his anger had caused him to stop being compassionate. Selah
I said, “What causes me to be sad the most is that it seems that God, who is greater than any other spirit being, is no longer using his power for us.”
But then, Yahweh, I recall your great deeds; I remember the wonderful things that you did in the past.
I contemplated all that you have done, and I thought carefully about your mighty acts.
God, everything that you do is amazing; there is certainly no god who is great like you are!
You are God, the one who performs miracles; you showed to the people of many people groups that you are powerful.
By your power you rescued your people {from Egypt}; you saved those who were descendants of Jacob and his son Joseph. Selah
It was as though the waters saw you and became very afraid, and even the deepest part of the water shook.
Rain poured down from the clouds; it thundered very loudly, and lightning flashed in all directions.
Thunder crashed in the whirlwind—your voice! Lightning lit up, and the earth shook violently.
Then you walked through the sea in a path that you made through the deep water, but your footprints could not be seen.
You led your people as a shepherd leads his flock of sheep while Moses and Aaron were the leaders of your people.
A song of Asaph. My friends, listen to what I am going to teach you; pay careful attention to what I will say.
I am going to give you some sayings that wise people have said. They will be sayings about things that happened long ago, things that were difficult to understand.
These are things that we have heard and known previously, things that our parents and grandparents told us.
We will tell these things to our children, but we will also tell our grandchildren to praise Yahweh for his power and the glorious things that he has done.
He gave requirements and instructions to the Israelites, those who are descended from Jacob, and he told our ancestors to teach them to their children.
He commanded this so that their children would also know them and so that they would teach them to their own children.
In that way, they also would trust in God and would not forget the things that he has done; instead, they would obey his commandments.
They would not be like their ancestors, who were very stubborn and kept rebelling against God; they did not continue firmly trusting in God, and they did not worship him alone.
The soldiers of the tribe of Ephraim had bows and arrows, but they ran away from their enemies on the day that they fought with their enemies.
They did not do what they had agreed with God that they would do; they refused to obey his laws.
They forgot what he had done; they forgot about the miracles that they had seen him perform.
While our ancestors were watching, God performed miracles in the area around the city of Zoan in Egypt.
Then he caused the Sea of Reeds to divide, causing the water on each side to pile up like a wall, with the result that our ancestors walked through it on dry ground.
He led them by a bright cloud during the day and by a fiery light during the night.
He split rocks open in the wilderness and gave to our ancestors plenty of water from deep inside the earth.
He caused a stream of water to flow from the rock; the water flowed like a river.
But our ancestors continued to sin against God; in the desert they rebelled against the one who is greater than any other spirit being.
By demanding that God give them the food that they desired, they tried to find out if he would always do what they requested him to do.
They insulted God by saying, “God surely cannot supply food for us here in this desert.
It is surely true that Moses struck the rock, and God made a huge amount of water gush out, but we, his people, {doubt} that he can also provide bread and meat for us.”
So when Yahweh heard that, he became very angry, and he sent a fire to burn up some of his Israelite people.
He did that because they did not trust in him, and they did not believe that he would rescue them.
But God spoke to the sky above them and commanded it to open like a door,
and then food fell down like rain, food that they named “manna.” God gave them grain from heaven.
So the people ate the food that angels eat. God gave to them all the manna that they wanted.
Later, he caused the wind to blow from the east, and by his power he also sent wind from the south.
The wind brought birds to eat which fell like rain. They were as uncountable as the grains of sand on the seashore.
God caused those birds to fall in the middle of their camp. There were birds all around their tents.
So the people {cooked the birds and} ate the meat; their stomachs were full because God had given them what they wanted.
But they had not yet eaten all that they wanted,
when God angrily killed some of their strongest men. He even sent young Israelite men to their graves.
In spite of all this, the people continued to sin; in spite of all the miracles that God had performed, they still did not trust that he would take care of them.
So he shortened their lives so they seemed to only be a few days or like they were gone as quickly as a breath of air, and he terrified them during even those few years.
Whenever God caused some of the Israelites to die, the others would repent; they would be sorry and seriously ask God to save them.
They would remember that God was like a huge rock on which they would be safe, and that he, who was greater than any other spirit being, was the one who would buy them back.
But they tried to trick God by lying to him.
They were not loyal to him; they did not keep the promises between God and them.
But God acted mercifully toward his people. He forgave them for having sinned and did not get rid of them. Many times he decided not to become angry with them and did not furiously punish them.
He remembered that they were only humans who die, humans who disappear as quickly as a wind that blows by and then is gone.
Many times our ancestors rebelled against God in the wilderness and made him very sad.
Many times they did evil things to find out if they could do those things without God punishing them. They frequently caused the holy God whom the Israelites worship to become sad.
They did not remember how powerfully he had acted, and they {forgot} about the time when he rescued them from their enemies.
They forgot about all the wonderfully powerful things he did near Zoan in Egypt.
He turned the rivers of {Egypt} to blood, so that the people could not drink their streams.
He sent swarms of flies among the people of Egypt that bit them, and he sent frogs that destroyed everything.
He gave their crops to the locusts. He let swarming locusts eat everything they had worked for.
He killed their grape vines with hail, and killed their sycamore trees with frost.
He sent a terrible thunderstorm with hail to kill all their domestic animals.
Because God was fiercely angry with the people of Egypt, he caused them to be very distressed. The disasters that struck them were like a group of angels that destroyed everything.
He let himself be angry with them, and he did not prevent them from dying; he sent a serious illness that killed many of them.
In that plague he caused all the firstborn sons of the people of Egypt to die.
Then he led his people out of Egypt like a shepherd leads his sheep, and he guided them like a flock in the desert.
He led them safely, and they were not afraid, but their enemies drowned in the sea.
Later God used his power to bring the Israelite people to the land he had set apart, to this hill country that he had taken for himself.
He drove out the people groups as the Israelites advanced; he distributed the land for each tribe to possess as their own, and he settled the tribes of Israel in the homes of those peoples.
But the Israelites defied the God who is greater than all other spirit beings and disobeyed him to see what he would do. They did not obey what he had required them to do.
They turned away and were unfaithful, just as their ancestors had been; they were as unreliable as a bow that does not shoot straight.
They made God angry by worshiping at shrines on the hilltops, and they made him jealous by worshiping carved idols.
When God saw what they were doing, he became very angry and completely rejected the Israelite people.
He stopped living at Shiloh, the place where he had set up his tent and lived among people.
He let enemies capture the sacred chest which showed how strong and glorious he was.
He let enemies kill his people in battle, because he was very angry with the people who belonged to him.
Fire destroyed the young men, and no one sang wedding songs for the young women.
Enemies killed the priests in battle, and the wives they left behind were not able to mourn for them.
Then the Lord acted as though he had been sleeping and had woken up, like a warrior who becomes alert after drinking wine.
He drove his enemies back and disgraced them forever.
He did not choose the descendants of Joseph to be the leading tribe, and he did not choose the tribe of Ephraim.
Instead he chose the tribe of Judah whose capital is on Mount Zion, which he loves.
He had them build his temple there, high up like the heavens, and he established it to last as long as the earth.
He chose David, who served him, and took him away from tending the sheep.
He took David from caring for the mother sheep and their lambs and appointed him to lead the people of Israel, the people who belonged to God.
David led them with a sincere and devoted heart, and he guided them with great skill.

A Levite from the clan of Asaph wrote this song. God, foreign nations have invaded the land that belongs to you. They have made your holy temple unfit for worship, and they have made Jerusalem a pile of ruins.
They left the dead bodies of the people who were faithful to you for birds and wild animals to eat.
They killed so many of your people that blood flowed like water all around Jerusalem. There were not enough people still alive to bury them.
The people of the nations around us insult us and laugh at us.
Yahweh, please do not stay so very angry with us, even though we sinned against you by worshiping other gods.
The people of other nations do not honor you as God. You should be angry with them and punish them,
because they are the ones who have killed so many Israelites and destroyed the land in which they lived.
Please forgive the wicked things we did in the past. Quickly be merciful to us, because we are desperate.
God, you are the one who saves us, so please help us! Do that for the sake of your glorious reputation. Forgive us for our sins so that people will honor you.
Do not let the other nations say, “Their God was not able to help them!” We want to see you punish those nations for killing the people who serve you.
Listen to the moans of your people who are now captives, and use your great power to save those who are about to die.
Lord, pay back our neighbors directly, seven times over, for the insults they have spoken against you!
Then we will always thank you. You care for us, your people, the way a shepherd cares for his sheep. Each generation of Israelites will tell their children how wonderful you are.

God, you are like a shepherd to the people of Israel, so please listen to me. You lead the descendants of Joseph the way a shepherd leads his flock. You were present with us in your temple above the statues of the cherubim; reveal your glory to us again!
Just as you moved powerfully through the wilderness right ahead of the tribes of Ephraim, Benjamin, and Manasseh, come powerfully once again and save us.
God, make us strong again. Regard us favorably and save us.
Yahweh, you are the God who commands the heavenly armies. You have been angry with us, and so you have not been doing what we ask when we pray to you. But please now answer our prayers.
You have caused us to experience constant sorrow. It feels as if you are punishing us three times as much as we deserve.
The nations around us have become hostile to us, and our enemies make fun of us.
God, you who command the heavenly armies, make us strong again! Regard us favorably and save us.

You brought your people out of Egypt as if you were transplanting a vine from there. You forced other nations to leave this land and you allowed your people to settle in it, as if you were planting that vine here.
You removed the foreign nations, just as a farmer clears the ground for a new plant. This enabled your people to become a strong nation that occupied the entire country.
It was as if that vine became so large that its shadow darkened the mountains and its branches were like great cedar trees.
They controlled the territory from the Great Sea in the west to the Euphrates River in the east.
But now you have allowed enemies to invade and conquer us, as if you had torn down a fence that protected that vine, so that everyone who walked past it could take whatever fruit they wanted from it.
Those enemies have destroyed the country, as if a wild boar had chewed up that vine and wild animals ate what remained.
God, commander of the heavenly armies, please help us again! Look down from heaven and see what is happening to us! Come and care for your people, who are like a vine that you planted
and worked hard to make sure that it would grow well. Your people are also like your own son whom you helped grow up to be strong.
But now, because you do not regard them favorably, their enemies are destroying them as if someone had cut down that vine and burned it.
Even though we are human, we are like your own son whom you helped grow up to be strong, so please help us with your power. Restore us to a position of honor.
Then we will not worship other gods again. Give us new life, and we will worship only you.
Yahweh, the God who commands the heavenly armies, make us strong again! Regard us favorably and save us.
Sing joyfully to God, who makes us strong! Shout with joy to the God whom we Israelites worship!
Start playing music! Beat tambourines and play lyres and pleasant-sounding harps.
Blow a ram’s horn for the new-moon festival {each month} and on the day of the full moon when the Festival of Shelters begins.
Do this because the God whom we Israelite people worship has commanded us to do it.
God told our ancestors to observe these festivals when he delivered them from slavery to the Egyptians, a people whose language they did not understand.
{Yahweh says,} “They had to hold on to heavy baskets full of bricks as they carried them on their shoulders, but I freed them from doing that.

When they were suffering, they cried to me for help, and I rescued them. {At Mount Sinai,} I spoke to them from dark clouds {and gave them laws}. Then I saw whether they trusted me when they complained at Meribah that they had no water. Selah
Listen to me, my people, while I warn you! I wish that you Israelites would pay attention to me!
You must not make any idols that represent any of the gods that other nations worship. You must never bow down to worship any of those gods.
I am Yahweh your God. I am the one who rescued you from slavery in Egypt. If you depend on me, I will provide everything that you need.
However, my people would not listen to what I said; the Israelites refused to obey me.
So I let them do whatever they stubbornly wanted to do; they did whatever they had decided to do.
I wish that my people would obey me! Yes, I wish that the Israelites would live the way I want them to!
Then I would use my power against those who are opposing them, and I would easily defeat their enemies.
Then those who had rebelled against Yahweh would bow down fearfully in front of him {to submit to his authority}. But the Israelites would always prosper.
I would make their fields produce abundant crops, and they would even find all the honey they wanted in wild bee hives in rocky places.”
A Levite from the clan of Asaph wrote this song. God has taken his place in the assembly that he governs; he pronounces judgment on the rulers there.
He says, “You must stop making unjust decisions and favoring wicked people! Selah
Defend poor people and orphans, and decide cases fairly for people who have no one else to help them.
Save defenseless people from what wicked people want to do to them!
You are foolish and ignorant! You do not recognize the right things to do. People are no longer living by the basic principles that make a society fair.
I said, ‘You are spiritual beings; you are all rulers over creation like the Most High.
But you will die as humans do; you will lose your power just as rulers do.’”
God, you rule all the nations, so take action and judge the people who live on the earth!
God, please take action to help us! Please do that right away!
I ask this because the enemies who hate you are defiantly approaching us with a large army.
They have plotted deviously together to fight against us Israelites whom you cherish.
They have said to each other, “Come on, let us destroy them so completely that no one will ever remember that Israel existed!”
They have all agreed to do this, and they have made an alliance against you.
This army includes soldiers who are Edomites, Ishmaelites, Moabites, Hagrites,
Gebalites, Ammonites, Amalekites, Philistines, and Tyrians.
The Assyrians are helping them. They have given military support to the Moabites and Ammonites {who are leading this army}. Selah
Defeat them just as you helped Gideon defeat the Midianites, and just as you helped Barak defeat Sisera{, the commander of the Canaanite king} Jabin at the Kishon River!
You destroyed those Canaanites at En Dor, and their dead bodies rotted on the ground.
Kill the leaders of this invading army just as Gideon killed Oreb and Zeeb, the Midianite commanders. Defeat all their rulers just as Gideon defeated Zebah and Zalmunna{, the Midianite rulers}.
They too had said, “Let us take for ourselves the land where God’s people dwell.”
My God, please defeat them so that they run away just as tumbleweed rolls away and just as chaff flies away in the wind!
Just as a forest fire burns down trees and flames burn up the dry vegetation on hillsides,
make them run away afraid as if a great storm were driving them off.
Completely disgrace them so that they will acknowledge who you are, Yahweh.
Embarrass them and make them always afraid. Humiliate them until they die.
Then they will know that you alone, Yahweh, are the Most High God who rules over everyone in the world.
Yahweh, commander of the heavenly armies, what a wonderful place your temple is!
I long greatly, deep inside, to be in the courtyards of Yahweh’s temple. With my whole being I call out to the only true God.
Even little birds have built their nests near your temple, and that is where they are taking care of their babies. Yahweh, commander of the heavenly armies, you are my king and my God.
What a good life people have who live by your temple! They worship you continually there. Selah
What a good life people have whom you make strong so that they can travel to your temple as they greatly desire!
As they pass through the {arid} Valley of Baca, they dig wells to look for water, and God sends autumn rains that fill those wells with life-giving water.
They become stronger as they go, and each of them arrives at the temple in Zion where God is present.
Yahweh, you are the God who commands the heavenly armies. Please answer my prayer. You are the God whom we Israelite people worship. Please do what I ask. Selah
God, please treat favorably the king you have appointed to protect us.

It is better be in your temple courtyards for a single day than to be anywhere else for a thousand days. I would rather stand at the entrance to the courtyard of my God’s temple than stay in any of the {comfortable} homes where wicked people live.

Yahweh our God makes us prosper, just as the sun makes crops grow, and he protects us, just as a shield protects a warrior. He is kind to us and honors us. Yahweh gives people who live rightly every good thing that they need.
Yahweh, commander of the heavenly armies, what a good life people have who trust you!
Yahweh, you have brought back the Israelites who were exiles so that this land can be prosperous again.
You forgave all the sins that your people committed. Selah
You completely ceased being angry with us and stopped punishing us severely.
God, you are the one who saves us. Please stop being upset with us, and make us strong again.
Please do not be continually angry with us and with our children and grandchildren.
Please help us so that we will thrive again. Then we, your people, will be happy because of you.
Yahweh, please treat us kindly as you promised and rescue us from our troubles.
I am going to listen to what Yahweh, my God, says to me. I believe he will say that he will make his people thrive if they are loyal to him. However, they must not do foolish things anymore.
He is surely ready to help people who deeply respect him. Then he will be gloriously present with us in our land.
He will be faithfully kind and true to us. He will do what is right and make us peaceful.
People on earth will be faithful to God, and God will act justly toward us from heaven.
Yes, Yahweh will give us good things, and our land will produce abundant harvests.
As he considers what to do, he will recognize what the right thing is to do, and he will do that.
A prayer of David. Yahweh, I am poor and helpless, so please do what I ask.
I am loyal to you, so please protect me. I worship you as my God and I trust you, so please save me.
I have been crying out to you continually, Lord, so please be kind to me.
I am asking you to help me, Lord, as someone who worships you, so please make me happy by doing that.
Do this, Lord, because you are good and you forgive people’s sins. You very faithfully love everyone who prays to you.
Yahweh, I am pleading with you in prayer to help me; please do what I ask.
Whenever I am in trouble, I call out to you, because I know that you will help me.
Lord, among all the gods that the nations worship, there is none like you; none of them has done the great things that you have done.
Lord, the nations that you have made will all come and bow down before you, and they will praise you.
They will do this because you are great and you do amazing things; you are the only true God.
Yahweh, please teach me how you want me to live so that I will act properly, as you wish. Give me a sincere desire to honor you.
Lord my God, I will thank you wholeheartedly, and I will praise you forever.
I will do that because you have been so faithfully kind to me; you have kept me from going way down into the place where dead people are.
God, proud people are attacking me. Yes, a group of cruel people is trying to kill me; those people do not respect you.
But you, Lord, are a God who is merciful and kind. You do not quickly become angry, and you are so faithfully kind and true to us.
Consider my situation and be kind to me; make me, your servant, strong. Help me as if I had been born in your household.
Do something to show that you are helping me so that my enemies will see it, and it will embarrass them. I believe that you, Yahweh, will help me and comfort me.
One of the Korahites wrote this song. Yahweh established his city on mountains that he made holy.
He loves the city of Zion more than any other place where Israelites live.
People say wonderful things about this city that belongs to God. Selah

{Yahweh says,} “When I talk about people who know me, this will include Egyptians and Babylonians. Indeed, I will also say about Philistines and Tyrians and Cushites, ‘This person is a native of Zion.’”
People will say about Zion, “Every one of those people is a native of that city,” and God Most High will personally keep Zion strong.
When Yahweh registers each of those people, he will record, “This person is a native of Zion.” Selah
Singers and musicians {will celebrate and say}, “Zion, everything that makes me flourish comes from you!”
Yahweh, you are the God who saves me. I continually ask you to help me.
Please pay attention to what I am saying as I pray to you.
I ask this because I have experienced so many bad things that I cannot endure any more; I am about to die and go to the place where dead people are.
People expect me to die soon because I have so little strength left.
It is as if I belong among dead people who are lying in their graves. It seems that you are no longer aware of such people and you stop taking care of them.
It is as though you have thrown me down to the bottom of a deep, dark pit.
I feel as if you are angry with me, and that is like an oppressive burden to me. It is as if I am drowning in your anger. Selah
Because my illness is so unpleasant and you have not healed me, my friends stay away from me, and I am not able to leave my home {to visit anyone}.
My eyes are swollen because I cry so much. Yahweh, throughout the day I call out to you for help as I spread out my hands toward you {in prayer}.
If I were to die, it would be too late for you to do a miracle to help me. Dead people do not come back to life and praise you! Selah
Dead bodies in graves do not talk about how you faithfully love us. In the place where dead people go, no one talks about how faithful you are.
No one in that dark place sees the amazing things you do; no one in the place where no one remembers anything knows how good you are.
But I {am still alive,} Yahweh, and I am calling out to you to help me. It is as if my prayer is already there waiting for you when you get up in the morning.
Yahweh, please do not reject me! Please do not ignore me!
Since I was young, I have been so ill that I have nearly died. I have been sick for so long with this terrible illness that you permit that I have no more hope.
I feel as if you are very angry with me. This terrible illness that you permit has destroyed the good life I could have had.
The bad things that are happening to me are like floodwaters that continually surround me and are about to drown me.
Because you have allowed this illness, my friends and family members stay away from me. I can no longer see where they are.
Yahweh, I will always sing about how faithfully you love your people. I will tell my children and grandchildren that you always do what you promise.
I know that you will always love us faithfully. Just as the sky is permanent, so you will always be faithful to us.
Yahweh has said, “I made a covenant with the man I chose {to be the king of Israel}. That was David, who loyally obeyed me. I made a solemn promise to him.
I said, ‘I will make sure that your descendants always rule as kings; yes, I will make sure that your dynasty never ends.’” Selah
Yahweh, the angels in heaven praise you for the wonderful things you do, When those holy beings gather, they celebrate how you always do what you promise.
No one in the sky is equal to Yahweh! None of the heavenly beings is like Yahweh!
When the holy beings gather together, they all respect God greatly. Everyone around his throne honors him.
Yahweh, you are the God who commands the heavenly armies. No one is as mighty as you are! You are always faithful in every way.
You control the sea so that it does not become too violent; when its waves become too large, you make them smaller.
It was you who {put the world in order as you created it, as if you had} completely destroyed the sea monster Rahab; You used your great power to defeat your enemies.
Because you created the world and everything in it, the sky belongs to you, and the earth also belongs to you.

You created the full extent of the world around us. You made everything to the north and to the south. You made everything to the west, where Mount Tabor is, and you made everything to the east, where Mount Hermon is. People throughout the world joyfully praise you because of who you are.
You are very powerful; yes, you are very strong, and you use your power to do great things.
As you rule, you always do what is right and just, and you are always faithful and true in everything you do.
Yahweh, the people who worship you with joyful shouts have truly good lives; they enjoy your favor as they live.
They rejoice continually because of who you are, and they celebrate how you always do what is right.
You make your people strong and glorious, and because you were pleased with us, you gave us a good king.
The one who protects us belongs to you, Yahweh; yes, our king belongs to you, the holy God whom we Israelites worship.
Long ago you spoke in a vision to the Israelites who were loyal to you. You said, “I have given strength to a mighty warrior; I have chosen a young man from among the people {to be the king}.
I have found David, who loyally obeys me, and I have had people anoint him with my holy oil {to appoint him as king}.
I will always support him with my power; indeed, I will make him strong.
He will never have to pay tribute to a foreign ruler, and no wicked enemy will defeat him.
I will defeat his opponents when they fight against him; yes, I will destroy his enemies.
I will always be faithful to him and treat him kindly, and I will make him a great ruler by my own authority.
I will make his realm extend from the Great Sea to the Euphrates River.
He will call out to me, ‘You are my Father; you are my God, the one who protects me and saves me!’
For my part, I will treat him as if he were my firstborn son, and I will make him the greatest of all the kings on the earth.
I will always love him faithfully, and I will always honor my covenant with him.
I will make sure that his descendants always rule as kings, so that his dynasty lasts as long as the sky exists.
However, if his descendants disobey my instructions and do not live according to what I have decreed,
if they treat my decrees as something they can ignore, and if they do not obey my commands,
then I will punish them to correct them because of the wrong things they have done as if I were hitting them with a rod.
But I will not stop faithfully loving David; I will not fail to do what I promised {for his descendants}.
I will not break my covenant; no, I will not take back what I said.
I guaranteed my promise to David by my own holy character. I said that I was not lying to him, and I meant it.
