I promised solemnly that his descendants would rule as kings forever. Yes, I said that I would preserve his dynasty just as I have made the sun to shine in the sky always.
The moon appears in the sky dependably each month, and in the same way, David’s dynasty will always endure.” Selah
Yet now it appears that you have completely rejected David’s descendant who was our king. It appears that you have abandoned him.
It seems as though you are disregarding the covenant you made with David. You have allowed his dynasty to end, as if you had not promised to preserve it.
You have allowed enemies to break down all the walls that protected his city {of Jerusalem}. It had strong defenses, but you have allowed those enemies to reduce them to ruins.
Now people can come along and steal the things that remain in the city. People in the surrounding countries are ridiculing us Israelites.
You have allowed our enemies to become strong, and they are celebrating how they have defeated us.
Our armies have had to retreat from battles because you have not helped us when we fight.
Our kingdom is no longer glorious, and we no longer have a king.
We are no longer strong, as young men are. This has disgraced us completely. Selah
Yahweh, please help us, and do not delay! Do not keep neglecting us! Do not keep being so angry with us!
Please remember how short human lives are! Please remember that you created us human beings as mere mortals!
No one can live forever and never die; everyone must go to the place where dead people are. Selah
Lord, you promised David that you would faithfully love us Israelites, and you did. You always keep your promises{, so please help us}!
Lord, consider the insulting things that many people are saying about us who loyally obey you! I deeply feel the pain of all those insults.
Yahweh, do something to stop your enemies from mocking the actions of the king you appointed.
May people always bless Yahweh! Amen! Yes, amen!
Lord, you have been like a home for us throughout our generations.
Before you created the mountains, before you formed the earth and everything that is in it, you were eternally God, and you will be God forever.
{When people die,} you cause their corpses to become soil again; you change their corpses to become dirt like that from which {the first} man was created.
When you consider time, a thousand years are {as short as} one day that passes; you consider that they are {as short as} a few hours in the night.
You cause people to die suddenly; they live {only a short time} as a dream lasts {only a short time}. They are like grass in the morning that comes and goes.
In the morning the grass sprouts and develops, then in the evening it dries up and completely withers.
Similarly, {because of the sins that we commit,} you become angry with us; you terrify us and then you destroy us.
It is as though you place our sins in front of you; spreading out even our secret sins where you can see them.
Because you are angry with us, you cause our lives to end; the years that we live pass as quickly as a sigh passes.
People live for {only} seventy years; if they are strong, {some of them live} for eighty years. But throughout our time we have much pain and troubles; our lives soon end, and we die.

No one has fully experienced the powerful things that you can do to people when you are angry with them, No, people are not adequately afraid of how you can punish them because you are angry with them.
So teach us to realize that we live for only a short time in order that we may think wisely {about how we use our time}.
Yahweh, how long will you be angry with us? Pity us who serve you.

Each morning, show us that it is enough for us if you love us faithfully as you have promised that you would do. {Show us this} so that we may shout joyfully and be happy all during the years that we live.
Cause us now to be happy for as many years as you afflicted us and we experienced bad things.
Enable us who serve you to see the {great} things that you do, and enable our descendants to see your glorious power {also}.
Lord, our God, give us your blessings and enable us to be successful; yes, cause us to be successful in everything that we do!
Those people whom God Most High protects will be able to rest safely because Shaddai cares for them.
I will declare to Yahweh, “You protect me; you are like a stronghold in which I am safe. You are my God, the one in whom I trust.”
He will rescue you from all hidden traps and save you from deadly diseases.

He will protect you as a bird does who covers her young under her wings. You will be safe in his care. As he faithfully does what he has promised, that is like a shield or strong wall that will protect you.
You will not be afraid of things that happen during the night that could terrorize you or of arrows {that your enemies will shoot at you} during the day.
You will not be afraid of plagues that infect people in the night or of other evil forces that kill people in the light of day.
Even if a thousand people fall dead alongside you, even if ten thousand people are dying around you, the deadly thing will not harm you.
All you need to do is watch and you will see that God is punishing evil people!
This is because you trust Yahweh, God Most High, who protects me, to also protect you.
Therefore, nothing evil will happen to you; no plague will affect your family
because Yahweh will command his angels to protect you in whatever you are doing.
They will even hold you up with their hands so that you will not hurt your foot on a big stone.
Yahweh will not allow your enemies to harm you; even if strong lions and poisonous snakes attack you, you will defeat them!
Yahweh says, “I will rescue those who love me; I will protect them because they know me.
When they call out to me, I will answer them. I will help them when they are experiencing trouble; I will rescue them and honor them.
I will reward them by enabling them to live a long time, and I will save them.”
Yahweh, it is good for people to thank you and to sing as they praise you, the Most High God.
It is good to proclaim every morning that you faithfully love us and to declare each night that everything that you say is true,
{singing} {to the music} of {instruments that have} ten {strings} and of lyres {and} with {musicians playing} melodies on a harp.
I do this, Yahweh, because what you have done makes me happy; I sing joyfully because of the things that you do.
Yahweh, the things that you do are great! We cannot understand all that you think.
These are things that foolish people do not know about, things that dolts cannot understand:
{They do not understand that} when the number of wicked people increases as blades of grass increase, and {when it seems that} all those who do what is evil prosper, Yahweh will destroy them forever.
But Yahweh, you will rule forever.
Just look at your enemies, Yahweh! Your enemies will certainly die. You will destroy everyone who does wicked things.
But you have caused me to be as strong as a wild ox; you have caused me to be very joyful.
I have observed my enemies as they oppose me, and I have heard those evil men.
But righteous {people} will prosper like {flourishing} palm trees, they will grow like the {tall} cedar trees in Lebanon.
They belong to Yahweh as securely as if they were trees with roots deep in his temple grounds. They are as prosperous and healthy as if they were trees growing in our God’s courtyard.
They are like trees that continue to bear fruit even when they are old. They remain strong and full of energy, like trees that are full of sap and have abundant leaves.
That shows that Yahweh is just; he is like a huge rock behind which I am safe, and he never does anything that is unjust.
Yahweh, you are the King! It is as though you are wearing royal robes that are majestic and powerful. You are the one who put the world firmly in place, and no one can move it {out of its place}.
You have been king since long ago; you have always existed.
Yahweh, the oceans rise up; their waves {loudly} pound {against the shore}; {it is as though} they roar with a powerful voice.
But you are more powerful than the roar of those oceans; you are more powerful than the huge ocean waves! You are Yahweh, the one who is great and powerful!
Yahweh, your laws are completely reliable; your temple is a beautifully holy place. {That will be true} forever.
Yahweh, you are a God who punishes {your enemies}. So reveal {to them} who you are!
You are the one who judges all people on the earth; so take action and give the arrogant people what they deserve.
Yahweh, wicked people just continue to be glad, and that is not right!
They abundantly speak arrogant things; all people who do evil things say that they are great people.
Yahweh, it is as though those wicked people were crushing us, your people; they distress the people who belong to you alone.
They murder widows, people from other countries, and also young people who have no fathers.
Those wicked people think to themselves, “Yahweh does not see {any of this}; the God whom the Israelites worship does not notice {the evil things that we do}.”
You wicked people in Israel need to understand {what is right}; you have been stupid and foolish far too long!
Since Yahweh is the one who made ears, of course he can hear {what you say}! Not only that, he created eyes; so of course he can see {the evil things that you do}!
He corrects {the leaders of} other nations, so he will punish {you}, as well. He has taught people everything that they know, so of course he knows everything {that you do}.
Yahweh knows everything that people are thinking; he knows that what they think is evil and useless.
Yahweh, how fortunate are those who allow you to discipline them, {how fortunate are} those whom you teach from your laws!
You relieve those people from bad things when they happen, and someday you will punish the wicked people and stop them from doing wicked things.
This will happen because Yahweh will not reject his people; he will not desert those who belong to him.
Yes, someday judges will again decide matters fairly for people, and all honest people will be pleased about that.
{But when evil people oppressed me,} I could find no one to defend me against the wicked things that evil people did to me.
If Yahweh had not helped me {at that time}, I would have gone quickly to the place where dead people say nothing.
Just when I thought, “I am about to die,” then, Yahweh, you saved me by being faithful and loving to me.
Whenever I am very worried, you comfort me and cause me to be happy.
Corrupt rulers, those who establish laws that allow people to do what is not right, cannot be your friends.
They plot together how to destroy righteous people, and they declare that innocent people must die.
But Yahweh has become like a fortress for me; my God is like a huge rock that protects me.
He will do to those wicked leaders the terrible things that they have done to others; he will get rid of them because they do wicked things. Yes, Yahweh our God will get rid of them.
{Everyone,} come and let us sing to Yahweh; let us shout joyfully to the one who protects us and saves us!
Let us thank him as we come before him and sing joyful psalms as we praise him.
Because Yahweh is a great God. He is a great king who rules over all other spirit beings.
He controls the whole earth. From the deepest places to the highest mountains, it belongs to him.
The seas are his because he is the one who made them. He also made the dry land.
{Everyone,} come, let us worship him and bow down {before him}. Let us kneel before Yahweh, who is the one who made us.
{Do this} because he is our God, and we are the people whom he protects, like sheep that a shepherd takes care of. I desire that today you may hear what Yahweh is saying to you.
He says, “Do not become stubborn as your ancestors did at Meribah, and as they did long ago at Massah in the wilderness.

There your ancestors tested whether I would continue to be patient with them. They wanted to see if they could do evil things and not have me punish them. They did this even though they had seen me perform many miracles.
For 40 years I was angry with those people. I said about them, ‘Those people are unreliable. They completely refuse to obey my commands.’
So because I was very angry, I solemnly said about them, ‘They will never enter {the land of Canaan} where I would have allowed them to rest!’”
Sing to Yahweh a new song! All you people throughout the earth, sing to Yahweh!
Sing to Yahweh and praise him! Every day proclaim to others that he has saved us.
Tell about how glorious he is to all people groups; tell all peoples everywhere the marvelous things that he has done.
Do this because Yahweh is great, and he deserves very much for people to praise him; people should revere him more than all other gods.
This is true because all of the gods that the other peoples worship are only idols, but it is Yahweh who made the heavens!
Yahweh is magnificent and majestic. His holy house shows how strong and beautiful he is.
You peoples in nations all over the earth, Proclaim that Yahweh is the one who is truly glorious and strong!
Praise Yahweh as he deserves for us to praise him; bring an offering and come to his temple.
Bow down before Yahweh because he is marvelously holy. Everyone on earth should tremble because of who he is.
Say to {all} the people groups, “Yahweh is the king!” He put the world in its place, and nothing will ever be able to move it. He judges {all} the peoples fairly.
All the beings that are in the heavens should be glad, and all the people on the earth should rejoice. The oceans and all the creatures that are in the oceans should roar {to praise Yahweh}.
Let it be as though the fields and everything that is in them are rejoicing. Then let it be as though all the trees in the forests are singing joyfully
in front of Yahweh. They should do this because he is coming to judge everyone on the earth, and this is certain. He will judge all the people fairly according to what he knows is true.
Yahweh is the king! I want everyone on the earth to be glad and I want all the people who live on the land in and around the oceans to {also} rejoice {about that}!
There are very dark clouds all around him; he always rules righteously and justly.
He sends fire out in front of him, and {that fire} burns all of his enemies.
All around the world he sends his bright lightning; people on the earth see {it}, and it causes them {to be afraid and} to tremble.
The mountains melt like wax before Yahweh; he is the Lord who rules over all of the earth.
Everything that people can see in the heavens makes it clear that he is righteous, and all the people groups see how glorious he is.
Everyone who worships carved images should be ashamed; all those who are proud of their useless false gods should be ashamed. All those gods should bow down to worship Yahweh!
The people of Jerusalem heard {Yahweh’s just decrees} and they were happy {about them}; people in the other cities in Judah also {heard and} rejoiced because you judge {people} justly, Yahweh.
Of course, Yahweh, you are the supreme king who rules over all the earth; You are far more powerful than any other spirit beings.
All you who love Yahweh, you must hate every evil thing {that people do}! Yahweh protects those who are faithful to him; he rescues them when wicked people try to harm them.
He makes good things happen for righteous people and he causes those who are honest to rejoice.
You righteous people, let Yahweh make you glad, and thank him, the one we all know to be holy!
A psalm. Sing to Yahweh a new song because he has done wonderful things! By being powerfully holy he has saved {his people}.
Yahweh has shown openly that he saves {his people}; he has revealed to people all over the world that he always does what is right.
He is always loyal to his covenant to be faithful to the Israelite people. Even the people who live in the most remote places of the earth will see that our God saves {his people}.
All you people everywhere should shout joyfully to Yahweh; praise him while you sing joyfully and make music!
Play to Yahweh on a harp, and sing along as you play.
{Some of you should} blow trumpets and ram’s horns {while others} shout joyfully to Yahweh, our king!
The oceans and all {the creatures} that are in the oceans should roar {to praise Yahweh}. The earth itself and everyone on it should do the same!
It should seem as though the rivers were clapping their hands {to praise Yahweh} and that the hills were singing together joyfully
before Yahweh because he will come to judge everyone on the earth! He will judge all the people in the world justly and fairly.
Yahweh is the supreme king, so all people should tremble {in front of him}! He sits on his throne {in the temple} above the {statues of} the cherubim, so the earth should quake!
Yahweh is a mighty king in Jerusalem; he is also the supreme ruler of all peoples.
They should praise you, Yahweh, because you are great and awesome! {They should say,} “He is holy!”
Yahweh is a mighty king {because} he loves what is just. You, Yahweh, have established what is fair. You have acted justly and righteously for the people of Israel.
Praise Yahweh, the God whom we worship! Bow down to him at {the temple, which is} his footstool. He is holy!
Moses and Aaron were two of his priests; Samuel also was someone who prayed to him. Those {three} cried out to Yahweh {to help them}, and he helped them.
He spoke to Moses and Aaron from the cloud that was {like} a {huge} pillar. They obeyed {all} the laws and commandments that he gave to them.

Yahweh, our God, you helped Moses, Aaron, and Samuel {when they cried out to you to help them}; you are the God who forgave them {for the sins that they had committed}, even though you punished them for the things that they did that were wrong.
Praise Yahweh, our God, and worship him {at the temple} on his holy hill; {it is right to do that} because Yahweh, our God, is holy!
A psalm of thanksgiving. Everyone in the world should shout joyfully to Yahweh!
We should worship Yahweh gladly! We should come before him singing joyfully.
We should acknowledge that Yahweh is God. It is he who made us; we did not make ourselves. We are the people who belong to him; we are like sheep that he cares for as a shepherd does.
Enter the gates {of his temple} thanking him; enter the courtyard {of his temple} singing songs to praise him! Thank him and praise him
because Yahweh always does good things for us. He will faithfully love us forever, and he will always fulfill everything that he has promised.
David wrote this psalm. Yahweh, I will praise you with singing! I will sing that you are just and that you faithfully love us.
I will examine how to live in the right way. Yahweh, I need you to come and help me! In everything that I do in my household, I will sincerely try to do what is right.
I will not tempt myself to do any bad thing. I hate any kind of sinful action; I will not allow myself to think about doing those things.
I will not be dishonest, and I will not do anything evil.
I will get rid of anyone who secretly slanders someone else. I will not tolerate anyone who is proud or arrogant.
I look for people in this land who are loyal to God to help me rule {this nation}. Only people who behave honestly may work for me.
I will not allow anyone who deceives others {to work} in my palace, and I will not allow anyone who tells lies to continue working for me.
I will start every day by working to get rid of all of the wicked people in this land. I will expel everyone who does what is evil from this city that belongs to Yahweh.
Yahweh, please listen to me when I pray to you; yes, please be attentive as I cry out to you!
When distressing things happen to me, please do not ignore me! Listen to me, and answer me quickly as soon as I call out to you!
Please hurry because my life is ending as quickly as smoke that disappears; my body feels like a fire is burning it.
I feel as though I am withering away like grass that the sun has scorched. You see, I do not even remember to eat any food.
I groan aloud so much that my bones protrude under my skin.
I am {lonely and despised} like an owl in the desert; I have become like a screech owl in the ruins {of a town}.
I lie awake {at night}; I am like a lonely bird sitting on a housetop.
During the whole of each day my enemies insult me. Those who make fun of me use my name when they curse people, saying, “May you be like him.”
It feels as though you have picked me up and thrown me away! Because you are so very angry with me, my food tastes like ashes and my tears fall into my drink.
My time to remain alive is {coming to an end} like an evening shadow {that will soon be gone}. I have withered as grass withers {in the hot sun}.
But Yahweh, you will rule forever on your royal throne; people of all times will talk about you.
You yourself will now act and be merciful to the people of Jerusalem; you will do this because it is now the time that you have set for you to be kind to them.
It is true that we who serve you love everything about Jerusalem.
Yahweh, someday the people of all nations will revere you, and all the kings on the earth will recognize how very glorious you are.
You see, it is Yahweh who builds Jerusalem; he will appear {there} gloriously.
Yahweh listens to the prayers of {his} people who are homeless. He does not ignore them when they pray for him to help them.
I will write these things down so that people in future years will know {what he has done}, {in order that} people who are not born yet will praise Yahweh.
{They will describe} how Yahweh looked down from his holy place in heaven and saw {what was happening on} the earth.
Yahweh looked down in order to help the groaning prisoners. He looked down in order to set free the people whom their enemies were about to kill.
As a result, people in Jerusalem will tell what Yahweh has done and praise him for it.
This will happen when many peoples, including those from other kingdoms, gather to worship Yahweh together.
{But now} he has caused me to become weak while I am still young; {I think that} I will not remain alive very long.
I say {to you}, “My God, do not let me die when I am only half-way through my lifetime! In contrast, you live forever!
You created the world long ago, and you are the one who made the heavens.

As for the earth and the heavens, they will disappear, but as for you, you will remain. All of it will wear out as clothes wear out. You will get rid of them as people get rid of old clothes, and they will no longer exist.
But you are Yahweh; you will always be.
The children of those who worship you will live safely {in Jerusalem}, and you will protect their descendants as they live in your presence.”
A psalm of David I tell myself, “Praise Yahweh!” To everything that is within me, I say, “Praise him because he is holy!”
I tell myself, “Praise Yahweh, and think about all of the kind things that he has done for me.”
He forgives all of my sins, and he heals me from all of my sicknesses.
He rescues me from things that would kill me; he blesses me by faithfully loving me and acting mercifully to me.
He gives me plenty of good things {during my entire life}. He makes me feel young {and strong} {as though I could fly high} like an eagle.
It is Yahweh who does all this! He does what is right and judges justly for all those whom people have been treating unfairly.
{Long ago} he revealed to Moses the way that he works; he showed to {our ancestors,} the people of Israel, the {mighty} things that he can do.
Yahweh acts mercifully and kindly; he does not quickly get angry {when we sin}; he always faithfully loves us.
He will not always rebuke us, and he will not remain angry forever.
He does not punish us for our sins nearly as much as we deserve.
Indeed, as high as the sky is above the earth, that is how much Yahweh faithfully loves everyone who reveres him.
He has taken away the guilt for our sins and put it as far from us as the east is from the west.
Just as parents always love their children, Yahweh always loves those who revere him.
Indeed, he certainly knows how weak we are; he remembers that he created us from dust.
The lifetime of humans passes quickly, like that of grass. We are like wild flowers that bloom for a short while,
but then the wind blows over them and they disappear, and no one knows they were ever there.
But Yahweh will continue to faithfully love all those who revere him, forever. He will do what is right for generations of their children,
that is, he will act that way to all those who obey the covenant that he made with them. Yes, he will act that way to all those who obey what he has commanded us to do.
Yahweh rules as king in heaven. From there, he rules over everything.
Praise Yahweh, you angels who belong to Yahweh, You powerful warriors who do what he tells you to do, you who obey what he commands!
Praise Yahweh, all you armies of his angels, you who serve him and do what he desires!
All of the creatures that Yahweh has created should praise him! They should praise him in every place where he rules, {which is everywhere}! I say to myself, “Praise Yahweh!”
I tell myself, “Bless Yahweh!” Yahweh, my God, you are magnificent! You are more majestic than a king appearing in his beautiful robes!
You use light {itself} as your robe; you spread out {all of} heaven as your tent.
The rain clouds are like the upper rooms of your palace. The clouds are like chariots for you; the wind is like a bird that takes you wherever you want to go.
You send the winds like your messengers, {and you control} fire as your servant.
You created the world to be secure, so that nothing can ever move it from its place.
Later, you covered the earth with a flood, like covering someone with clothing; water even covered the mountains.
Then you commanded the water, and it receded; yes, you spoke loudly, and the water rushed away.
Part of the water ascended {to its place} above the mountains, and part of it descended the valleys {to its place in the earth}. All of it went {back} to the place that you had determined for it.
Then you set a boundary for the water that it cannot cross over. That boundary ensures that the water will never again cover the whole earth.
You make the springs that pour water into the stream beds; their water flows between the mountains.
Those streams provide water for all of his wild animals to drink. The wild donkeys {drink the water and} are no longer thirsty.
Birds make their nests beside the streams. They sing among the branches {of the trees}.
From the heavens you send rain down on the mountains. As a result of doing this, you satisfy all of the creatures on earth {with many good things}.
You make grass to grow for the cattle {to eat}, and you make plants to grow for people to cultivate, so that they can make bread from {those plants that grew in} the soil.
You give us {grapes that produce} wine that makes us cheerful; you give us {olives that produce} oil to make our faces shine, and you give us {grain to make} bread that makes us strong.
Yahweh, you send plenty of rain to water your cedar trees that you planted in Lebanon.
Birds make their nests in those trees, and storks make their nests in the cypress trees.
High up in the mountains is where the wild goats live, and hyraxes live in the rocky cliffs.
Yahweh, you made the moon to indicate the times for our festivals, and you made the sun to always go down at the right time.
You bring darkness, and it becomes night when all of your forest animals prowl around.
The young lions roar then as they seek their prey, looking for the food that you have provided for them.
At dawn, they go back to their dens and lie down.
{That is when} people go to their work; and they do their work until it is evening.
Yahweh, you have made so many different kinds of things! You were very wise as you made them all. The earth is full of the creatures that you made.
We see the ocean, which is vastly wide between its shores! It is full of many kinds of wriggling creatures, so many that no one can count them. There are creatures ranging from small to big.
Ships sail on the sea. Leviathan is also there, the creature that you made to splash around in it.
All of these creatures depend on you to give them the food that they need at the right time.
When you give them the food that they need, then they gather it. You give it to them freely. They eat until they are full of your good things.
But when you refuse to give food to them, they panic. When you cause them to stop breathing, they die; their bodies decay and become part of the soil.
When you cause {newborn} creatures to begin to breathe, they begin to live. You give new life to {all the living creatures on} the earth.
I want all of Yahweh’s creatures to glorify him forever! I want Yahweh to rejoice about everything that he has created!
He makes the earth shake just by looking at it! When he {merely} touches the mountains they start to burn!
I will sing to Yahweh as long as I live. I will praise my God until the day that I die.
May Yahweh be pleased by all {these things} that I have thought about him. As for me, I will rejoice because I know him.
However, I want sinners to disappear from the earth, and for there to be no more wicked people! I tell myself, “Bless Yahweh!” Praise Yahweh!
Give thanks to Yahweh; worship him and pray to him. Tell everyone in the world what he has done!
Sing to him; praise him with instruments; tell others about all of his wonderful miracles!
Be proud of Yahweh, who is the holy one. You people who worship Yahweh, rejoice!
Ask Yahweh to help you and to make you strong; always try to be with him!

You people who are descendants of Yahweh’s servant Abraham, you descendants of Jacob, the people whom Yahweh has chosen, think about all of the wonderful things that he has done; he performed miracles, and he proclaimed {righteous} judgments.
He is Yahweh, the God whom we worship. He rules over people throughout the earth.
He never forgets the covenant that he made; that is, he will maintain what he promised for countless generations.
That is the covenant that he made with Abraham, and that he repeated with an oath to Isaac.
Then he repeated it as a reliable covenant with Jacob, that is, with Israel, and it was a covenant that would last forever.
What Yahweh said to them was, “I will give to you the region of Canaan; that will be what you {and your descendants} inherit from me.”
Yahweh said that to the people of Israel when there were only a few of them. They were just a tiny group of people who were living in that land like strangers.
They continually wandered from one place to another, living in various kingdoms and people groups.
But Yahweh did not allow others to oppress the people of Israel. On their behalf, he warned kings {by saying to them},
“Do not harm the people whom I have chosen! Do nothing bad to my prophets!”
Yahweh created a famine in the land of Canaan, that is, all of the people there had no food to eat.
{So the people of Israel went to Egypt, but} before they went, Yahweh had already sent someone {there}. {He sent} Joseph, whom his brothers had sold to be a slave.
{Later, while Joseph was in prison in Egypt,} the guards trapped his feet in shackles, and they put an iron collar around his neck.
{Joseph was in prison} until the time when the events that he had predicted happened. Yahweh spoke to him {during this time} and taught Joseph to trust him more.
The king of Egypt, the ruler of the people, commanded his servants who went to the prison and set Joseph free.
Then the king chose Joseph as the one to decide about everything in the king’s household, that is, to be in charge of everything that the king possessed.
The king permitted Joseph to command the king’s officials to do anything that Joseph wanted them to do, and Joseph taught the king’s advisors how to be wise.
{Later, Joseph’s father} Jacob, also called Israel, arrived in Egypt. He lived like a foreigner in that land that belonged to the descendants of Ham.
Over the years, Yahweh caused the descendants of Jacob to become very numerous. As a result, the enemies of the people of Israel considered that the people of Israel were becoming too strong.
So Yahweh caused the rulers of Egypt to hate Yahweh’s people, and they devised ways to oppress his people.
But then Yahweh sent his servant Moses along with {Moses’ older brother} Aaron, whom Yahweh had also chosen {to serve him}.

Yahweh sent darkness so that the land of Egypt was dark, and Moses and Aaron obeyed what Yahweh told them to do.
Yahweh caused all of the water in Egypt to become blood, which caused all of their fish to die.
Then he caused the land to become full of frogs; the royal family even had frogs in their bedrooms!
Then Yahweh commanded {that flies come}, and {swarms of} flies descended {on the people of Egypt}. Gnats also swarmed across the whole country.
Yahweh sent them hail instead of rain, and he started fires that burned throughout their land.
The hail ruined their grapevines, fig trees, and destroyed all the other trees in their country.
Yahweh commanded locusts to come, and hordes of them came of different kinds; so many came that no one could count them.
The locusts ate every green plant in their land, including all of the crops.
Then Yahweh killed every firstborn son, the one who first demonstrated that the man was virile, {in every house} of the people of Egypt.

Then Yahweh brought the Israelite people out {from Egypt}. They were carrying {many heavy things made of} silver and gold {that the people of Egypt had given to them}, and yet none of his people stumbled as they went.
The people of Egypt were glad when the Israelite people left because the people of Egypt had become very afraid of the Israelites.
{Then} Yahweh spread a cloud to cover the Israelites; and at night {it became} a {big} fire {in the sky} to give them light.
{Then} the Israelites asked {for meat to eat}, and Yahweh sent {flocks of} quail to them, and he gave them plenty of {manna} bread from the sky {each morning}.
{One day} Yahweh split open a rock, and water poured out {from the opening for the people to drink}. The water became a river flowing in the desert.
Yahweh did those things because he continually thought about the sacred promise that he had given to his servant, Abraham.
So his people were joyful as Yahweh brought them out {from Egypt}. These people whom he had chosen were shouting joyfully as they went.
Then Yahweh gave to the people of Israel the land that had belonged to the people groups {that lived there in Canaan}. So the Israelites took over the fields that those peoples had planted.
Yahweh did all these things so that his people would do all the things that he had commanded them to do. Praise Yahweh!
Praise Yahweh! Thank Yahweh because he is good and because he faithfully loves us forever!
Because Yahweh has done so many great things, no one can tell all the great things that Yahweh has done, and no one can praise him enough.
How happy are those who act fairly, always doing what is right!
Yahweh, be kind to me when you help your people! Include me when you rescue them!

Allow me to see the people whom you have chosen become prosperous again. Allow me to be happy with the people of your nation when they become happy again. Allow me to praise you along with all those others who belong to you.
We have sinned just as our ancestors did; we have done all kinds of evil.

Our ancestors did not appreciate the wonderful things that you did when they were in Egypt. They forgot about the many times that you showed that you faithfully loved them. Instead, when they were at the Sea of Reeds, they rebelled against you.
Even so, he rescued them because of who he is, so that he could show that he is very powerful.
He rebuked the Sea of Reeds and it became dry. Then he led our ancestors through it and even the deepest parts were as dry as a desert.
In that way he rescued them from their hateful enemies.
Then their enemies drowned under the water {of the Sea of Reeds}; not one of them remained {alive}.
When that happened, our ancestors believed that Yahweh had truly done for them what he had promised to do, and they sang to praise him.
But they soon forgot what he had done for them; they did things without waiting to find out what Yahweh wanted them to do.
They intensely wanted certain foods in the wilderness. They did evil things there that challenged God to punish them.
So he gave them what they requested, but then he made many of them sick so that they died.
Later when some of the men in the camp became resentful of Moses and of {his older brother} Aaron, who was dedicated to serve Yahweh {by being a priest},
the ground opened up and Dathan fell into it and it also buried Abiram and his people.
God made a fire start among their people that burned up all the wicked people {who agreed with them}.
Then the Israelite leaders made a metal statue of a calf at Mount Horeb and they worshiped it.
So instead of worshiping their glorious God, they worshiped a statue of a bull that eats grass!
They ignored God, who had rescued them by the great miracles that he performed in Egypt.
They stopped thinking about the wonderful things that he did for them in Egypt and the amazing things that he did for them at the Sea of Reeds.
Because of that, God said that he would get rid of the Israelites; but Moses, whom God had chosen {to serve him}, confronted God to persuade him not to destroy {them}.

Then our ancestors refused to enter the beautiful land {of Canaan} because they did not believe that God would fulfill his promise {that he would enable them to take the land from the people who were living there}.
Instead, they stayed in their tents and complained. They did not obey what Yahweh said that they should do.
So Yahweh solemnly swore to them that he would cause them to die there in the wilderness,
and that he would spread their descendants among the people of other nations, yes, that he would disperse them in those {foreign} lands.
Later the Israelite people began worshiping the statue of Baal at Mount Peor, and they ate meat that had been sacrificed to dead {ancestors}.
When the people did these things, that made Yahweh angry, so {again} he caused many of them to get a terrible disease.
But Phinehas stood up and punished {the ones who had sinned}, and as a result the plague ended.
Because of what Phinehas did, people have considered him to be a righteous man, and people in all future years will continue to remember him as righteous.
Then at Meribah, where the water came out {of the rock}, our ancestors caused Yahweh to become angry {again}, and Moses suffered because of what they did.
Moses suffered because they caused him to become very angry, and he said things that were foolish.
Our ancestors did not destroy the other people groups as Yahweh had told them to do.
Instead, the men married women from those people groups, and they started doing the {evil} things that those people did.
Our ancestors worshiped the idols of those people, and that is how they began to reject Yahweh and his ways.
{Many of} the Israelites sacrificed their sons and daughters to the demons {that those idols represented}.
They killed their own sons and daughters, who had done nothing wrong, by offering them as sacrifices to the idols of the Canaanites. Because of those murders, the land of Canaan became defiled.
Because of what they did they made it impossible for Yahweh to accept them. By worshiping idols instead of faithfully worshiping only Yahweh, they became like prostitutes.
So Yahweh became very angry with his people; he was completely disgusted with them.
As a result, he allowed other people groups to conquer our ancestors, so that those who hated our ancestors were their rulers.
Their enemies oppressed our ancestors and completely controlled them.
Many times Yahweh saved his people, but they insisted on rebelling against him, and they destroyed themselves by being more and more sinful.
However, Yahweh saw everything that was distressing to them, and he listened to them when they cried out to him for help.
He thought about the covenant that he had made with them, and because he was completely committed to faithfully loving them, he decided that he would stop {punishing them}.
He caused all those who had captured the Israelites to feel sorry for them.
Yahweh our God, rescue us and bring us back to Israel from among those other people groups so that we may thank you who are holy and joyfully praise you!
Praise Yahweh, the God whom we Israelites worship! Praise him now and forever! Let all the people say, “We agree! Praise Yahweh!”
Thank Yahweh because he is good and because he faithfully loves us forever!
Those whom Yahweh has saved should tell others that he has rescued them from their enemies.
He has gathered them together from {many foreign} lands; he has gathered them from the east and the west, from the north and from the {southern} sea.
Some of those who returned from those countries wandered in the trackless desert; they could find no town to live in.
They were hungry and thirsty, and they became weak and discouraged.
Then because they were distressed, they called out to Yahweh, and he rescued them from what was distressing them.
He led them along a straight road where they walked {safely} to cities where they could live.
They should praise Yahweh for how he has loved them faithfully and for the wonderful things that he does for all people!
They should thank him because he satisfies people who are thirsty, and he gives hungry people plenty of good food to eat.
Some of them sat in deep darkness; they were prisoners, suffering in iron {chains fastened to their hands and feet}.
They were suffering in prison because they had rebelled against God; they actually rejected the instructions that the Most High God gave to them.
God made them experience difficult things so that they would no longer be proud. When bad things happened to them, there was no one who would help them.
Then because they were so distressed, they called out to Yahweh, and he rescued them from what was distressing them.
He broke the chains that were on their hands and feet and brought them out of those very dark prisons.

Yahweh broke down the bronze gates and he cut through the iron bars of their prison. Therefore they should praise Yahweh for how he has loved them faithfully and for the wonderful things that he does for all people!
Some of them foolishly rebelled {against God}, and they suffered because of their sins.
They did not want to eat any food, and they almost died.
Then because they were so distressed, they called out to Yahweh, and he rescued them from what was distressing them.
Then Yahweh healed them by speaking a message of healing; in this way he saved them from dying.
They should praise Yahweh for how he has loved them faithfully and for the wonderful things that he does for all people!
They should give offerings to him to show that they are thankful, and they should tell about the miracles that he has performed by singing joyfully!
Some of them sailed in ships; they bought and sold things far away across the sea.
These people saw the creatures that Yahweh created; they saw the amazing things that he had made {as they traveled} across the very deep seas.
Then he commanded the winds to become strong. They became a storm and stirred up very high waves.
The ships in which they were sailing went up on the high waves, then they went down into the troughs between the waves. This dangerous action terrified the sailors.
They stumbled about and staggered as drunken men do, and everything that they tried to do was useless.
Then because they were distressed, they called out to Yahweh, and he rescued them from what was distressing them.
He calmed the storm and he stilled the waves.
Then they were very glad that the storm had become calm and Yahweh brought them {safely} into the harbor where they had wanted to go.
They should praise Yahweh for how he has loved them faithfully and for the wonderful things that he does for all people!
They should praise him among the Israelite people when they have gathered together, and they should praise him in front of the leaders of the community.
Yahweh causes rivers to become dry so that the land becomes barren, and he makes springs of water to become dusty ground.
Yahweh causes land that normally produces a lot of crops to become salty wastelands. He does that because the people who live there are very wicked.
But Yahweh also creates pools of water in deserts, that is, he causes springs to flow where the ground had been dry.
Then he brings people who are hungry into that land, to live there and to build cities there.
Then they sow {some of} the fields with seeds and {in other fields} they plant grapevines and it all produces {a large amount of} crops.
He blesses those people so that they have very many children, and so that their herds of cattle become very large.
Then the people become fewer because the leaders oppress them and cause them to become distressed and to suffer.
Then Yahweh shows that he despises the leaders {who oppress them}, and makes those leaders wander in a wilderness where there are no roads.
But he rescues poor people from those who oppress them and causes {their} families to increase in number as flocks of sheep do.
People who live rightly see {Yahweh do these things}, and they rejoice; wicked people {know about these things, too,} {but they} have nothing to say in reply.
Those who are wise should think carefully about these things; they should thoughtfully consider all the things that Yahweh has done to show that he faithfully loves them.
God, I am completely committed to {worshiping} you. I will sing and I will play music {to praise you}. I will do this with my whole being!
I will arise before the sun rises, and I will praise you while I play my lyre and my harp.
Yahweh, I will thank you as foreign people listen; yes, I will play music to praise you before other people groups.

I will do that because the way that you faithfully love us is so great that it is like the distance between the heavens and the earth, and the way that you faithfully keep your promises is so great that it is like the distance between the earth and the clouds.
God, show {all creatures} that you are greater than anything in the heavens! Show how wonderful you are {to people} all over the earth!
Please answer our prayers and rescue us from our enemies by your power so that we, the people whom you love, may be safe.
Because God is holy, he answered, “I will joyfully divide the area of Shechem {for you} and I will distribute {among my people} the land in the Valley of Succoth.
{The region of} Gilead is mine; {the area of the tribe of} Manasseh is mine; {the tribe of} Ephraim is {like} my war helmet; and {the tribe of} Judah is {like} my royal scepter.
The people of Moab serve me as those who wash my feet; the people of Edom also belong to me as menial servants; I have defeated the people of Philistia.”
I wait for God to lead us to {fight against the people of} Edom; I wait for God to lead my army to {attack} their {capital} city that has strong walls around it.
God, we hope that you have not abandoned us; {we are distressed that} you have not been going with us when our army marches out {to fight our enemies}.
Please help us when we fight against our enemies because the help that humans can give {to us} is worthless.
{But} with you {helping us}, we will win; you are the one who will {enable us to} defeat our enemies.
A note to the worship leader: David wrote this psalm. God, you are the one whom I praise, so please answer my prayer
because evil and dishonest people slander me and tell lies about me.
On all sides of me they say things that show that they hate me, and they harm me for no reason.
I show them that I love them but instead of being kind to me, they say that I have done evil things. So I pray to God {about it}.
I do good things for them and they respond by doing evil things to me. I love them and they respond by hating me.
So appoint a wicked judge who will judge my enemy, and bring one {of his enemies} who will stand next to him and accuse him {of doing evil things}.
Let that judge declare that my enemy is guilty, and may you judge that even his prayer {to you} is a sin.
Then cause him to die soon; let people honor someone else rather than him.
Cause his children not to have a father anymore, and cause his wife to become a widow.
Cause his children to wander far from their ruined homes, begging and looking for food.
Let the people to whom he owed money seize all of his property; let strangers take away everything that he worked to acquire.
Make sure that no one is faithfully loving to him; make sure that no one pities his fatherless children.
Cause all his children to die, so that there will not be another generation to continue his name.
Yahweh, consider all of the evil things that his ancestors did and do not forgive the sins that his mother committed.
Please think about their sins always, but cause everyone on earth to completely forget who they were.
I pray these things because that man{, my enemy,} was never faithful toward anyone as your covenant says we must be; instead, he persecuted poor, needy, and grieving people until they were dead.
He enjoyed cursing {other people}, so now people are cursing him. He did not want to bless {other people}, so there will be no one who blesses him.

Cursing {other people} is as natural for him as wearing clothes. Cursing {other people} is so much a part of who he is that it is like the water that he drinks; it is so much a part of who he is that it is like olive oil that has soaked into his bones.
Cause those terrible curses to continually afflict him like clothes that cling to him and like the belt that he wears every day.
Yahweh, let this {curse} be the way that you punish all of those who accuse me {of doing bad things} and all of those who say evil things about me.
But you, Yahweh, my God, please be kind to me because of who you are! Rescue me {from my enemies} because you faithfully love me as you promised.
I ask you to do this because I am destitute and I am intensely sorrowful.
I think that my time to remain alive will end as quickly as an evening shadow disappears. I will be gone as quickly as a man shakes off a locust.
My knees are weak because I have fasted very often, and my body has become very thin; any fat is gone.
The people who accuse me despise me; when they see me, they insult me by shaking their heads at me.
Yahweh, the God whom I worship, please help me! Rescue me because you faithfully love me!
Then my enemies will know that you, Yahweh, are the one who has done it!
As for them, they will curse {me}, but you, in contrast, will bless {me}. When they persecute {me}, {the result will be that} you make them ashamed, but you cause {me,} your servant, to be glad!
Please let everyone see that those who accuse me are completely disgraceful! Yes, cause other people to see that they are shameful as easily as someone sees the clothes that they wear!
I will thank Yahweh very much out loud; I will praise him when I am among the crowd of people who are worshiping him.
I will do that because he defends poor people {like me} in order to save {us} from those who would condemn us to die.
David wrote this psalm. Yahweh said to my lord, “Sit {here,} close to me, in the place of highest honor until I completely defeat your enemies and make them {like} a stool for your feet!”
Yahweh will extend your powerful kingdom from Zion {to other lands}; you are to rule over all your enemies.

When you lead your army into battle, your people will offer themselves freely {to join your army}. The way that they are completely devoted to you will be beautiful. You will be as strong as you were as a young man every day, as surely as the dew comes that waters the earth every morning.
Yahweh has made a solemn promise and he will never change his mind {about it}; {he said to the king,} “You are an eternal priest in the way that Melchizedek was a priest.”
The Lord fights for you; when he becomes angry, he defeats many kings.
He will punish the people of many nations; he will cause many {enemy soldiers} to fall dead, with crushed heads, all over a broad land.
But the king will drink from the stream alongside the road; because of {all} this, he will be victorious.
Praise Yahweh! I will thank Yahweh with my entire inner being every time that those who do what is right meet together.
The things that Yahweh does are wonderful! All those who delight in those things study them carefully.
The things that he does show how wonderful and glorious he is, and that he is eternally righteous.
He has done wonderful things that people will always remember; Yahweh always acts kindly and mercifully.
He provides food for those who profoundly respect him; he never forgets the covenant that he made {with our ancestors}.
By enabling his people to capture the lands that had belonged to other people groups, he showed to {us,} his people, that he is very powerful.
He does everything fairly and in the right way, and we can trust that everything that he tells us to do is for our good.
We must obey his instructions forever; he created them in order to do what is best for us, and they are completely right.
He rescued us, his people, {from being slaves in Egypt,} and he made a covenant {with us} that will last forever. He is holy and awesome!
Having a profound respect for Yahweh is the way to become wise. All those who obey his instructions will come to understand why it is good to do them. We should praise him forever!
Praise Yahweh! How fortunate are those who have a profound respect for Yahweh; How fortunate are those who happily obey his commands!
Their descendants will prosper in their land; Yahweh will bless all who do what is right.
Their families will be wealthy, and their righteous deeds will endure forever.
For those who honor God, it is as if a light were shining on them in the darkness, on those who are kind, merciful, and righteous.
It is good to be kind to others and to generously lend money to them. A person like that does everything honestly.
Righteous people do this because they know that bad things will never overwhelm them; other people will always {joyfully} remember them.
Righteous people are not afraid when they receive bad news; they confidently trust in Yahweh.
They are confident and not afraid because they know that they will see God defeat their enemies.
They give things generously to poor people; their kind deeds will endure forever; people will greatly honor them.

Wicked people will see {those things} and become angry; they will gnash their teeth {angrily}, then people will stop hearing from them and they will die. The wicked things that they want to do will never happen.
Praise Yahweh! You people who serve Yahweh, praise him! Praise Yahweh for who he is!
Everyone should praise Yahweh for who he is, both now and forevermore!
From the people who live in the far east to the people who live in the far west, everyone should praise Yahweh for who he is!
Yahweh rules over all the nations, he is more glorious than anything under the heavens.
There is no one who is like Yahweh, the God whom we worship, who sits on his throne in the highest heaven
and who stoops down to look at the sky and at the earth.
He rescues very poor people from the very poor way that they live
and causes people to honor them by making them leaders among those who rule his people.
He also enables women who have had no children to live in their houses as happy mothers with children. Praise Yahweh!
When the Israelite people left Egypt, yes, when the descendants of Jacob left those people who spoke a foreign language,
the land of Judah became the place where people worshiped God; and the land of Israel became the area that he ruled over.

{When they came to} the Sea {of Reeds}, {it was as though the water} saw {them} and ran away! {When they came to} the Jordan River, {the water in the river} stopped flowing {so that the Israelites could cross it}.
{When Mount Sinai shook,} {it was as though} the mountains skipped like rams and the hills jumped like lambs.
{If someone asks,} “What happened at the Sea {of Reeds} that made it seem to run away? What happened that caused {the water in} the Jordan {River} to stop flowing?
{What happened at Mount Sinai that made the} mountains {seem to} skip like rams and made the hills {seem to} jump like lambs?”
{I would reply,} “The earth trembles because the Lord is there! Everyone should tremble because of the presence of the God whom Jacob worshiped!”
He is the one who caused pools of water to flow from a rock {for the Israelite people to drink}; indeed, he caused a spring to flow from a solid rock!

Yahweh, {we ask} not so people will honor us, no, not that at all; rather, we want people to honor you alone because of seeing how you faithfully love us and by seeing you do what you have promised to do.
It is not right that other people groups should say {about us}, “We do not see their God doing anything {to help them}.”
Well, the God whom we worship lives in heaven; he does whatever he wants!
But the idols of those people groups are only silver and gold {statues}; humans made them.
Their idols have mouths, but they cannot say anything; they have eyes, but they cannot see anything.
They have ears, but they cannot hear anything; they have noses, but they cannot smell anything.
They have hands, but they cannot feel anything; they have feet, but they cannot walk; they cannot even make any sounds in their throats!
The people who make those idols are {as powerless} as those idols, Everyone who trusts in those idols {to do anything} is also {powerless}!
You, my fellow Israelite people, trust in Yahweh! He is the one who helps you and protects you like a shield.
You {priests, the} descendants of Aaron, trust in Yahweh! He is the one who helps you and protects you like a shield.
All you who deeply respect Yahweh, trust in Yahweh! He is the one who helps you and protects you like a shield.
Yahweh has not forgotten us; he will bless {us}. he will bless us Israelite people! He will bless the priests!
Yahweh will bless all those who deeply respect him— those who are less important as well as the important people, that is, each one!
I pray that Yahweh may give {many children} {both} to you, {my fellow Israelite people,} and to your children {after you}.
I pray that Yahweh, the one who made heaven and the earth, may bless all of you!
The highest heavens belong to Yahweh, but he gave everything that is on the earth to humankind.
People who are dead are not able to praise Yahweh; when they go to the place where dead people are, they become silent and cannot praise him.
But we who are alive will praise Yahweh, both now and forevermore. Praise Yahweh!
I love Yahweh because he hears me when I cry out for him to help me.
I love him because he listens to me, so I will call out to him all during my life.
Everything around me caused me to think that I was about to die; it seemed to me that I was already dying. I was distressed and very sad.
But then I called out to Yahweh. I said, “Yahweh, I plead with you to save me!”
Yahweh is kind and does what is right. He is the God whom we worship, and he loves us.
Yahweh protects those who are helpless; when I was experiencing bad things, he saved me.
I encourage myself to relax once again because Yahweh has restored me.
Indeed, Yahweh has saved me from dying, he has delivered me from being sorrowful, and he has kept me from making bad mistakes.
So while I am still alive, I will live as Yahweh directs me.
I continued to trust {in Yahweh}, even when I said, “As for me, I am greatly suffering.”
For my part, I was so distressed that I thought, “I cannot trust anyone.”
I can never repay Yahweh for all the good things that he has done for me.
{But I can do this:} I will present a cup {of wine as a thank offering} as I call out to thank him for saving me.
Also, as the people who belong to Yahweh watch, I will give to him the offerings that I solemnly promised to give to him.
Yahweh is very grieved when one of his people dies.
Certainly I am one of Yahweh’s people; I am his servant; I have belonged to him since my mother bore me. So he saved me from what was going to kill me.

The following is the written lesson of the Teacher, who was a descendant of David and who ruled as king in Jerusalem.
The Teacher said: Every aspect of human life is as temporary and insubstantial as the fading mist of my breath! Everything is vaporous!
I want to know whether the never-ending labor of being alive in this world ever produces any sense of satisfaction or joy in this life that makes the labor of life worthwhile.
One generation of people dies, and another generation is born. Nonetheless, nothing seems to change.
The sun rises every morning and sets each evening. Then, it hurries back to the eastern horizon, from which it will rise again.
The wind blows southward. Then, it changes direction and blows northward. It seems to go around and around, and yet, it always seems to go where it is supposed to go.
All rivers and streams flow into the ocean, but the ocean is never full. Instead, all that water will continue to flow wherever it has always flowed.

These repetitive natural processes only make humanity tired. Similarly, no matter how much people have seen in their lives, they will always want to see more; no matter how much people have heard in their lives, they will always want to hear more.
Whatever happened in the past will happen again. Likewise, whatever people have done in the past, people will do it again. Nothing happens that is ever new.
Now, someone might claim to have discovered something novel. But, in reality, someone discovered it a long time ago, in times long since past.
No one ever remembers the people or the events of the past. The same will be true of the people and events of the future, and even of those after that!
Now imagine that I, the Teacher, was Qoheleth, who ruled as the king of Israel in the city of Jerusalem.

As Qoheleth, I resolved within myself to use my intellect and my understanding of the world to study everything that people do during their lives on this earth. I discovered that God has employed every human being in the difficult job of being alive.

Yes, I looked around and observed everything that people do during their lives. Now pay attention! I saw that our lives are as temporary and insubstantial as the fading mist of my breath. Humanity's endless labor is often as silly and frustrating as trying to grab a handful of the wind.
It is just like people say: “No one can fix what appears broken, and no one can count what is not there.”

So, I said to myself, “Now, pay attention! You know that I, the Teacher, have become wiser than any other king who has ever reigned in Jerusalem. I have experienced first-hand what it means to be exceptionally wise and intelligent.”

Having said this, I resolved to learn more about what it means to be wise, as well as what it means to be stupid and insane, by personal experience. I discovered that even these pursuits were as silly and frustrating as trying to grab a handful of the wind.
It is like people also say: “The wiser one gets, the angrier and more depressed they feel; knowing more about life only makes life hurt more.”

Then I said to myself, “Let me experiment. I will try to make myself as happy and satisfied as possible by doing everything that I enjoy.” Now pay attention! I concluded that even the joy and satisfaction I experienced from these pleasures were as temporary as the fading mist of my breath.
So I thought deeply and concluded that giddy laughter is the behavior of crazy people. Likewise, I reasoned that merely pursuing what I enjoyed did me no good.

So I thought deeply about the effect that indulging myself with wine or letting myself behave stupidly might have on me. All the while, I remained sober and alert. I thought about this up to the point that I could discern through my experiences the best use of humanity’s short lives on this earth.
So I did as many memorable and impressive things as I could. I ordered slaves to build palaces for my leisure and to till and plant vineyards for my pleasure.
I commissioned royal groves of fruit trees in my honor and gardens with flowing streams. Into those groves, I ordered that slaves should plant many kinds of fruit-bearing trees.
Furthermore I ordered the construction of irrigation pools and canals that provided water for entire forests of lush growth to honor me.

I purchased male and female slaves, and they bore children who were also my slaves in my palace. I also owned more livestock of herd and flock animals than any other previous king in Jerusalem’s history before me.

Moreover, I accumulated large amounts of silver and gold that I obtained from the tributary gifts of kings and the rulers of foreign territories. I owned slaves, both men and women, who sang for me, and I married wives and concubines, who provided me with sexual pleasure.

After all my efforts, I had attained more honor, power, and wealth than any king who had ever reigned before me in Jerusalem. Yet I continued to think soberly so that I could evaluate all of my work properly.

In all my efforts, I allowed myself to indulge in every desire that I had. Whatever I wanted, I permitted myself to enjoy it. I did this because my difficult projects made part of me happy, and that experience felt like a reward for all my hard work.

But then I stopped to think about everything I had accomplished, and all the difficult work that I had done to accomplish it all. Pay attention! I concluded that both my great effort and everything I achieved were as fleeting and insubstantial as the fading mist of my breath. Once again, my labors had been as silly and frustrating as trying to grab a handful of the wind. Nothing I did provided me with any sense of satisfaction or joy that made the difficulty of life worthwhile.

This led me to start thinking about the potential benefits of being wise alongside those of being crazy or stupid. I did this because, being king, I had more opportunity to investigate these issues than any other human being.

And then I recognized that being wise is far more helpful in life than being stupid, just like it is easier to live well when one has a source of light by which to see than when there is only darkness.

It is like people say: A wise person is able to live well and succeed, just like someone who walks about in the daylight can see where they are going. A foolish person, however, endangers themselves with their misinformed decisions, just like someone who walks about in the dark of night cannot see where they are going.

This made me say to myself, “I am going to die just as inevitably as stupid people! In this way, all my hard work to become a wise person appears to have made no difference! What was the point?” I reminded myself that even my attempts to become wise and live a longer and more fulfilled life were as fleeting and insubstantial as the fading mist of my breath.

After all, no one remembers anyone who dies, whether they lived wisely or stupidly, for very long. After a while, people will forget about both of them. How sad! No matter whether we live wisely or act like an idiot, everyone will eventually forget about us!

Because the job of being a human in this life includes enduring these realities that seemed to me to be burdensome and lamentable, I began to despise being alive. Everything seemed to be as temporary and insubstantial as the fading mist of my breath, and as silly and frustrating as trying to grab a handful of the wind.

Then I began to despise all the difficult and stressful work that I had labored to do during my life, especially because, after I die, someone else will come to inherit everything that I have earned, acquired, or accomplished with my life.

And no one can predict whether my successor will be a wise or a stupid person. Either way, even if he is stupid, he will have the ability to enjoy all the things that I labored so hard and so wisely for in my life to obtain and accomplish. Regardless, even his enjoyment of the outcomes of my hard work will be as fleeting and insubstantial as the fading mist of my breath.
As I thought further about all my life's work, I began to feel hopeless and depressed.

Partly I felt this way because it’s possible that someone might labor at his work wisely and expertly, even skillfully, for his entire life. But when he dies, his successor will inherit everything, even though the successor did not do any of the hard work that produced his inheritance! Yet even these painful realities are as fleeting and insubstantial as the fading mist of my breath.
After all, the emotionally and physically difficult labor that people do throughout their lives does not seem to produce anything that is both good and enduring for them.

This is because every day of one's life only seems to cause one pain. Furthermore, the work people do during their lives only produces grief. It is so grievous that, when they ought to be asleep at night, people's minds are so restless and anxious that they cannot rest. Yet even so, all of this is as fleeting and insubstantial as the fading mist of my breath.

So this is what I have concluded: The best way that people can live is simply to enjoy whatever they have to eat and drink and to allow themselves to find something enjoyable about their work. I have personally experienced that this kind of present-minded joy only comes when God gives it to someone.
After all, there is not a single human being who can enjoy the things he has if God does not first give those things to him.

God does this by making the people of whom he approves wise, insightfully intelligent, and happy. Conversely, God has decided that whoever disobeys him will work hard only so that they gain wealth that God will take away and give to those of whom he, God, approves. Yet in truth, even their wealth and hard work are as fleeting and insubstantial as the fading mist of my breath, and as silly and frustrating as trying to grab a handful of the wind.
There is a fixed moment at which everything in this life happens, and a determined period for every kind of event that happens during a person’s life:
People will give birth, and people will die; people will plant their crops, and people will reap and harvest those crops.
People will kill people, and people will heal people; people will tear structures down, and people will build structures.
People will cry, and people will laugh; people will grieve, and people will celebrate.
People will throw rocks, and people will gather rocks; people will hug, and people will refuse to hug.
People will look for lost things, and people will lose found things; people will store things, and people will throw things away.
People will rip their clothing {in grief}, and people will sew clothing back together; people will stay quiet, and people will talk.
People will love one another, and people will hate one another; people will go to war, and people will mediate peace.
Again, I want to know whether the never-ending, difficult labor of human life ever produces any sense of satisfaction or joy for hard-working people that makes the difficulty worthwhile.
I have observed the job of living in which God has employed every human being to bustle about doing.

God makes everything that happens in a person's life beautifully fitted for the moment that God has determined for it. And at the same time, God enables humanity to perceive that he is at work in their lives. Even so, God does not allow humanity to completely understand everything that God does—from the time that he created this world and began governing it to the point at which he brings all things to an end.
In light of this, I confess that the best way for humanity to live is to gratefully celebrate life and to live ethically while one is alive.

And, furthermore, whenever a person is able merely to enjoy whatever they have to eat and drink, and to find something gratifying in the work that they do, this is a priceless thing that God has enabled, like a present that he gives to humanity sometimes.
I also confess that all of God’s decisions are fixed and unchanging. It is like people say: No one can improve what God does, either by addition or subtraction.

Current events are not new. Something like things happening now already happened in the past. Likewise, future events will not be new. Something like the things that will happen in the future are already happening now. Despite all of this, God is the one who truly understands what every person is trying to understand.

However, here is something else that I observed: The very places in society from which people expect rulers to make just, fair, and equitable decisions are frequently places in which rulers make unjust, oppressive, and sinful decisions!

When I observed this, I confessed to myself, “God will hold accountable both people who make fair and equitable decisions and those who make unjust, oppressive, and sinful decisions. He will do this because he has determined that there is a moment for everything that happens during a person’s life, including God's judgment of the decisions of rulers in those places.”
This led me to confess further to myself: “God is governing the world this way because he wants people to clearly understand that they are really no different than animals.”

After all, human lives and animal lives end in the same way. People die just like animals die, and they seem to possess the same capacity to die. Because of this, it appears that being human offers no benefit over being an animal. All life is as fleeting and insubstantial as the fading mist of my breath.
When people and animals die, people bury both in the ground. Both people and animals are as mortal as if God made them from dirt, and when each dies their dead bodies become dirt once again.

This commonality causes me to wonder whether people are correct in their assumptions about what happens to people when they die. Perhaps, humans ascend to the place in which God lives, and only animals descend into wherever other dead things lie in the ground.

So I confess, once again, that the best way for people to live is to allow themselves to enjoy what their hard work produces— even the difficult work itself. This is because God has given each person their work for that day. It is their daily allotment—no more, no less. After all, nobody can really know for sure what will happen to them tomorrow.

Next, as I continued to contemplate, I observed all the ways in which people suffer from oppression during their lives. Now pay attention! As I watched those people cry, I realized that no one was there to reassure them in their grief. Furthermore, those who oppressed them appeared to possess power such that no one was able to reassure them in their grief.
This sad reality made me feel like those people who have already died are much more fortunate than the people who remain alive.

Yet the people whose mothers have not yet given birth to them are even more fortunate than both people currently alive and those people who have already died. Indeed, the unborn have not yet had to experience or witness any of the evil actions that humans do during their lives.

Then I observed that people work as hard as they do and strive to be successful only because they are jealous of their friends' lifestyles and possessions. Yet even their ill-motivated labor is as fleeting and insubstantial as the fading mist of my breath and as silly and futile as trying to grab a handful of the wind.

It is just like people say: Rather than work hard, foolish people merely relax with their unproductive hands folded on their laps, ready to eat their meal. Yet as they do so, they unwittingly ruin themselves, as if they were feasting on their own bodies!

People also say this: “Despite appearances, being contented with a simple, peaceful lifestyle is twice as good as being rich but living a life of stressful labor—as silly and frustrating as trying to grab a handful of the wind.”
I proceeded to contemplate another facet of people’s lives—one that also seemed as fleeting and insubstantial as the fading mist of my breath.

I saw someone who lived alone. He appeared to have no family—no children, nor any brothers or sisters lived with him. And every day, the lonely person labored without stopping. Even though he was very wealthy, he never felt fully satisfied with his lavish life and many possessions. Then he asked himself, “Why am I allowing my hard work to deprive me of things that I enjoy?” His attempts to satisfy himself with a lavish lifestyle were as fleeting and insubstantial as the fading mist of my breath. His joyless labor was really the most lamentable part of the difficult job of being alive in which God has employed humanity.
Having a friend is more advantageous than living one’s life alone. After all, together two people can experience better outcomes in their hard work.

First, if you were to fall down, a friend could help you get up again, but if you are alone and you fall down, you will only experience hardship and pain, because no one will be there to help you stand up again.
Second, if you and a friend were to lie down to sleep in the cold, you could help one another stay warm, but if you try to sleep in the cold alone, of course you will be cold!

Third, if someone stronger than you were to attack you, he might beat you up by yourself. However you and your friend would be able to ward off your attacker together! Three people could defend themselves even more easily, just as a rope that someone made from three strands is harder to rip in half than a rope with one or two strands.

It is preferable to be a poor young man who nonetheless acts wisely than to be a king who, despite his age, acts like a fool and refuses to pay attention when people try to give him good advice, as he did when he was younger.

I imagine that it is possible for a young man like that to live so successfully that he becomes king—even ruling over the land in which his mother gave birth to him in poverty, so severe that it was like someone tying her up with ropes.
But then I imagine all of the people in this young man’s kingdom who merely go about their lives. The person who will be the successor to the young king is among them.

Despite his current popularity with the endless crowds of his subjects, after a few years future generations will be tired of him too. So, in the end, even the wise way he lived that led to his success as king is as fleeting and insubstantial as the fading mist of my breath and as silly and frustrating as trying to grab a handful of the wind.

Be mindful of how you behave when you go to worship God at his house. Draw near to him to worship him by listening expectantly. That is far better than offering sacrifices to God in the ways that foolish people do. They are ignorant even of the fact that they are behaving inappropriately in God’s presence!

Do not be so quick to say something to God that you speak rashly about the words you say. Neither should you allow yourself to raise an issue hastily in God’s presence. You ought to remember that this God is the true uncreated God who rules from heaven, and that you, a mere creature, live here on the dust of the earth. For this reason, you ought to think carefully before you say anything in God’s presence.
