They have built worship sites to honor Baal, and at those places they have burned their sons in the fire as burnt offerings to Baal. I never commanded them to do that, I never told them to do that, and I never even thought about anyone doing that.
So pay attention, because a time will come when people will no longer call this place Topheth or Son of Hinnom Valley. Instead, they will call it the Valley of Slaughter.

In this place I will ruin the plans of the people that live in Jerusalem and the rest of Judah. I will allow their enemies to kill many of them with swords and allow those who want to kill them to succeed. Then I will let their dead bodies lie on the ground where all the scavenging birds and wild animals will eat them.
I will completely destroy this city so that it becomes a desolate place that people despise. Everyone who passes by it will be horrified and will gasp when they see all the destruction.

I will allow your enemies who want to kill you to surround the city so tightly and for so long that the food will all run out. Then the people in the city will become so desperately hungry that they will eat the flesh of their own sons and daughters, and each person will eat the flesh of his neighbor.’
{Then Yahweh said to me,} “After you say all of that, smash the jar while the people who came with you are watching.

Then say to them, ‘Yahweh, the commander of the heavenly armies, says this: Just as someone smashes a potter’s jar so that no one can ever put it back together, I will smash this people and this city in a similar way. People will bury the dead in Topheth until there is no more room to bury anyone else.

That is what I will do to this place and to the people who live here,’ declares Yahweh. ‘I will allow your enemies to desecrate this city like {king Josiah caused} Topheth {to be a place that was unfit for people to worship me in}.

Your enemies will desecrate the houses throughout Jerusalem and the palaces of the kings of Judah as {King Josiah did to} Topheth. That includes every house where you burned incense on the rooftops to honor the stars {that you worshiped,} and where you poured out wine {as an offering} to your gods.’”

Then {I}, Jeremiah returned from Topheth, where Yahweh had sent me to tell them that message. I went and stood in the courtyard of Yahweh’s temple and said this to all the people who had gathered there:

“Yahweh, the commander of the heavenly armies, the God of Israel, says this: ‘Pay attention! I am about to bring on this city and on all the towns around it every disaster that I said I would, because the people have stubbornly refused to listen to what I have said to them.’”
Pashhur, whose father was Immer, was a priest, and he was the chief supervisor in Yahweh’s temple. He heard Jeremiah prophesying these things.
So Pashhur beat {me}, Jeremiah, the prophet, and then put me in the stocks at the Upper Benjamin Gate in Yahweh’s temple.

The next day, Pashhur released {me,} Jeremiah from the stocks. Then {I,} Jeremiah said to him, “Yahweh is not going to call you Pashhur {anymore}. Instead, {he is going to call you} Terror on Every Side.

{Yahweh will call you this} because this is what he says regarding you: ‘Pay attention! I am going to make you a source of terror to yourself and to all your friends. You will watch as your enemies kill your friends with swords. I will let the king of Babylon conquer all the people of Judah. His soldiers will take some of them to Babylon, and they will kill others with swords.

I will enable their soldiers to take away everything valuable from this city—all its wealth, all the goods people worked hard to produce, and all its precious things—along with all the treasures that belonged to the kings of Judah. The enemies will plunder everything and carry it to Babylon.

And {as for} you, Pashhur, they will take you and everyone in your household, as captives to Babylon. You will die there, and people will bury you there—they will bury you and all your friends there, the ones you gave false prophecies to.’”

{Then I, Jeremiah, said,} “Yahweh, you persuaded me {to become your prophet,} and I let you persuade me. You were stronger than I was, and you won. Now people ridicule me throughout the day; everyone makes fun of me.
Whenever I speak your messages, I shout, ‘{Yahweh is going to cause you to experience} violence and destruction!’ So because I tell people your messages, they insult me throughout the day.

Sometimes I think to myself, “I will stop mentioning Yahweh, and I will stop speaking messages from him.” However, {when I try to remain silent,} his message becomes like a fire in my inner being, that I cannot hold back. I grow weary of trying to contain it, and I cannot hold back {from speaking Yahweh’s messages}.

I hear many people whispering {about me, saying, “He is the man who proclaims that there will be things that cause us to be} terrified all around us! We must tell {the authorities} what he is saying!” All the people who pretended to be my friends are watching for me to make a mistake. {They say,} ‘Maybe we can trick him into saying something wrong, and then we can defeat him and get our revenge on him.’

However, Yahweh is with me, and he defends me powerfully. So those who persecute me will stumble and will not defeat me. They will feel very ashamed because they did not succeed, and no one will ever forget how God disgraced them.

Yahweh, the commander of the heavenly armies, you examine those who do what is right. You know what everyone thinks and what motivates them. Allow me to see you punish those people who want to harm me, because I have told you about my case and asked you to help me.”
Sing to Yahweh! Praise Yahweh! Because he rescues needy people from the power of wicked people.
I curse the day my mother gave birth to me! May no one celebrate that day.
{As for} the man who brought the news to my father, and made him very happy by saying, “{Your wife} has given birth to a baby boy”, I wish someone would curse that man.

May Yahweh destroy that man as he did to the cities he destroyed {in the past}, without acting mercifully {toward them}. May that man hear people crying out in distress in the morning and hear {enemy soldiers} shout their {battle} cries at noon.
{I say this} because he did not kill me before I came out of my mother’s womb. If he had, I would have died inside my mother and never come out.

I wish that I had not come out of my mother’s womb so that I would not have to experience all these difficult things that cause me to feel so miserable, and so that I would not come to the end of my life feeling disgraced.

Yahweh gave me {another} message when King Zedekiah {of Judah} sent a man named Pashhur, whose father was Malkijah, and a priest named Zephaniah, whose father was Maaseiah{, to talk to me. They pleaded with me,} saying,

“{The army of} King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon is attacking Judah, so please speak to Yahweh for us. {Ask him if he will help us.} Perhaps he will force Nebuchadnezzar’s {army} to leave by performing a miracle for us, like the miracles he performed {previously}.”
I replied to them, “{Go back to King} Zedekiah. Tell him this,

‘This is what Yahweh, the God whom we Israelites worship, says: “Pay attention! I will cause your weapons to be useless in fighting against the king of Babylon and his army that is outside the walls of Jerusalem, attacking. I will cause your soldiers to lay their weapons down in the midst of this city.
I myself will fight against your army with my very great power, because I am very angry with you.
I will send a very terrible plague on the people of this city, and on their domestic animals, and {many of} them will die.’

Yahweh says, ‘After those things occur, I will enable {the army of} King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon, and your other enemies, and the others who seek to kill you, to capture {you,} {you} Zedekiah who rule in Judah, and your officials, and {all the other} people who remain in this city and have not died from the plague, from enemy soldiers, and from starvation. I will allow Nebuchadnezzar’s army to slaughter those of you who remain; they will not act mercifully toward you at all or spare people.’

And tell this to this people: ‘Yahweh says that you must pay careful attention and decide whether you want to choose the way that will result in your dying or choose the way that will result in your staying alive.

Everyone who remains in Jerusalem will die because enemy soldiers will kill them or they will die from starvation or from diseases. But those who surrender to the army of Babylon that is surrounding your city will live. They will escape with nothing except their lives, but will remain alive.

{This will happen} because I, Yahweh, have decided to cause the inhabitants of this city to experience disasters and not to experience something good. I have decided to allow {the army of} the king of Babylon to capture this city and his army will destroy it completely by fire.’”
Yahweh also told me to say this to the family of the king of Judah: “Listen to this message from Yahweh.

This is what he says to you descendants of King David: ‘Every day, make fair decisions for the people whom you judge. Help those whom people have robbed. Rescue them from robbers and abusers. If you do not do that, I will be angry and punish you with a fire that will be impossible to extinguish, because of all the sins that you have committed.

Know that I will oppose you people {of Jerusalem}, you who live on top of a rocky hill above the valley. {I will oppose} you people who boast, saying, “No one can attack us and break through our defenses.”
I will punish you for your wicked deeds like you deserve to be punished; {It will be as though} I will light a fire in your forests that will burn up everything around you.’”
Yahweh gave me this message: “Go down to the palace of the king of Judah and tell him this message.
Say, ‘Listen to what Yahweh has to say to you, king of Judah, you who rule in succession to King David. You, your officials, and your people who enter through these gates must listen.

This is what Yahweh says: Treat people fairly and do what is right. Rescue anyone who has had his things stolen. Rescue that person from the power of the one oppressing them. Do not mistreat foreigners who are living among you, or orphans, or widows. Do not harm anyone, and do not kill innocent people in this place.

If you carefully obey these commands, then there will {always} be a king from David’s royal line ruling {in Jerusalem}. Each king with his officials and his people will ride through the gates of this palace in chariots and on horses.
However, if you refuse to obey these commands, then I, Yahweh, swear by my own name that this palace will become a pile of rubble.’””

This is what Yahweh says about the palace of the king of Judah: “{I value} this palace as much as I value the forests in {the region of} Gilead and the mountains in Lebanon. Nevertheless, I will certainly make it a desolate place where no one lives.
I will send enemy troops to destroy it; each soldier with his own weapons. They will chop down the fine cedar beams and throw them into the fire.
People from many nations will pass by the ruins of this city and ask one another, ‘Why did Yahweh do this to such a great city?’
{Other} people will answer, ‘{He did it} because his people stopped obeying the agreement they had made with Yahweh their God and instead worshiped and served other gods.’”

Do not weep for King Josiah who died; do not mourn for him. {Instead,} weep bitterly for {King Jehoahaz, his son, because} he will go away into exile, {weep} because he will never come back and he will never see his homeland again.
Yahweh says this about Shallum son of Josiah, king of Judah, who became king after his father Josiah and who was captured and taken away from here {to Babylon}: “He will never come back here again.
He will die in the place where his enemies took him, and he will never return to this land.”

{Yahweh says,} “Terrible things will happen to King Jehoiakim! He does not act fairly when he forces people to build his palace. He forces his neighbors to work for nothing and does not pay them for their labor.

He says, “I will {force my workers} to build me a huge palace with large, spacious rooms on the upper level. I will {make them} cut out windows for me, and panel the walls with boards made of cedar wood, and paint it bright red.”

Having a beautiful palace with cedar paneling does not make a king great! Your father {Josiah} had plenty of things to eat and drink, but he always treated people fairly and did what was right. Because of that, things went well for him.
Josiah made sure that judges treated poor and needy people fairly, and things went well because of that. That is what it means to truly know me.” {That is what} Yahweh declares.

“But Jehoiakim, you pay attention to nothing and desire nothing except getting things by cheating people and shedding the blood of innocent people, and oppressing people, and you use force to get what you want.

Therefore, this is what Yahweh says about Jehoiakim son of King Josiah, king of Judah: “{When he dies} people will not mourn for him, saying, ‘How sad, my brother! How sad, my sister!’ People will not mourn for him, saying, ‘How sad, my master! How sad for him who was majestic!’
People will bury his corpse the way they dispose of a dead donkey: they will drag his body out and throw it beyond the gates of Jerusalem.
{You people of Jerusalem,} go up to Lebanon and cry out! Shout loudly in Bashan! Cry out from Abarim, because your enemies have destroyed all the nations that were your political allies.
I warned you when things were going well for you, {but} you said, ‘I will not listen.’ You have behaved this way ever since you were young, for you have never obeyed me.

I will punish all your leaders; {it will be as though} they have been blown away by the wind. Your enemies will take your political allies away as prisoners. Then you will certainly feel deeply ashamed and everyone will despise you because of all the evil things you have done.

You {people of Jerusalem} who think you are as safe as a bird nesting in the cedar trees that grow in Lebanon, people will greatly pity you when you begin to suffer, you will suffer severely as a woman does when she is giving birth!”
Yahweh declares, “As surely as I am alive, even if you, Coniah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, were a ring on my finger that shows that I am the king, I would still pull you off.
You are afraid of King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon and his huge army, {because} they are wanting to kill you. I will enable them to capture you.
I will expel you and your mother who gave birth to you into another land where neither of you were born, and you will both die there.
Neither of you will ever return to this land that you both will greatly desire to return to.”

{People say,} “Coniah will be like a broken pot that people despise or a vessel which no one wants. Enemy soldiers will force him and his children to go to a foreign land that they are not familiar with.”
People of this land, people of this land, people of this land, listen to what Yahweh says!

This is what Yahweh says: “Write down {in the record about the kings of Judah} that {it will be as though} this man has no descendants, and that he has not been successful during his lifetime, because none of his children will become king and rule in succession of King David as king over Judah.”

Yahweh declares, “Terrible things will happen to the leaders of my people, {who were supposed to guide and care for my people like shepherds guide and care for their sheep}. Terrible things will happen to the leaders of my people because they have scattered and harmed my people {instead of caring for them}.

So this is what I, Yahweh, the God whom the Israelite people worship, say to those leaders: ‘Instead of taking care of my people as a shepherd does for his sheep, you have scattered them and driven them away, and you have not paid attention to them. Know that I will make sure to punish you for the evil things that you have done.’” This is what Yahweh declares.
“Then I myself will gather the rest of my people from all the countries where I have driven them. I will bring them back to their own land, where they will have many children and increase in number.
I will appoint other leaders for my people who will take care of them. My people will never again be afraid or dismayed, and none of them will go missing.” This is what Yahweh declares.

Yahweh {also} declares, “Listen! A time is coming when I will appoint from David’s family line a righteous descendant. He will rule as king and will act wisely. He will do what is just and right throughout the land.
At the time he begins to reign, Yahweh will rescue the people of Judah, and the people of Israel will live securely. People will call him by this name: ‘Yahweh makes us right with him.’”

“So listen! A time is coming,” Yahweh declares, “when people {who are making a solemn promise} will no longer say, ‘{I promise, as surely} as Yahweh lives, the one who brought the Israelite people up from the land of Egypt.’

Instead, they will say, ‘{I promise, as surely} as Yahweh lives, the one who brought {us} Israelite people back {to our own land when} he led us from the land to the northeast and from all the {other} countries where he had exiled us.’ Then they will live in their own land {again}.”

{This is what I, Jeremiah, say} about the prophets: My mind is greatly distressed. My entire body is shaking. I am so overcome by strong feelings that I am less capable of doing things, like a man who has had too much wine. {I feel this way} because of Yahweh, and because of his holy words.

The land is full of people who commit adultery. Because Yahweh has placed a curse on the land, the land dries up and the pastures in the wilderness have dried up. The people do evil things, and those who have powerful positions use them to do things that are not right.
Yahweh declares, “Even the prophets and the priests have turned away from me. I have found them doing evil things even in my temple.

So I will make the events of their life be as though they were walking on slippery paths in the dark. I will ensure that they experience hardships {so that it will be as though} I am pushing them down and they are falling, when I cause disastrous things to happen to them at the time when I punish them.” This is what {I} Yahweh declare.

“I saw that the prophets in Samaria were doing something that was wrong: They were prophesying, saying that Baal gave them the messages they were proclaiming and they were deceiving my people, the Israelites.

And {now} I have seen the prophets in Jerusalem doing something horrible: They commit adultery and habitually tell lies. They have encouraged people who do evil so that no one stops doing evil things. All of them have become as wicked as the people of Sodom, and the people of Jerusalem have become as wicked as the people of Gomorrah.”

So this is what Yahweh, the commander of the heavenly armies, says about those prophets: “Know that I will cause them to suffer so that it will be as if they will eat bitter things and drink poisoned water, because on account of the lies being prophesied by the prophets of Jerusalem, wicked things are done throughout the whole land.”

This is what Yahweh, the commander of the heavenly armies, says: “Do not pay any attention to what those prophets say to you, {because} they are only deceiving you. They tell you about things that they imagined in their own minds. Yahweh did not give them those messages.
They keep saying to people who despise me, ‘Yahweh says that things will go well for you.’ They tell everyone who stubbornly does whatever he wants to do, ‘Nothing bad will happen to you.’

But none of these prophets has ever been in a council meeting where Yahweh gave his private counsel or seen and heard what Yahweh said. None of them has paid attention to what Yahweh said and truly listened.
Look! Yahweh has sent out a furious storm. It whirls down on the heads of wicked people.
Yahweh will not stop being angry until he has completely accomplished everything that he has planned. In the future, you will clearly understand this.
“I did not send these prophets, yet they rushed {to tell people their messages}. I did not speak to them, yet they {kept on} prophesying.
If they had sought my counsel, then they would have proclaimed my words to my people, and they would have caused my people to stop doing evil things.”
Yahweh {also} declares, “I am not a God who is only nearby. I am also a God who is far away.
No one can hide in a secret place where I cannot see him.” Yahweh declares, “I am present everywhere, in heaven and on the earth.” This is what Yahweh declares.
“I have heard what those prophets have said, the ones who claim to speak for me but prophesy lies. They say, ‘I had a dream {that God gave me}! I had a dream {that God gave me}!’
These prophets will not stop prophesying false things that come from their own deceitful minds.
They plan to make my people forget about me by telling their dreams to one another, just as their ancestors forgot about me when they started to worship Baal.

Allow any prophet who has a dream to tell his dream. However, those who have messages that truly come from me must speak my messages faithfully. As straw and grain are certainly very different, so messages from false prophets are certainly very different from messages from true prophets.” It is {I}, Yahweh, who declare this.

“My message has great power. It is as though my messages burn like a fire; they strike people’s inner beings like someone strikes a rock with a hammer and smashes it into pieces.” {I} Yahweh declare this.
“So, I oppose all those prophets who steal messages from each other and then claim those messages came from me,” {I} Yahweh declare this.
“I oppose those prophets {who steal messages from each other and then} use their tongues to say, ‘Yahweh declares this,’” This is what {I} Yahweh declare.

“I am against the ones who prophesy lying dreams. Those people tell their lying dreams to my people and their lies and careless behavior cause my people to stop obeying me. I did not command them {to speak those things} or send them {to my people} and as a result they certainly do not help my people.” This is what {I}, Yahweh declare.

{Yahweh said to me, Jeremiah,} “When any of these people or a prophet or a priest asks you, ‘What message has Yahweh given you?’ you must reply to them, ‘What burden? Yahweh declares that he will forsake you!’
And if any prophet or priest or Israelite person says, ‘I have a message from Yahweh,’ I will punish that person and his family.
What you should ask each other is, ‘What is Yahweh’s answer?’ or ‘What has Yahweh said?’

But stop saying ‘{I have} a message from Yahweh,’ because when each person claims his own words are a message from Yahweh, he distorts the message of the living God, Yahweh, the commander of the heavenly armies, our God.
This is what you should ask each prophet: ‘What has Yahweh answered you?’ or ‘What has Yahweh said?’

But if he says, ‘I have a message from Yahweh,’ then {I} Yahweh say this: ‘Because you have kept saying, “{I have} a message from Yahweh,” even though I told you, “You must not say, ‘{I have} a message from Yahweh.’”
So I {Yahweh,} will certainly forget about you and forsake you and this city that I gave to you and to your ancestors. {I will expel you} from my presence.
I will cause people to make fun of you forever. People will never forget that I caused you to be ashamed.’”’”

After King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon had taken away Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, along with the officials of Judah, the craftsmen, and the smiths from Jerusalem and brought them to Babylon, Yahweh showed me something. I saw two baskets of figs that someone had placed in front of the temple of Yahweh.
One basket had very good figs in it, like figs that ripen early in the season. The other basket had very bad figs in it that no one could eat because they were so bad.
Then Yahweh said to me, “Jeremiah, what do you see?”
Then Yahweh gave me this message. He said,

“This is what {I} Yahweh, the God of the Israelite people, say: Like these good figs, similarly I will regard favorably the people of Judah whom I sent away from this place to the land of the Chaldeans.

I will watch over them for the purpose of doing good things for them, and I will cause them to return to this land. I will establish them and not destroy them. I will cause them to prosper, and I will not remove them.
I will enable them to desire to know me, that I am Yahweh. They will be my people, and I will be their God, for they will return to me sincerely.

But, this is {also} what {I,} Yahweh, say: Like the bad figs that are so bad that people cannot eat them {and instead get rid of them}, so I will treat Zedekiah the king of Judah, his officials, those who still remain in Jerusalem, those who are still living in this land, and those who have gone to live in the land of Egypt.

I will deliver them over so that horrible things that will harm them will happen to them with the result that people in every kingdom on the earth will reproach them, and they will be the subject of proverbs, and taunts, and curses, in all the places where I will exile them.
I will cause them to experience wars and famines and diseases, until they have disappeared from the land that I gave to them and to their ancestors.”

Yahweh gave this message to {me,} Jeremiah, about all the people of Judah. This happened during the fourth year that Jehoiakim son of Josiah ruled as king of Judah, which was also the first year that Nebuchadnezzar ruled as king of Babylon.
{I,} Jeremiah, a prophet {of Yahweh}, spoke {this message} to all the people of Judah and to all the people living in Jerusalem. I said,

“For twenty-three years Yahweh has been giving me messages —from the thirteenth year that Josiah son of Amon ruled as king of Judah until today. I have spoken to you again and again, but you have not listened.
Yahweh also, repeatedly, sent to you all his {other} prophets who serve him, but you did not heed their warnings. You refused to pay attention.

{Those prophets} said, ‘Each of you must stop your evil habits and stop doing evil things. If you do that, you will be able to continue living in this land that Yahweh gave to you and to your ancestors to be yours forever.
Do not cause {me,} Yahweh to become angry by serving and worshiping idols that you have made with your hands. If {you do not do those things}, I will not cause harmful things to happen to you.’

Yahweh says, ‘Yet you refused to pay attention to the messages that I gave my prophets, and as a result you made me very angry by {worshiping} the idols that you made. That caused harmful things to happen to you.
Therefore, Yahweh, the commander of the heavenly armies, says this: Because you have not paid attention to what I said {to you through my prophets},

know that I am about to summon all the people groups who live north of you’ —this is what {I,}Yahweh say —‘I will also summon my servant Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon. I will bring them against this land and against the people living in it and against the people of all of these surrounding nations and I will completely destroy them. I will make them an object of horror and scorn, and they will stay in ruins forever.

I will cause happy singing and laughing to cease in your land. There will no longer be bridegrooms or brides talking {joyfully}. No one will hear the grinding of millstones, and there will not be people lighting lamps {in the evening}.
This entire land will become an empty ruin, and the people of these nations will serve the king of Babylon for seventy years.

Then, when seventy years have passed, I will punish the king of Babylon and his people for the wrong things they have done’ —this is what Yahweh says. ‘I will also punish the land of the Chaldeans and make it an empty ruin forever.
I will cause them to experience everything that I have said I would do to it —everything that Jeremiah has prophesied against all the nations, everything that {my servant} wrote in this book.

The people of many nations and powerful kings will then force the Babylonians to serve them, like the people of Babylonia caused my people to become slaves. I will give the Babylonians what they deserve for the things they have done.’”

Then Yahweh, the God of {us} Israelites, {gave me a vision. In the vision he was holding a cup of wine}. He said this to me: “Take this cup from my hand. The wine in it {represents} the punishment I am about to send. Go and make all the nations drink from it—all the nations to which I am sending you.
When they drink {it}, they will stagger and will act like crazy people because of the wars that I am going to send against them.”
So I took the cup from Yahweh, and I made the people of all the nations to which Yahweh had sent me, drink from it.

{First I went to} Jerusalem and the {other} cities of Judah, and the king and the officials. And, starting from that day, they all {eventually} lost their positions of authority and became people whom others ridiculed, and they became the object of peoples curses.
{In the vision I then went to Egypt and gave some of the wine to} Pharaoh king of Egypt, along with his servants, his officials, and all his people,

and all the foreigners {living in Egypt. In the vision I also went to the land of Uz and gave some of the wine to} all the kings of the land of Uz, and all the kings of the land of the Philistines —those in Ashkelon, Gaza, Ekron, and the few people remaining in Ashdod.
{I also gave some of the wine to} the people of Edom, Moab, and to the Ammonites.
I also {gave some of the wine to} all the kings of Tyre and all the kings of Sidon, and the kings of the coastlands across the sea.
{In the vision I then went} to the people of Dedan, Tema, and Buz {and gave them some of the wine}, and all those who cut their hair short on the sides.
I also {gave} all the kings of Arabia {some of the wine}, and all the kings of the foreign people who live in the wilderness.
I also {gave} all the kings of Zimri, all the kings of Elam, and all the kings of Media {some of the wine}.

{I also gave} all the kings of the north {some of the wine}, both those near and those far away {from Israel}, one after another —{I went to} all the kingdoms on the earth. And {finally in my vision, I went to} the king of Babylon {and gave him the wine that symbolized that Yahweh would punish the people of Babylon because he was angry with them} and he shall drink it after the other kings.

“Then {in the vision Yahweh said to me,} tell them, ‘Yahweh, the commander of the heavenly armies, the God of Israel, says this: Drink and become drunk and vomit. Fall down and never get up again, because of the wars that I am sending against you.’
If any of them refuse to take the cup from your hand and drink, tell them, ‘Yahweh, the commander of the heavenly armies, says this: You absolutely must drink!

Pay attention! I am already starting to cause the people of my own city to experience disaster and I will certainly punish you! I will punish you, for I am causing there to be wars in all the nations on the earth” —this is what Yahweh, the commander of the heavenly armies, says.

“Now prophesy all these words to them and say to them, ‘Yahweh will shout loudly from heaven above, from the holy place where he lives he will raise his voice. He will shout loudly against the people of his own land, so loudly that {it will sound like} the roar of a lion. He will shout to everyone on the earth, {like} people shout triumphantly when they are treading on grapes {to make juice for wine}.

I will terrify the people of Elam in front of their enemies, in front of those who are trying to kill them. Because I am extremely angry with them, I will bring disaster on them. That is what I, Yahweh, declare. I will send soldiers with swords to pursue them until I have destroyed all of them.
I will rule and judge the people of Elam, and I will destroy their king and their officials there. That is what I, Yahweh, declare.
Yet in the distant future I will restore the fortunes of the people of Elam and bring them back to their land. That is what I, Yahweh, declare.”
Yahweh spoke this message about the city of Babylon and about the land of the Chaldeans {that is, Babylonia,} and he gave it to Jeremiah the prophet to announce:

“Tell the nations what will happen, and make sure that they hear it; raise a flag to signal them, and do not keep any of it secret. Everyone can now see that the idols of Babylon are worthless and that its images can do nothing to help anyone.

A nation from the north will march against Babylon and will turn its land into a place that horrifies everyone who sees it. No one will live there anymore; both the people and the animals will run away from it.

I, Yahweh, declare that in those days, at that time, the people of Israel and the people of Judah will come back together. They will weep as they travel, and they will come looking for me, Yahweh their God.

“My people have become like sheep that have gotten lost. Their leaders have caused them to wander away from me, taking them from one hill to another, until my people forgot that I was the one who kept them safe.

“You Israelites, get away from the city of Babylon, and go out from the land of the Chaldeans! Lead the way out, just as male goats walk ahead of the flock.

Listen! I am stirring up a group of powerful nations in the north, and I am bringing them against Babylon. They will line up in battle formation against the city, and they will capture it. Their soldiers will shoot their arrows skillfully, and every arrow will hit its target.
Enemies will plunder the land of the Chaldeans, and everyone who plunders it will take away all that they want. That is what I, Yahweh, declare.

You people of Babylon are celebrating and shouting for joy because you plundered the people who belong to me. You prance about restlessly, like a young cow treading out grain, and you whinny like strong stallions.

However, Babylon, the city that is like a mother to you, will suffer complete shame and disgrace. It will become the least important of all the nations, a dry and empty wilderness where nothing grows.

Because I, Yahweh, am extremely angry with Babylon, no one will live there; the whole city will lie in ruins. Everyone who passes by Babylon will shudder in horror and will hiss to show their scorn when they see how badly enemies have ruined it.
All you archers, take your positions around Babylon! Shoot at the city; do not save any of your arrows, because its people have sinned against me, Yahweh.

Shout your battle cry against the city from every side! The people of Babylon are surrendering; the towers that support its walls are collapsing, and enemy soldiers are tearing its walls down. I, Yahweh, am paying Babylon back for what it did, so pay it back yourselves! Do to its people exactly what they have done to others!

Do not let anyone in Babylon plant crops or harvest the grain with a sickle. Because the enemy army will attack so cruelly, all the foreigners living there will run back to their own people; each one will flee to his own land.

The people of Israel are like sheep that lions have chased and scattered. The king of Assyria was the first one who attacked and devoured them, and after him Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon crushed them completely.”

So this is what Yahweh, the commander of the heavenly armies, the God whom the Israelites worship, says: “Listen! I am about to punish the king of Babylon and his land, just as I punished the king of Assyria.

I will bring the people of Israel back to their own land, where they will have plenty of food from the fields of Carmel and Bashan. In the hill country of Ephraim and in Gilead they will eat all that they want.

I, Yahweh, declare that in those days, at that time, if anyone searches for any wrong thing that the people of Israel have done, he will find nothing, and if anyone searches for any sin that the people of Judah have committed, he will find nothing, because I will forgive the few people whom I allow to survive.

Attack the land of Merathaim! Attack the people who live in Pekod! Chase after them, kill them, and destroy them completely, doing everything that I have commanded you. That is what I, Yahweh, declare.”
People hear the noise of battle throughout the land; they hear the noise of terrible destruction.
Babylon used to crush all the other nations, the way a hammer smashes things, but now Yahweh has shattered Babylon itself! The other nations shudder in horror at what has happened to Babylon!
Yahweh says, “I set a trap for the people of Babylon, and I caught them before they realized what was happening. I found them and seized them, because they had fought against me.”

Yahweh has brought out the armies that he will use to show how angry he is, just as a warrior opens his storehouse and takes out his weapons. The Lord Yahweh, the commander of the heavenly armies, has work to do in the land of the Chaldeans.

You enemies, come against Babylon from far away! Break open the buildings where its people store their grain! Pile up the ruins of the city in heaps, the way people pile up grain, and destroy the city completely. Do not let anyone there survive.
Kill all of Babylon’s strongest soldiers; send them all down to the slaughter. How terrible it will be for them! The time has come when Yahweh will punish them.
Listen! People who have escaped and fled from the land of Babylon are announcing in Zion how Yahweh our God has paid Babylon back, how he has punished its people for destroying his temple.

Yahweh says, “Summon the archers to attack Babylon! All you who shoot arrows, set up your camps all around the city. Do not let anyone escape from it. Pay its people back for what they have done; do to them everything that they have done to others, because they arrogantly defied me, Yahweh, the holy God whom the Israelites worship.
So its young men will fall dead in the city squares, and on that day all its soldiers will die. That is what I, Yahweh, declare.”
The Lord Yahweh, the commander of the heavenly armies, says, “Listen, you arrogant people of Babylon! I am against you, because the time has now come when I will punish you.
You arrogant people will stumble and fall, and no one will help you get up again. I will start a fire in your cities, and it will burn up everything around you.”

This is what Yahweh, the commander of the heavenly armies, says: “Enemies are cruelly oppressing the people of Israel and the people of Judah. Everyone who captured them is holding them tightly and refusing to let them go.”

However, the one who will set them free is strong; his name is Yahweh, the commander of the heavenly armies. He will certainly defend them when they plead their case, so that he may bring rest to their land and make the people who live in Babylon tremble.
Yahweh declares, “Enemy soldiers will come with swords to kill the Chaldeans and the people who live in Babylon, and also its officials and its wise men.
They will kill the false prophets of Babylon, and everyone will see that those prophets were fools. They will attack Babylon’s warriors, and those warriors will tremble with terror.

They will kill Babylon’s horses and destroy its chariots, and they will kill the foreign soldiers who fight in its army, and those soldiers will lose all their courage. Enemies will break into Babylon’s storehouses and carry off everything valuable.
I will send a drought on Babylon’s rivers, and they will dry up, because the people there have filled their land with idols, and those terrifying idols have made the people act like madmen.
So wild animals of the desert will live there along with hyenas, and ostriches will make their homes in the city. No people will ever live there again; no one will settle there for all time to come.

I will destroy Babylon just as I destroyed the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah and the towns near them. No one will live there; no human being will ever stay there again. That is what I, Yahweh, declare.
Look! An army is coming from the north. I am stirring up a great nation and many kings from lands far away.

Those soldiers carry bows and curved swords; they are cruel and will not act mercifully toward anyone. The noise they make is as loud as the roaring sea. They ride on horses, and they line up in battle formation like one man to attack you people of Babylon.
When the king of Babylon hears the reports about that army, he will lose all his strength and courage. He will feel great distress and anguish, like a woman who is about to give birth.

Look! I will attack suddenly, like a lion that comes out of the thick bushes along the Jordan River and springs on sheep in a safe pasture. In a moment I will chase the people of Babylon out of their land, and then I will appoint over them the ruler whom I choose. No one is like me, and no one can call me to account. No ruler anywhere is able to stand and oppose me.”

So listen to what Yahweh has decided to do to the city of Babylon and to what he has planned to do to the land of the Chaldeans: Enemies will certainly drag away even the weakest of the Babylonians, and Yahweh will certainly turn their homeland into a wasteland.
When enemies capture Babylon, the noise will be so loud that the whole earth will shake, and people in all the nations will hear the Babylonians crying out.

Yahweh says this: “Listen! I am about to bring {an army} against the city of Babylon and against the people who live in the land of the Babylonians that will destroy them {as quickly as} a powerful wind.

I will send foreigners to attack Babylon. Like a strong wind, they will scatter its people in every direction and leave its land empty. They will surround that city on every side when the time comes for me to destroy it.

Do not give the archers of Babylon time to string their bows, and do not let any soldier there stand up wearing his armor. Do not spare Babylon’s young men. Destroy its whole army completely, as a sacrifice.
Enemies will kill Babylon’s soldiers in their own land. The enemies will stab them, and let their bodies fall in the streets of the city.”

This will happen because Yahweh, the commander of the heavenly armies, has not abandoned the people of Israel or the people of Judah. He is still their God, even though the Israelites throughout their land have sinned again and again against the holy God whose people they are.

Run away from the city of Babylon! Each of you, run away to save your life! Do not stay there and die when Yahweh punishes its people for their sins, because the time has come for Yahweh to punish them as they deserve. He is paying them back for what they have done.

{When Yahweh used Babylon to severely punish every nation on the earth, it was as though} Babylon was a golden cup in Yahweh’s hand that he made all of the nations of the earth drink wine from until they became drunk. As a result, the people of those nations now behave like crazy people.

But suddenly enemies will conquer the city of Babylon and destroy it. {When that happens, Babylon’s enemies will mock its people by saying,} “Cry out loudly because of what has happened to Babylon! Bring healing salve for its wounds; maybe someone can heal it with medicine!”

{The foreigners living there will say,} “We tried to heal Babylon, but it did not get well. Let us abandon it, and let each of us return to his own land, because its people have sinned so much that {it is as though} their sins have piled up to the sky, and God is punishing them an equal amount.”

{The Israelites will say,} “Yahweh has shown everyone that we were the ones who were doing what was right. Come, let us go to Zion and tell the people there everything that Yahweh our God has done {for us}.”

{You soldiers of Media,} sharpen your arrows! Fill your quivers {with them}! Yahweh has made the kings of Media determined to fight {against Babylon}, because he has decided to destroy the city of Babylon. Yahweh will do this to repay its people {for what they did}; he is punishing them for what they did to his temple.

Raise a signal flag to attack the walls of the city of Babylon! Post more guards! Station men to keep watch! Set soldiers in place to attack without warning, because Yahweh is now doing exactly what he planned to do to the people who live in Babylon, which is what he also said that he would do to them.

The city of Babylon sits beside the great river and its many canals, and its people have become very wealthy. But now the time for that city to exist has ended. {It is as though} Babylon’s life is over.

Yahweh, the commander of the heavenly armies, has solemnly sworn by himself, “City of Babylon, I will certainly fill you with enemy soldiers, as many of them as a swarm of locusts, and they will shout {triumphantly} over you {when they defeat you}.”
Yahweh is the one who made the earth because he is powerful; he set the world firmly in place because he is wise, and because he understands everything, he created the heavens.

When he thunders, the waters in the sky roar, and he causes clouds to rise from the most distant places on the earth. He sends lightning along with the rain, and he sends out the wind from where he keeps it.

People tend to be stupid and ignorant. Even craftsmen who work with gold should feel disgraced because of the idols that they carve, because the idols that they cast deceive people; they are not alive at all.
Those idols are worthless, and people ought to laugh at them. When the time comes for Yahweh to punish {the people who worship} them, he will destroy them all.

The God whom the descendants of Jacob worship is not like those idols, because he is the one who formed everything that exists, including the tribe that he chose to belong to him. His name is Yahweh, the commander of the heavenly armies.

{To the army of Babylon, Yahweh would say,} “I have used you as a soldier uses his war club to smash {his enemies}; by means of you I have destroyed {the armies of other} nations, yes, by means of you I have conquered kingdoms.
By means of you I have destroyed horses and the men who ride them; by means of you I have destroyed chariots and the men who drive them.
By means of you I have destroyed men and women, old people and young people, young men and young women.
By means of you I have destroyed shepherds and their flocks, farmers and the oxen that they plow with, governors and the officials who serve under them.

But now{, people of Israel,} I will punish the people of the city of Babylon and all of the people of that entire country for all of the terrible things that they did in Zion. I will do this in a way that you people of Israel will see it happen. That is what I, Yahweh, declare.”

{To the people of Babylon, Yahweh would say,} “Listen, you people of Babylon! I am against you. You have ruined nation after nation all over the earth. I will use my power to strike you; I will topple you down from the heights where you stand, and I will leave you as nothing but a heap of burned rubble.

No one will ever again take stones from your ruins to set in the corner of a building or to lay as the foundation of a house, because your city will lie empty forever. That is what I, Yahweh, declare.”

Raise a signal flag in the land! Blow a ram’s horn among the nations to call them to war! Set the nations apart to fight against Babylon! Summon the kingdoms of Ararat, Minni, and Ashkenaz to attack it! Appoint an officer to lead the army against it! Bring up so many horses that they look like a swarm of locusts!
Set the nations apart to fight against Babylon: the kings of Media, their governors and all their officials, and every land that they rule.

The ground will shake violently, because Yahweh will certainly do to the city of Babylon everything that he has planned. He will make the land of Babylon completely desolate, so that no one lives there at all.

The warriors of Babylon will stop fighting; they will stay inside their fortresses. They will lose all their strength and become helpless and terrified. Their enemies will set the buildings of the city on fire and will break down the bars that hold its gates shut.
One messenger will run to meet another messenger, and one man carrying a report will run to meet another, in order to tell the king of Babylon that enemies have captured every part of his city,
that they have seized the places where people cross the river, that they have burned the marshes with fire, and that his soldiers are in a panic.

Yahweh, the commander of the heavenly armies, the God whom the Israelites worship, says this: “Enemies will trample the people of the city of Babylon, just as oxen trample grain on a threshing floor. Very soon the time will come for me to cut them down, as farmers cut down grain at harvest time.”

The people of Jerusalem say, “Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon has devoured us and left us confused; he has taken everything we owned, so that we are as empty as a jar that no one has filled. He swallowed us as greedily as a huge sea creature swallows its prey; he took all our finest possessions to satisfy himself, and then he washed us away like garbage.”

The people who live in Zion will say, “May the people of Babylon suffer for the violence that they did to us and to our relatives!” The people of Jerusalem will say, “May the people who live in the land of the Chaldeans pay for murdering us!”

So Yahweh says this to the people of Jerusalem: “Listen! I myself will argue your case for you, and I will pay your enemies back for what they did to you. I will dry up the river that flows through Babylon and cause its springs to stop flowing.
The city of Babylon will become piles of rubble, a place where jackals make their dens. Everyone who sees it will shudder in horror and will hiss to show their scorn, and no one will live there.
All the people of Babylon act fiercely together, roaring and snarling like young lions.

While they are drinking and growing reckless, I will set out a banquet for them; I will make them so drunk that they shout with glee, and then they will fall asleep and die; they will never wake up again. That is what I, Yahweh, declare.
I will bring them down to slaughter them, as easily as someone leads lambs and rams and male goats to the place where a butcher kills them.”
Enemies have captured the city of Babylon! They have seized the city that everyone on the earth used to praise! Everyone in the nations who sees what has happened to Babylon shudders in horror!
Enemy armies have swept over the city of Babylon and have completely overwhelmed it, just as the roaring waves of the sea cover the land.
The cities of Babylonia have become ruins, a dry and empty wilderness. No one lives in that land, and no one even travels through those cities.

Yahweh says, “I will punish Bel, the god whom the people of Babylon worship, and I will force him to give back everything that he swallowed. People from other nations will no longer crowd together to worship him. The wall around the city of Babylon will fall down.
My people, get out of that city! Each of you must escape and save your own life, because I, Yahweh, am extremely angry with the people there!

Do not lose your courage, and do not be afraid when you hear people reporting what is happening in that land. People will bring one report this year and another report the next year, reports that people are attacking one another violently in the land and that one ruler is fighting against another ruler.

So listen! The time is coming soon when I will punish the people of Babylon for the idols that they carved. Everyone in their land will feel ashamed, and enemies will kill its people, whose bodies will lie in the middle of the city.

Then everyone in heaven and everyone on the earth will shout joyfully because of what has happened to the city of Babylon, because the armies that will destroy it will come from the north. That is what I, Yahweh, declare.”
The people of Babylon must die because they killed the people of Israel, just as they killed people in nations everywhere.

You Israelites whom enemies did not kill in the war, leave that city and go! Do not wait any longer! Even though you are far away from your own land, keep remembering Yahweh and worshiping him, and keep thinking about the city of Jerusalem.

The Israelites say, “We feel ashamed, because we have heard people insult us; we cannot lift up our faces, because we feel so much shame, since foreigners entered the holy places in the temple of Yahweh and defiled them.”
Yahweh replies, “So listen! The time is coming when I will punish the people of Babylon for the idols that they carved, and all through their land the people whom enemies wound will groan in pain.
Even if the people of Babylon could build their city as high as the sky and make its defenses impossible to reach, I would still send armies to destroy it. That is what I, Yahweh, declare.”
Listen! People in the city of Babylon are crying out! Enemies are destroying everything in the land of the Chaldeans!
Yahweh is ruining the city of Babylon and silencing the loud noise of its crowds. The enemies advance with a roar like floodwaters; they shout so loudly that everyone can hear them.

An army has come to destroy the city of Babylon. Enemies have captured its strongest soldiers and have broken their bows to pieces. Yahweh is a God who pays people back for what they have done; he will certainly give the Babylonians what they deserve.

Yahweh says, “I will make the officials and the wise men of Babylon drunk, along with its governors, its other officials, and its warriors, and they will fall asleep and die; they will never wake up again . That is what I, the King, declare; my name is Yahweh, the commander of the heavenly armies.”

Yahweh, the commander of the heavenly armies, says this: “Enemies will completely tear down the thick wall around the city of Babylon, and they will burn its high gates. The peoples who built that city worked hard for nothing; fire will consume everything that the nations made, and all their work will only exhaust them.”

Jeremiah the prophet gave this message to Seraiah son of Neriah, son of Mahseiah, when Seraiah went to Babylon with Zedekiah the king of Judah. This happened in the fourth year that Zedekiah ruled Judah. Seraiah was the official who arranged where the king would stay each night.
Jeremiah had written on one scroll all the disasters that would come on Babylon; he wrote down all these words about Babylon.
Jeremiah said to Seraiah, “When you arrive in Babylon, read all these words aloud so that the people there hear them,
and then say, ‘Yahweh, you yourself said that you would destroy this place, so that nothing would live here anymore, neither people nor animals; you said that it would lie empty forever.’
When you have finished reading this scroll, tie a stone to it and throw it into the middle of the Euphrates River.

Then say, ‘Babylon will sink like this and will never rise again, because of the disaster that Yahweh will bring on it, and its people will collapse from exhaustion.’” That is the end of the messages that Jeremiah gave.

Zedekiah was 21 years old when he became king, and he ruled in Jerusalem for eleven years. His mother’s name was Hamutal. She was the daughter of a man whose name was Jeremiah. She was from the city of Libnah.
Zedekiah did many things that Yahweh considered to be evil, just as {his older brother} Jehoiakim had done.

Yahweh made these things happen to the people who lived in Jerusalem and other parts of Judah because he was very angry with them. He finally allowed the Babylonians to force them to leave their country. That happened when Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.

{Because Zedekiah had rebelled,} King Nebuchadnezzar led his whole army to attack Jerusalem. They arrived there after Zedekiah had been ruling for nine years, on the tenth day of the tenth month of that year. They surrounded the city and built earthen ramps against its walls to help them attack it.
The Babylonians kept attacking the city {for the next two years,} until Zedekiah had been ruling for eleven years.
By the ninth day of the fourth month of that year, the famine in the city had become very severe. There was no more food for the people to eat.

Then the Babylonian soldiers broke through the city wall and entered the city. {King Zedekiah and} the Judean soldiers tried to escape at night {when the Babylonians would not see them}. They used the gate near the king’s garden to go through the inner and outer walls of the city. Zedekiah {and the soldiers} tried to escape through the Jordan River valley. But the Babylonians had surrounded the city{, and some of their soldiers saw where they went}.
So Babylonian soldiers chased after them. They caught up to King Zedekiah in the plains around Jericho. His soldiers ran away {instead of fighting to defend him}.

So the Babylonian soldiers were able to capture King Zedekiah. They brought him to Nebuchadnezzar, who was in the city of Riblah in the region of Hamath. Nebuchadnezzar declared that Zedekiah was guilty of rebelling against him.
There at Riblah, King Nebuchadnezzar forced Zedekiah to watch as his soldiers killed all of his sons. They also killed many Judean leaders whom they had captured.
Then the soldiers gouged out Zedekiah’s eyes and put bronze chains on his hands and feet. King Nebuchanezzar brought him ]to the city of Babylon and put him in prison for the rest of his life.

On the seventh day of the fifth month of that year, after Nebuchadnezzar had been ruling for nineteen years, Nebuzaradan arrived in Jerusalem. He was one of King Nebuchadnezzar’s most important officials. He commanded the royal bodyguards.
He ordered his soldiers to burn down Yahweh’s temple, the king’s palace, and all the important buildings in Jerusalem.
Then the Babylonian soldiers who had come to Jerusalem with Nebuzaradan tore down the walls all around Jerusalem.

After that, Nebuzaradan and his soldiers took to Babylon some poor people and the people who were still alive in Jerusalem. They also took other people who lived in the region of Judah. Some Judeans had previously surrendered to the Babylonian army, and they took them away too.
But Nebuzaradan allowed some of the very poor people to stay in Judah to take care of the vineyards and to plant crops in the fields.

The Babylonian soldiers broke into pieces the bronze pillars, the carts, and the giant bronze water basin that people called the sea. Those things had been in the temple courtyard. They took the bronze to Babylon.
They also took the pots, shovels, wick snuffers, bowls, incense dishes, and other bronze items that the priests used for their work in the temple.

The soldiers also took away from the temple all the items that were pure gold or pure silver. These included the basins, the pans for carrying hot coals, the bowls, the pots, the lampstands, the incense dishes, and the cups.

There was too much bronze for the Babylonians to weigh in the items that King Solomon had commanded his workers to make for Yahweh’s temple. Those items included the two pillars, the giant water basin that people called the sea, the twelve bronze oxen under it, and the carts.
Each pillar was eight and one quarter meters tall and five and one half meters around. They were hollow, and their sides were nearly eight centimeters thick.

The bronze decorative top of each pillar was two and one quarter meters tall. Bronze strands in the shape of nets and bronze ornaments in the shape of pomegranates surrounded the pillar tops. Each pillar had the same decorations.
There were 24 pomegranates on each side of each pillar, for a total of 96. {There was also a pomegranate on each corner, so} there was a total of 100 pomegranates on each net.
Nebuzaradan took some prisoners. These included the high priest Seraiah, Zephaniah, who was another leading priest, and the three Levites who had supervised the temple courtyard entrance.

The prisoners also included the royal official responsible for the army, seven of the king’s advisors who had not fled, the commander who recorded the names of Judean men as they came to serve as soldiers, and 60 men who were serving as soldiers and were still in the city.
Nebuzaradan took them all as prisoners to the king of Babylon at the city of Riblah.

There at the city of Riblah in the province of Hamath, the king of Babylon had his soldiers kill all of the prisoners. That is what happened when the Babylonians forcefully took the people of Judah away from their land.
This is how many people Nebuchadnezzar had his soldiers take away to Babylon. When he had been ruling for almost seven years, they took away 3,023 people from Judah.
When he had been ruling for almost 18 years, his soldiers took away 832 more people from Jerusalem.
When Nebuchadnezzar had been ruling for almost 23 years, Nebuzaradan, the commander of his royal bodyguards, took away 745 more people from Judah. In total, the Babylonians took away 4,600 people.

Later, when King Jehoiachin of Judah had been a prisoner in Babylon for 37 years, Nebuchadnezzar’s son Evil Merodach became the king of Babylon. During his first year as king, on the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month, he treated Jehoiachin favorably. He released him from prison.
He reassured Jehoiachin that he would treat him well, and he gave him a position of greater honor than the other kings whom the Babylonians had {conquered and} brought to their royal court.
He gave Jehoiachin new clothes to replace the clothes that he had been wearing in prison, and he allowed Jehoiachin to eat meals with him every day for the rest of his life.
The king of Babylon also gave Jehoiachin money to buy the things he needed. He gave him a regular amount that was sufficient for his needs. The king continued to do that until Jehoiachin died.

Jerusalem, the city that was once so full of people, is now empty and deserted. It was once the greatest city among all the nations, but now it is like a widow—alone and without protection. It was once honored among the provinces like a princess, but now her people are forced to do slave labor.

Jerusalem’s inhabitants weep and cry bitterly all through the night; tears run down their cheeks. None of the nations that loved them have come to comfort them. All their allies have turned against them; they have all become their enemies.

Enemies drove the people of Judah out to other countries, and made them suffer greatly as slaves. They live among foreign nations, where they find no peace or rest. Their enemies caught up with them; they were trapped and could not escape.

No one comes to Zion anymore for the sacred festivals, so the roads to the city are silent and empty. The city gates stand deserted; the priests groan in sorrow. The young women of the city are grieving, and the whole city is filled with bitterness.

Jerusalem’s enemies have become rulers over it; its adversaries are doing well. Yahweh has caused it to suffer greatly, because of all the ways its people sinned against him. Its children have been taken captive and marched away before the enemy.

All the glory and beauty that Zion once had has left it completely. Its leaders are like deer that are starving because they cannot find any grass to eat. They stumble along weakly with the enemy chasing them.

Now as Jerusalem suffers in exile and misery, its people remember all the good things that they had in former times. When the enemy conquered the people, no one came to help them. Some enemies watched and laughed contemptuously as others destroyed the city.

Jerusalem’s people sinned so greatly that the city became something everyone treated as filthy and defiling. All those who had honored it now despise it, because they have seen how shamefully disgraced it has become. Now its people moan and humbly hide.

Everyone can see that the people in Jerusalem have made themselves impure by sinning, but its people never thought about what would happen to them as a result. The enemy devastated Jerusalem in a terrible way; no one has come to comfort its people. They cried out, “Yahweh, see how we are suffering! The enemy has triumphed over us!”
The enemy took possession of all its precious treasures. Its people watched as foreign nations entered the temple— the nations that you, Yahweh, had commanded to stay out of your holy place.

All the people groan and search for food. They have traded their precious things just to get something to eat so that they can stay alive. They cried out, “Yahweh, look at us! See how people treat us contemptuously!”

Jerusalem’s people cried out to those passing by the ruined city, “Do you not care at all about what has happened to us? Look around you and see— has anyone ever suffered as much as we have suffered? Yahweh inflicted this terrible pain on us on the day when he was fiercely angry.
He sent fire down from above that burned deep inside us. He set a trap that caught our feet and forced us to turn back. He left us devastated and abandoned, exhausted and miserable all day long.

God tied our sins around our necks like a heavy yoke; they are twisted tightly together so that we cannot remove them. They are piled onto our necks and weigh us down, so that we have no strength left. The Lord handed us over to enemies we have no power to defeat.

The Lord has despised and rejected all our warriors. He called our enemies together at the right time to destroy our young men. The Lord has crushed the people of Judah like someone treading on grapes in a winepress.

These are the things we weep over, weeping without stopping; our eyes overflow with tears. There is no one near us to comfort us or to restore our strength. Our children have been left with nothing, because the enemy has overcome us.”

Zion’s people reach out their hands, pleading for help, but no one comes to comfort them. Yahweh ordered that all the nations surrounding Jacob would become his enemies. Jerusalem has become something all the neighboring nations treat as defiling and avoid.

Jerusalem’s people said, “Yahweh is righteous, because we disobeyed his commands. Listen, all you peoples of the world, and see what great pain we are in. Our young women and young men have been taken away as captives.
We called to our allies for help, but they completely betrayed us. Our priests and our elders died in the city, while they were desperately searching for food just to stay alive.

Yahweh, look at how much we are suffering! Our stomachs churn with anguish; our hearts are completely devastated within us, because we have deeply and truly rebelled against you. In the streets, the sword kills people; inside the city, people are dying like a plague.

People have heard us groaning in misery, but no one has come to comfort us. All our enemies have heard about the disaster that came upon us; they are glad about it, because you are the one who brought it. Bring the day of punishment that you promised, when they will suffer as we have suffered!

Let all the evil things they have done come to your attention, and punish them for what they have done. Treat them the way you treated us for all the ways we sinned against you. We are constantly sighing and groaning, and we grieve greatly.”

The Lord was very angry with the people of Jerusalem, so he brought darkness and judgment on them. Jerusalem used to be a beautiful and glorious city, but he humiliated it and brought it down to nothing. When the day came for him to punish Israel, he did not even spare his own temple.

The Lord completely destroyed all the homes of Jacob’s descendants and was not merciful to them. Because he was furious, he tore the fortresses of the people of Judah down to the ground. He disgraced their kingdom and its rulers.

Because he was extremely angry, he took away all of Israel’s power. He refused to protect his people when their enemies attacked them. He destroyed everything among Jacob’s descendants like a raging fire that burns up everything around it.

He got ready to shoot his bow at us, his own people, as though we were his enemies. He used his power to kill everyone we loved most among the people of Jerusalem. He was extremely angry with us; his anger burned like a fire.

The Lord started treating us like an enemy; he destroyed Israel. He destroyed all of Jerusalem’s palaces and turned its fortresses into ruins. He caused the people of Judah to grieve and weep even more.

He wrecked his own temple as easily as someone tears down a garden hut; he destroyed the place where people gathered to worship him. Yahweh caused the people of Zion to stop celebrating their sacred festivals and Sabbath days. Because he was so furiously angry, he rejected both the king and the priest.

The Lord turned away from his own altar; he abandoned his own holy place. He let the enemies have power over the walls of Jerusalem’s palaces. Those enemies shouted triumphantly inside Yahweh’s temple, as if they were celebrating one of the sacred festivals.

Yahweh planned to destroy the wall of Jerusalem. He carefully measured it out for destruction and then he did not stop himself from devouring it. He made the outer wall and the inner wall fall into ruin; together they crumbled.

Jerusalem’s gates have sunk into the ground; Yahweh smashed the bars that held them shut. The enemy has taken the king and the officials away to foreign nations; no one teaches them God’s instruction anymore. The prophets also no longer receive any messages from Yahweh.

The old men of Jerusalem sit on the ground and say nothing. They have thrown dust on their heads and put on rough sackcloth {to show how deeply they grieve}. The young women of Jerusalem bow their faces all the way down to the ground.

I have cried until my eyes can produce no more tears; my stomach is churning with anguish. I feel as if my insides are spilling out on the ground, because so many of my people have died. Even children and babies are fainting in the city streets because they have nothing to eat.
The children cry out to their mothers, “We need food and drink!” They collapse in the city streets like fatally wounded soldiers, and they die slowly in the arms of their mothers.

People of Jerusalem, there is nothing I can say to help you. Nothing that has ever happened to anyone else compares to what has happened to you people who live on mount Zion; I do not know how to comfort you. The disaster that struck you is as vast as the sea; no one can restore you.

The prophets among you claimed to hear messages from Yahweh, but what they said was false and worthless. They did not rebuke you when you sinned so that you could have changed your ways and avoided disaster. Instead, the messages they told you were lies that caused you to do wrong things.

Everyone who passes by on the road claps their hands to mock you. They hiss with contempt and shake their heads at Jerusalem: “Can this really be the city that people used to say was the perfectly beautiful city, the city that made all the earth rejoice?”

All your enemies open their mouths wide against you to mock you. They hiss with contempt and grind their teeth with hatred; they say, “We have devoured her! This is the very day we waited for; we have lived to see it!”

Yahweh has done what he planned to do; he has carried out the threat that he announced long ago. He has torn the city down and shown no mercy; he has let your enemies celebrate over you, and he has made those who attack you more powerful than ever.

The people of Jerusalem cried out to the Lord from deep within themselves. People of Jerusalem, let your tears flow like a river all day and all night! Do not stop weeping; do not let your eyes rest from crying.

Get up and cry out during the night, right when the night watches begin! Tell the Lord everything that is in your heart, holding nothing back, like water pouring out. Raise your hands and pray to him for your children to survive, because they are fainting from hunger on every street corner.

Yahweh, look at what you have done and pay attention! Think about whom you have treated this way! Women should never have to eat their own children, the babies they lovingly cared for! No one should kill priests and prophets inside your own holy place!
People of every age lie dead on the ground in the streets. The enemy has killed all our youth. On the day you were angry, you {let the enemy} kill them; you let them slaughter them mercilessly.

You called enemies to attack me from every direction, as if you were summoning guests to come to a feast. On the day Yahweh was angry, no one escaped and no one survived. The children I carried and raised, my enemy has destroyed them all.
I am a man who has suffered greatly because God punished me when he was very angry.
He sent me into a place where I only suffer and nothing good happens to me.
He keeps acting against me again and again, all day long.
He afflicted my body and broke my bones.
He attacked me on every side and caused me to suffer terribly.
He made me feel hopeless, like no one remembers me.
He has completely trapped me so that I cannot escape.
Even though I beg him to help me, he refuses to listen when I pray.
He has blocked every way forward for me so that I cannot make any progress in my life.
He waited to attack me like a bear hiding to ambush its prey, like a lion crouching in a hidden place.
He ruined my plans and destroyed me; he made me poor.
He deliberately chose to attack me and made me the one he would harm.
He deliberately caused me intense suffering.
All my own people mock me constantly with their songs.
He has caused me to suffer so much that I cannot bear it.
He completely humiliated me and degraded me.
God took away all my peace; I no longer remember what happiness feels like.
So I said to myself, “I cannot endure any longer, and I have no more reason to hope in Yahweh.”
Yahweh, remember how I have suffered and wandered; I have suffered so very greatly.
I keep thinking about it over and over, and it makes me deeply depressed.
Yet when I think about this one thing, I find reason to hope:
Yahweh never stops faithfully loving us, and he never stops showing us mercy.
Every morning he shows us mercy again; he is always faithful to us.
I said to myself, “Yahweh is all that I need; so I will confidently wait for him.”
Yahweh is good to everyone who depends on him, to everyone who hopes that Yahweh will help him.
It is good to wait quietly for Yahweh to save us.
It is good for a person to endure suffering patiently while still young.
A person should accept his situation quietly and not complain when God causes him to suffer.
He should bow down with his face to the ground, because there may still be reason to hope.
He should offer his cheek to the one who hits him and accept all the insults people give him.
The Lord does not reject people forever.
Even though he causes people to grieve, he will show them mercy because he always faithfully loves them.
He does not enjoy causing people to suffer or making them grieve.
When people crush all the prisoners in a land under their feet,
when they cheat someone and deny him what he deserves right in front of the Most High God,
when they treat someone unfairly in his legal dispute—the Lord does not approve of any of these things.
No one can simply speak and make something happen unless the Lord has commanded it.
The Most High God is the one who decides both the bad things and the good things that happen.
No living person should complain when God punishes him for his sins.
Instead, we should carefully examine how we have been living, and we should turn back to Yahweh.
We should sincerely pray, raising our hands to God in heaven:
“We have sinned and rebelled against you, and you have not forgiven us.
Because you were angry, you chased after us; you killed us without showing us any mercy.
You made yourself unreachable so that you did not hear any of our prayers.
You have made the other nations treat us as though we are nothing but garbage and filth.
All our enemies have spoken hateful things against us.
We have experienced nothing but fear and danger, ruin and destruction.”
Many tears flow from my eyes because enemies have destroyed my people.
My tears pour out and will not stop; they will not end
until Yahweh looks down and sees us from heaven.
What I see makes me grieve deeply because of what has happened to all the women of my city.
My enemies relentlessly pursued me without any reason, even though I had done nothing wrong.
They threw me into a pit to kill me and dropped stones on top of me.
Water rose over my head, and I said to myself, “I am going to die!”
I called out to you, Yahweh, from the deepest part of that pit.
You heard me; do not ignore me when I cry out to you for help!
You came near when I called to you and said, “Do not be afraid!”
Lord, you defended me; you saved my life.
Yahweh, you have seen how my enemies have wronged me; make things right for me!
You have seen how they want to take revenge on me and all the things they have planned to do to me.
Yahweh, you have heard them insult me and all the things they have planned to do to me.
Those who oppose me whisper and mutter things about me all day long.
Look at them! No matter what they are doing, they make fun of me in their songs.
Yahweh, pay them back for what they have done!
Make them stubborn, and let your curse fall on them.
Because you are angry with them, chase them and destroy them so they no longer exist anywhere on earth.
How terrible that the people of Jerusalem, who used to be so valuable, have now become completely worthless! The enemy has thrown out the precious young men at every street corner.
People once considered the young men of Zion to be extremely valuable, but now everyone treats them as completely worthless, like ordinary clay pots that a potter makes.
Even jackals nurse their young, but the women among my people have neglected their own children and have stopped caring for them.
The babies are so thirsty that their tongues stick to the roofs of their mouths. The children beg for food, but no one gives them any.
People who used to eat the finest food now starve in the streets. People whose parents raised them wearing expensive clothes now search through garbage heaps for something to eat.
God has punished my people more severely than he punished the people of Sodom. He destroyed Sodom in an instant, and nobody cried for it.
Jerusalem’s most honored people used to look very pure and healthy. They had strong, attractive bodies and appeared very vigorous.
But now they look so dark and thin that no one recognizes them in the streets. Their skin has shriveled tightly over their bones and has dried out completely.
Those who died quickly in battle were better off than those who died slowly from starvation, because the starving people wasted away gradually since no food grew in the fields.
Women who were normally very compassionate cooked their own children. They ate them as food when the enemy destroyed Jerusalem.
Yahweh expressed all of his anger against Jerusalem. He burned the city with fire and destroyed it down to its very foundations.
No king anywhere on the earth, and no one else in the whole world, believed that an enemy could ever enter the city of Jerusalem.
But it happened because Jerusalem’s prophets sinned and her priests did evil things. They killed innocent people right there in the city.
