“Yet, your beauty made you self-assured. You used your international renown to act like a prostitute. You freely offered illicit sexual favors to every man you came across, and they enjoyed your beautiful body.
You used some of your beautiful clothing to make yourself gaudy, decorated shrines. On them, you behaved like a prostitute. Yes, you had illicit sex with men, and they enjoyed your beautiful body.
You also used the beautiful gold and silver jewelry that I had given you to fashion ritual statues with male anatomy, and you had illicit sexual relations with them.
You took your embroidered clothes and clothed your ritual statues with them, and you placed my oil and my incense as votive offerings in their presence.

You also took the food that I gave you— the fine flour, olive oil, and honey that I fed you—and you presented it in the presence of those ritual statues as pleasingly aromatic votive offerings. That is exactly what happened.” That is what the Lord Yahweh declares.
“You even took your sons and your daughters, the children that you had borne to me, and you sacrificed them as food to those idols. Was your prostitution such a small matter to you,
that you also butchered my children and burned them alive as offerings to those ritual statues?

All the while, when you were committing these disgusting, heinous actions and prostituting yourself, you never once remembered your birth story, when you were completely naked, floundering in your own blood!
How terrible it will be for you!” That is what the Lord Yahweh declares! “So, after you did all those heinous acts,
you constructed a domed building for yourself and erected lofty shrines in every public square.

At every street intersection, you constructed your lofty shrine. So you made your once-beautiful body abominable, offering yourself to every man you came across. So, more and more, you behaved like a prostitute.
Then you even had illicit sex with the Egyptians, your well-endowed neighbors, and so you acted more and more like a prostitute, never ceasing to anger and grieve me.
So I acted powerfully against you and reduced your apportioned rations. So I let the Philistine people do what they wanted with you. They despised you, and yet your obscene behavior embarrassed them!
You also had illicit sexual relations with the Assyrian people because you were insatiable. You behaved like a prostitute with them, and yet even then you could not satisfy your desires!
So, you behaved more and more like a prostitute, reaching all the way to the territories of the Babylonian Empire! Yet even that did not satisfy your desires!
How weak-willed you are! You love the wrong things!” That is what the Lord Yahweh declares. “You did all these things, acting like an impudent prostitute who does whatever she wants.

When you constructed your domed brothel at every street intersection and erected your lofty shrines in every public square, you were not even like an ordinary prostitute, because you refused to accept payment.
You are an unfaithful wife, who prefers strangers to her own husband!
Prostitutes usually receive gifts from men, but you gave your gifts to all your lovers; you bribed them to come to you from all around to have illicit sexual relations with you!

So as you behaved like a prostitute, you were the opposite of other women. No man solicited you; instead, you paid them, and they did not pay you. In this way, you were the exact opposite of a normal prostitute!”
So then, you prostitute, heed Yahweh’s message!

This is what the Lord Yahweh says, “You lustfully offered yourself and exposed your naked body in your illicit sexual relations with your lovers. Furthermore, you crafted your disgusting and indecent ritual statues, and you offered those idols the blood of your own children!

Because of this, I am summoning all your lovers, the ones you found so attractive—everyone you loved, along with everyone you hated. I will assemble them against you from all around, and I will strip you naked in front of them so that they will see you completely naked.
I will execute against you the legal sentence reserved for women who commit adultery and women who murder. I will sentence you to an angry and impassioned, bloody death.

I will let your enemies dominate you: They will demolish your brothels and smash your lofty places. They will strip off your clothes and take your beautiful jewelry, and they will leave you completely naked.
They will bring a mob against you. Then, they will stone you to death and cut your body into pieces with their swords.
They will burn down your houses and execute their judgments against you while many women watch. I will put an end to your prostituting behavior, and you will no longer pay your lovers.
Then I will vent my fury against you, and my jealous passion will leave you alone. I will calm myself down and cease being angry.

Because you did not remember your birth story, but instead you infuriated me with all these deeds, I hereby declare that I will hold you accountable for your behavior. That is what I, the Lord Yahweh, declare! You have added this obscene behavior to all your other disgusting and indecent practices!
Now, pay attention! Everyone who quotes proverbs will quote this proverb about you: ‘The daughter is just like her mother.’

You are truly your mother’s daughter. She abhorred her husband and her children. You are also just like your sisters. They abhorred their husbands and their children. After all, your mother was ethnically Hittite, and your father was ethnically Amorite!

Now, your older sister is named Samaria. She resides with her daughters to the north of you, citizens of Jerusalem. Your younger sister is named Sodom. She resides with her daughters to the south of you.

You did not merely practice their lifestyles or do the disgusting things they did. Instead, in a surprisingly short while, in all your habits and practices, you became even more corrupt than they ever were!”
This is what the Lord Yahweh declares: “I swear by myself that your sister Sodom and her daughters never did what you, Jerusalem, and your daughters have done.
Take note! This is how corrupt your sister Sodom was: She and her daughters were arrogant; they had plenty of food and lived comfortably at ease, but they never helped those who were poor or needy.
They were arrogant and did disgusting and illicit things in my presence. So, when I saw what they were doing, I forcibly removed them from my presence.

As for Samaria, she did not commit even half the sins that you committed. You have done so many more disgusting and illicit things than either Samaria or Sodom did, so that your abominable acts have made your sisters appear righteous!

So now you must feel the emotional disgrace of having interceded for your sisters. Your sins, which were far more disgusting and illicit than theirs, have made your sisters appear more righteous than you! So you also must be ashamed and feel the disgrace of having made your sisters, Sodom and Samaria, appear righteous.
Nevertheless, I will restore the well-being of your sisters—that of Sodom and her daughters, and of Samaria and her daughters—and I will restore your well-bring along with theirs,
so that you will feel humiliated and ashamed of all that you did when your disgusting behavior consoled your sisters.
I will restore all of you—your sisters, Sodom and her daughters, Samaria and her daughters, and you and your daughters as well—to the kind of life you enjoyed before you suffered my punishments.
When you were arrogant, you would not even mention your sister Sodom.

But that was before I exposed your own corrupt and depraved behavior. Now, you are just like your sister Sodom! The people of Aram and all her neighbors, and the Philistines all around you, mock you and despise you!
You yourself have suffered the consequences of your obscene behavior and your disgusting, illicit practices.” That is what Yahweh declares.
So, this is what the Lord Yahweh says, “When you abrogated the covenant you made with me, you showed no respect for your solemn promises. I will deal with you as these actions deserve.
Yet I myself will uphold and fulfill the solemn promise that I made with you when you were young. Yes, I will make a promise with you that will never end.

Then you will recall what you once did and feel humiliating shame when you reconcile with your sisters, both those older than you and those younger than you. I will present them to you as your daughters, but not because of my covenant with you.
So I myself will make my solemn promise with you. When this happens, you will finally understand exactly who I am and what I am like—I am Yahweh!

I will do this so that you will recognize all that you have done and feel ashamed. When I forgive you for all that you have done and restore our relationship, your disgrace will cause you to never again open your mouth to speak.” This is what the Lord Yahweh declares!’”
Yahweh gave me another message. He said,
“Human, tell this ambiguous story to the Israelite people.
Tell them, ‘This is what the Lord Yahweh says, “There once was a huge eagle with powerful wings and long feathers of many colors. It flew to Lebanon and grasped the top of a cedar tree.
It broke off the topmost of its young branches and carried it away to the Canaanite territories. The eagle set it down in a city of vendors.
Then it took some of the seed of that land and planted it in a fertile field, in a slip beside abundant water. He planted it there like one plants a willow tree.
That seed sprouted and became a low, spreading vine. Its tendrils grew toward the eagle, and its roots extended down beneath it. So it became a vine that produced woody branches and put out canes.

There was another huge eagle with powerful wings and many feathers. Now, the spreading vine bent its roots toward this second eagle. From the garden bed where it grew, the vine stretched out its tendrils toward the eagle, hoping that it would give the vine more water.
The first eagle had planted the vine-plant in a fertile field that ran along flowing water so that it could grow woody canes and produce fruit and become a splendid vine.”’

Then say, ‘This is what the Lord Yahweh says, “This vine will clearly not flourish! Someone will rip up its roots and strip off its fruit, so that it wilts and dies. All its fresh new leaves will wilt and die. (And it will not take a strong arm or many people to pull it up by its roots!)

Now, consider this: Even though the eagle planted it, it will clearly not flourish! When the hot east wind blows on it, it will entirely wither and die. Yes, it will wither away, right in the garden bed where it once grew.”’”
Then Yahweh gave me this message:

“Ask those Israelite people who continually revolt against me, ‘You do not understand what this ambiguous story means, do you?’ Tell them, ‘Remember: The Babylonian king Nebuchadnezzar came to Jerusalem, captured the Judahite king Jehoiachin and his public officials, and brought them back to himself in Babylon.

Then he took one of the royal family—Jehoiachin’s uncle, Zedekiah—and made a royal treaty with him, coercing him to swear a solemn oath. He also forcibly removed the most powerful local rulers of Jerusalem,
so that the Judahite kingdom would remain weak and unable to revolt against him. Instead, it could survive only by honoring its treaty with the Babylonian king, Nebuchadnezzar.

However, the man whom the Babylonian king set up, Zedekiah, revolted against Nebuchadnezzar and the Babylonian Empire. Zedekiah dispatched his messengers to Egypt, to Pharoah Hophra, so that the Egyptian Empire would equip him with horses and many soldiers. Clearly, Zedekiah will not flourish! He who does such things will certainly not survive! Zedekiah disregarded the treaty he made with the Babylonian king Nebuchadnezzar, so he will clearly not survive!
I swear by myself that Zedekiah will die in Babylon, in the city of the king who made him king, whose oath he disregarded and whose treaty he violated. This is what I, the Lord Yahweh, declare!
Hophra, the king of Egypt, will not employ his massive army to fight alongside Zedekiah in the battle when the Babylonian Empire constructs a siege ramp and erects siege walls to kill many people.

Zedekiah, the so-called king of Judah, showed no respect for his oath to Nebuchadnezzar and broke the treaty he had made. Make note: He made a solemn promise, yet he did all these things. So, he will clearly not survive!

So, this is what the Lord Yahweh says: “I swear by myself that the oath to Nebuchadnezzar that Zedekiah disregarded, he swore in my name! And the covenant he violated was with me! I will repay him for these actions!

I will ensnare Zedekiah and capture him, like an animal that a hunter traps with a net. I will forcibly bring him to Babylon, and there I will legally arraign him for disloyally betraying his promises to me.

With their swords, Babylonian soldiers will murder every one of Zedekiah’s soldiers who flees in the battle, and those who survive will disperse in every direction. When all this happens, you will recognize that I, Yahweh, have spoken!”

This is what the Lord Yahweh says: “I myself will remove a shoot from the top of a tall cedar tree, and I will plant it. I will break off a newly grown, green twig from the topmost of its young shoots, and I myself will plant it on a towering mountain.

I will plant that newly grown green twig on the highest mountain of Israel, where it will grow woody branches and bear fruit and become a magnificent, wide cedar tree. Birds of every kind will nest under it; every kind of winged animal will live in the shade of its branches.

Then every tree in the field will finally understand exactly who I am and what I am like—I am Yahweh! I fell tall trees and cause small trees to grow tall; I dry up green trees and make dry trees flourish. I {am} Yahweh—I have spoken, and I will certainly do it!”’”
Then Yahweh gave me another message. He said,
“What do you people mean when you quote this proverb about the land of Israel? You say, ‘The parents ate sour grapes, but it was their children who got the sour taste in their mouths.’
I swear by myself that you, Israelite people, will no longer quote that proverb in Israel. That is what I, the Lord Yahweh, declare!
Pay attention! All lives are mine—parents and their children alike. It is the person who sins who will die.
Suppose there is a virtuous person who does what is just and honest.

He does not eat meat that people have sacrificed to ritual statues at the shrines on Israel’s hilltops, nor does he pray to the idols that the Israelite people worship. He does not defile another man’s wife, nor does he have sexual relations with a woman during her monthly period of menstruation.

He does not extort anyone. When he borrows money from someone and the person gives him something as collateral for repayment, he gives that item back to the lender. He does not steal from anyone. Instead, he gives his food to hungry people and gives his clothing to people who have no clothes.
When he lends someone money, he does not charge interest or engage in usury. He refuses to do what is immoral or corrupt. Instead, he judges honestly between one person and another.

He carefully acts according to my regulations and lives faithfully by heeding my norms. In this case, people should consider this person righteous. He will surely continue to live! That is what I, the Lord Yahweh, declare.
But suppose that such a virtuous man has a violent son, who murders people. Then that son does any of these evil things to other people—
all the things that his father never did: He eats meat that people have sacrificed to ritual statues at the shrines on Israel’s hilltops; he defiles another man’s wife.

He extorts people who are poor and helpless. He steals from people, and, when he borrows money from someone and the person gives him something as collateral for repayment, he refuses to return that item to the lender. He prays to the idols that the Israelite people worship and commits other disgusting and illicit things.

When he lends someone money, he charges interest and engages in usury. Such a person will surely not go on living! Because he has done all these disgusting and illicit things, people must execute him and hold him responsible for his own death.
But pay attention! Suppose that such a violent man has a son who witnesses all the sins that his father commits, considers them, but does not do such things.

He does not eat meat that people have sacrificed to ritual statues at the shrines on Israel’s hilltops, nor does he pray to the idols that the Israelite people worship. He does not defile another man’s wife;

He does not extort anyone. When he borrows money from someone and the person gives him something as collateral for repayment, he gives that item back to the lender. He does not steal from anyone. Instead, he gives his food to hungry people and gives his clothing to people who have no clothes.

He refuses to do what is immoral or corrupt. When he lends someone money, he does not charge interest or engage in usury. He lives in a way that heeds my norms and carefully acts according to my regulations. In this case, such a person will not die because of his father’s sins; he will surely go on living!
But as for his father, pay attention! He will die because of his own depraved behavior. After all, he extorted people, stole from his relatives, and generally did what is wrong among his people.

But you retort, ‘Why would the virtuous son not suffer for the wrong that his father did?’ I answer: The son has done what is just and honest and has carefully lived his life according to all my regulations. For this reason, he will surely go on living!

The person who sins is the one who will die. A son will not suffer what his father’s corrupt actions deserve, nor will a father suffer what his son’s corrupt actions deserve. Righteous people will enjoy the consequences of their righteous behavior, and wicked people will suffer the inevitable outcomes of their wicked behavior.

But suppose that a wicked person stops doing all the sinful things that he once did and begins to carefully live his life according to all my regulations and do what is just and honest. If this happens, this once-wicked person will surely go on living! I will not put him to death.
I, Yahweh, will not treat him according to any of the rebellious things that he once did. Instead, he will go on living because of the virtuous things that he now does.
Indeed, I do not enjoy it when wicked people die. I do not want them to die! That is what I, the Lord Yahweh, declare. So, when they stop behaving wickedly, they will go on living.

But suppose a virtuous person stops doing what is just and honest and begins to behave corruptly and to do the same disgusting things that wicked people do. That formerly virtuous person will certainly not go on living! I will not credit him for the just and honest things that he once did. Instead, he will die because he has disloyally betrayed his promises to me and has committed many sins.
But you retort, ‘The Lord’s conduct is not fair!’ Listen to this, you Israelite people: It is not what I do that is unfair; rather, it is what you do that is unfair!
If a righteous person stops doing what is right and honest and commits sins, he will die because of the sins that he committed.
But if a wicked person stops doing wicked things and does what is just and honest, he will save his own life.
Because he witnessed all his sinful actions and stopped revolting against me, he will surely go on living; he will not die.
But you people of Israel say, ‘The Lord does not act fairly.’ You people of Israel, it is not my ways that are unfair; rather, it is your ways that are unfair.

Therefore, Israelite people, I, Yahweh, will judge each one of you according to what you have done. Repent, and stop all your rebellious behavior, so that your sins will not cause you to die! This is what I, the Lord Yahweh, declare!
Stop revolting against me. Remove your rebellious behavior as if it were garbage to throw away! Change the way you think and the way you live. Israelite people, there is no reason for you to die!
I do not enjoy it when any person must die! So repent so that you might live! This is what I, the Lord Yahweh, declare!”
Yahweh said to me, “Lament over the ruling officials of Israel.
Say this to the Israelite people: ‘Imagine—your mother was such a lioness; she lay herself among male lions and bore more and more cubs surrounded by young, virile lions.
She reared one of her cubs until he was a virile lion, teaching him to hunt and kill wild animals; he even learned to kill and eat people!
When people from other nations learned about him, they captured him in a pit. They put hooks on him and dragged him away to Egypt.
The young lion’s mother waited for him to return, but she was utterly disappointed when he never came back. So she reared another one of her cubs, and made him into another virile lion.
He prowled among the other lions, and he too became a virile lion. He learned to hunt and kill wild animals, and he even killed and ate people!
He consorted with his widows, and he razed cities into ruins. When he roared, everyone who lived in the land ran away.
But then people from the surrounding nations arrayed themselves against from every province. They spread their net over him; they trapped him in a pit.
They shut him in a cage, They put hooks on him and dragged him away to the king of Babylon. They locked him in a prison so that the people on the mountains of Israel would never again hear him roar.
Imagine—your mother was like a flourishing, verdant vine that somebody planted beside flowing water. Because there was plenty of water, she had many canes and produced many grapes.
It had strong, woody branches, suitable to become a ruler’s scepter. It towered high overhead, into the very clouds, and people could see how tall it was and how full it had become.

However, Yahweh became so angry that he pulled the vine up by its roots and flung it down to the ground. A hot east wind dried up its fruit, The vine’s strong branches broke off; they dried up, and a fire burned them up.
Now, Yahweh has transplanted that vine—your mother— in a desert, in a dry and arid region.
A fire has spread out from the stem of its shoot, which has burned up all its fruit. So now, no strong branch remains on it— no branch that could become a ruler’s scepter.’

In the seventh year after the Babylonians forcibly removed King Jehoiachin and the many other citizens of Jerusalem and relocated them to Babylon—on the tenth day of the fifth month—some of the Israelite elders came to inquire of Yahweh what they should do. So, they sat down in front of me.
Then Yahweh gave me this message. He said,

“Human, speak to the Israelite elders and tell them, ‘This is what the Lord Yahweh says: “So you have come to inquire of me what you should do! I swear by myself that I refuse to let you ask me anything.” That is what the Lord Yahweh declares.’
Human, you must announce my judgment against those elders! Yes, you must pronounce my judgment! Make them acknowledge the disgusting and illicit things that their ancestors did.

Tell them that this is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say: ‘When I chose your ancestors to be my people, I solemnly swore an oath to the descendents of Jacob. While they lived as slaves in Egypt, I demonstrated to them who I am. I solemnly swore to them that my name was Yahweh, and that I was their God.

At that same time, I solemnly promised them that I would bring them out of the Egyptian territories into a land that I had explored and selected for them. The soil in that land was very fertile and produced good crops abundantly—it was the most beautiful of all lands.

I said to them, “Every one of you must discard the abhorrent idols that attract your attention and devotion, and you must not make yourselves ritually unfit to worship me by revering the ritual statues that the Egyptians worship! I am Yahweh your God!”

But they revolted against me and refused to obey me. Not one of them discarded the abhorrent idols that attracted their attention and devotion, nor did they desert the ritual statues that the Egyptians worshiped. So I declared that I would completely vent my furious anger against them—right there in the Egyptian territories.

But I did not do this, because I wanted to preserve my reputation. I did not want the citizens of the nations among whom my people were living to think little of me. They had witnessed me disclose myself to my people when I brought them out of the Egyptian territories.
So I brought them out of the Egyptian territories and led them into the desert wilderness.
I told them how they ought to live, and I taught them my norms. Anyone who heeds these things will live because of them!
I also gave them the day of my Sabbath rest. I intended those days to remind them of exactly who I am and what I am like. I am Yahweh, who sets them apart to belong to me.

But the Israelite people revolted against me in the wilderness. They ignored my instructions and refused to live by my norms, even though anyone who heeds these things will live because of them! They also completely dishonored my Sabbath days. So I declared that I would completely destroy my people by venting my furious anger against them in the desert wilderness.
But I did not do this because I wanted to preserve my reputation. I did not want the citizens of the nations who witnessed it when I brought Israel out of Egypt to think little of me.

I also solemnly swore to them in the desert wilderness that I would not bring them into the land that I had given them. The soil in that land was very fertile and produced good crops abundantly—it was the most beautiful of all lands.
I swore this because they ignored my instructions, refused to live by my norms, and dishonored my Sabbath days. After all, they deeply desired to worship their ritual statues.
But I had compassion on them and did not kill every Israelite person; I did not completely destroy them in the desert wilderness.

I said to the children of the Israelite people who had died in the wilderness, “Do not live by the instructions that your parents followed; do not heed their norms, and do not make yourselves ritually unable to worship me by honoring your parents’ ritual statues.
Remember: I am Yahweh your God. Live according to my instructions; carefully heed my norms and do them!
Honor my Sabbath days as holy, so that they remind you of exactly who I am and what I am like. I am Yahweh, your God!”

But their children also revolted against me. They ignored my instructions and refused to live by my norms, even though anyone who heeds these things will live because of them! They also completely dishonored my Sabbath days. So I declared that I would completely vent my furious anger against them in the desert wilderness.

But I held back from punishing them and did not carry out my intent to destroy them, because I wanted to preserve my reputation. I did not want the citizens of the nations who witnessed it when I brought Israel out of Egypt to think little of me.
I also solemnly swore to them in the desert wilderness that I would scatter them among other nations and territories.

I did this because the Israelite people ignored my instructions, refused to live by my norms, completely dishonored my Sabbath days, and focused their devoted attention on the gods that their ancestors worshiped by honoring ritual statues.
So I permitted them to follow instructions that were not good for them and norms by which they could not preserve their lives.

I let them defile themselves by the sacrifices they offered to other gods when they ritually burned their firstborn children alive. I did that in order to devastate them, so that they would know exactly who I am and what I am like. I am Yahweh!”’
Therefore human, tell the people of Israel, ‘This is what the Lord Yahweh says: “Here is yet another way that your ancestors insulted me! They disloyally betrayed their promises to me.

I led them into the land that I had solemnly promised to give to them. But whenever they saw a hill or a verdant tree, they offered their sacrifices to other gods there. At those places, they presented offerings to the other gods that angered me, burning aromatics that gave off a pleasing smell and pouring out their wine offerings.
So I asked them, ‘What is this high place that you keep going to?’” (To this day, people call such places Bamah, a name that means ‘high place.’)’

Therefore, tell the people of Israel, ‘This is what the Lord Yahweh says: “You are making yourselves ritually unfit to worship me in the same way that your ancestors did! Likewise, you are being unfaithful to me by worshiping the detestable idols that they worshiped!

When you worshiped your other gods, presenting your ritual gifts and burning your children alive as sacrifices to the other gods, you made yourselves unfit to worship me! And you are still doing these things today! So I will certainly not let you ask me for advice, you people of Israel. I swear by myself that I refuse to let you ask me anything.” That is what the Lord Yahweh declares.

“What you are thinking will never happen. You say to yourselves, ‘We want to become like the other nations, like the empires of other lands, who worship ritual statues that they have crafted from wood and stone.’”
This is what the Lord Yahweh declares: “I swear by myself that I will rule over you by my great power and authority. I will show you how furiously angry I am!
By my great power and authority, I will lead you out from among the foreign nations and collect you from the territories where I scattered you. And I will show you how furiously angry I am!
I will lead you into a desert wilderness that lies among the other nations, and there, I will personally arraign you.
I will legally arraign you just as I did with your ancestors in the desert wilderness near the land of Egypt.” That is what the Lord Yahweh declares!
“I will count each one of you, like sheep passing under a shepherd’s staff, and I will require you to honor the covenant that I made with you.

I will expel from among you those who revolt against me and disobey me. I will lead them out of the territories where they have been living as foreigners, but they will never enter the land of Israel. Then you will finally understand exactly who I am and what I am like—I am Yahweh!”

As for you, people of Israel, this is what the Lord Yahweh says: “If you refuse to listen to me, then go ahead and worship your idols, every one of you! But you will never again dishonor my holy name by offering your gifts to your idols.

Because this is what the Lord Yahweh declares: “On my holy mountain, Zion, Israel’s lofty mountain, all the people of Israel, every one of them, will worship me there in the Israelite territories. There, I will accept them, and there I will require them to bring me their ritual contributions, the firstfruits of their tributes, along with all their holy sacrifices and offerings.

When I smell your aromatic sacrifices, I will reconcile myself with you. Then I will lead you out from among the foreign nations and gather you from the territories among which I scattered you. Then the nations will witness what I do among you and will recognize that I am holy.
You will finally understand who I am and what I am like when I bring you into the land of Israel, the land that I solemnly swore to give to your ancestors.

In that land, you will remember how you formerly behaved and everything you did that made you ritually unfit to worship me. As a result, you will despise yourselves for all the corrupt, wicked things that you did.

You will understand exactly who I am and what I am like—I am Yahweh!—when I act mercifully toward you to protect my reputation, and not according to what your wicked and corrupt behavior deserves, you people of Israel.” That is what the Lord Yahweh declares.’”
Yahweh gave me another message. He said,

“Human mortal, turn and face toward the south. Prophesy an ecstatic message concerning the southern region, and tell the Israelite people my prophetic messages concerning the scrub-forest land in the Negev.

Tell them about that forested part of the Negev, ‘Listen to the message that Yahweh is sending you! He says, “Pay attention! I, the Lord Yahweh, am about to start a fire in you, and it will ignite every tree in the Negev, both the verdant trees and the dry ones. No one will put out that blazing fire, and it will scorch every part of the land—from the south to the north.
Then everyone alive will see that I, Yahweh, started that fire. No one will ever put it out.”’”
Then I said, “Oh, Lord Yahweh! People are dismissing me by saying, ‘He is only speaking in figures of speech!’”
Then Yahweh gave me another message. He said,
“Human, turn and face toward Jerusalem. Speak out an ecstactic prophetic message against the temple there, and declare what I have to say about the people who live in the land of Israel.

Tell the people of Israel, ‘This is what Yahweh has to say: “Pay attention! I have become your enemy! I am about to send a warring army against you, and it will kill both the righteous people and the wicked people among you.
Because I am going to kill both righteous people and wicked people among you, I will send that army against everyone who lives in the land of Israel—from its southernmost parts to its far north.
Then everyone will understand that it was I, Yahweh, who sent that army and that I will not call it back until it has finished.’”
So then, as for you, human—exclaim an audible groan of your deep sorrow! Groan in anguish and bitter grief while the people of Israel are watching you.

They will ask you, ‘Why are you groaning?’ And you must answer, ‘I am groaning because of the news that I have heard about what is about to happen. When other people learn of it, all of them will lose their courage; they will become dismayed and terrified, and they will urinate themselves. Pay attention! A disaster is coming, and it will certainly happen. That is what the Lord Yahweh declares!’”
Yahweh gave me another message. He said,
“Human, declare my message! Tell the people that this is what I, the Lord, say: ‘I see a sword! A sword! Someone has sharpened it and polished it.

He sharpened it in order to slay many people; he polished it so that it gleams brightly, as if it were lightning! We have no reason to celebrate! This sword will cut down every wooden rod, even the royal scepter of my son Judah.
The sword’s owner polished it so that a warrior could grip the sword in his hand. He sharpened and polished it, in order to give it to the man who will use it to kill.

Human, mourn and loudly weep! After all, this sword will attack my people and all the local officials of Israel! I have decided that my people and their leaders will die by that sword. So slap your hand against your thigh to show how horrified you are.
I am putting my people to the test, and the sword will destroy the royal power of Judah, which shuns my warnings. That is what I, the Lord Yahweh, declare.’

So then you human, speak my messages, and clap your hands together to show that I have decided to punish them. Let that sword strike them once more— even a third time! That sword kills people; it is a sword that slaughters great numbers of them, closing in on them from every side.

I am doing this so that they will lose their courage and so that many of them will fall over and die. At every city gate, I have stationed soldiers with pointed blades. How terrible this is! Someone made that sword to flash about as it strikes; the soldiers will pull out their swords to massacre people with them.
Go on, soldiers! Slash your swords to the right! Again! Slash them to the left! Thrust your swords wherever your sword’s edge happens to go!
Even I myself will clap my hands to announce that I have finished judging them, and then I will no longer be angry. This will assuredly happen because I, Yahweh, have said it would!”
Yahweh gave me another message. He said,

“As for you, human, draw a map on which you have mapped out two routes for the army of the king of Babylon to march along. Both routes must start out from the same territory. Then, fashion a signpost and place it at the place where each route turns toward a major city.

Map out a route for that army to travel to the city of Rabbah, where the Ammonite people live, and map out another route for it to travel to Judah, to the city of Jerusalem, which possesses fortified walls.

The king of Babylon will stop and stand at attention at the place where the road divides, where the two roads begin. There, he will ask the gods to provide him with insight as to which way he should go. He will shake marked arrows and see which one falls out; he will ask his household idols what to do; and he will examine the liver of an animal that he has killed for messages from the gods.

He will receive insight that suggests he should go to Jerusalem and attack the city. It tells him to assemble battering rams to knock down its outer gates. It tells him to give the order to kill the people. It tells his soldiers to shout the battle cry. It tells them to array the battering rams against the city gates, and to construct a siege ramp that allows soldiers to climb over the outer walls. It tells them to build siege walls around the city.

The citizens of Jerusalem will think that the insight he receives from his gods means nothing. After all, they had sworn oaths of loyalty to him. But the king of Babylon will remind them of the violations of their oath that they have committed, and his soldiers will capture them.

So then, tell the people of Israel that this is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say: ‘The king of Babylon has reminded everyone how guilty you are. You have openly rebelled, and everything that you do shows how sinfully you have lived. Since he has reminded everyone of this, your enemies will forcibly capture you.’
As for you, you evil and ungodly ruler of Israel—the moment has arrived during which Yahweh will finally punish your sinful behavior!
This is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say: ‘Take off your royal turban! Remove your crown! Things must change! Consider the important unimportant, and the unimportant important.
I will utterly destroy the city of Jerusalem! Jerusalem will remain in ruins until the one comes who has the right to rule it; then I will deliver the city over to him.’

As for you, human, declare my messages and tell the Israelite people that this is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say about the people of Ammon and about how they mocked my people. Tell them, ‘Soldiers have drawn their swords to slaughter the Ammonite people; they have polished their swords in order to destroy people, so that they brightly flash back and forth as they kill with them.

Although your priests and prophets saw deceitful visions about you and gave you false insight from the gods, those swords will kill you just like any evil and ungodly person. The moment has arrived when Yahweh will finally punish your sinful behavior!
Soldiers, put your swords back into their sheaths! I will judge you in the very place where I created you, in the land from whence you came.
I will show you how indignant I am with you. I am so extremely angry that I will punish you, and I will deliver you to bloodthirsty, brutal men who are experts at destroying people.
Fire will destroy you like kindling, and you will die violently there in your own land. No one will ever remember you again. After all, I, Yahweh, have said this will happen!’”
Yahweh gave me another message. He said,

“As for you, human—you must pronounce my legal verdict against the city of Jerusalem. It is a city in which people murder and oppress other people! Inform the citizens of the city about all the despicable and indecent things that they have done.

You must tell them, ‘This is what the Lord Yahweh says: ‘You citizens of Jerusalem make people who live in the city bleed by murdering and oppressing them! By doing that, you ensured that it is now the proper moment for me to punish you. You have crafted idols for yourselves that harm you, and by doing that you have made yourselves unfit to worship me.

When you murdered and oppressed people, you made yourselves guilty. When you crafted your idols, you became unfit to worship me. Because of your actions, the moment when I will punish you will happen very soon. You will die soon! That is why I have caused the people of other nations to insult you and the people in every territory to laugh at you.
Both people who reside near you and far away from you will mock you. Your reputation is disgraceful, and your city is full of dismayed panic.
Pay attention! Notice how every one of the Israelite local officials who lives in Jerusalem uses his own power to murder and oppress people!
These local officials living in Jerusalem treat their fathers and mothers with contempt. They oppress the foreigners who live among them, and they extort orphans and widows.
Your local officials treat the things that the priests have set apart for service to me as if they were worthless! They dishonor my Sabbath days!

These men who live among you in Jerusalem spread false rumors about others in order to oppress and harm them. These people eat sacrificial food that they have offered to ritual statues at the shrines on Israel’s hilltops. They have done obscene things right in front of you, citizens of Jerusalem!
Israel’s local officials who live in Jerusalem have had sexual relations with their fathers’ wives. They have raped and abused women during their monthly menstruation.

One man despicably has sexual relations with his neighbor’s wife. Another man commits ritually impure obscenities with his daughter-in-law. Still another man in Jerusalem rapes and abuses his own half-sister, his father’s daughter!

Some of these local officials in Jerusalem accept illicit payments to oppress and harm people. They charge excessive interest when they lend money, and they profit by extorting their fellow Israelites. They have even forgotten all about me.” That is what the Lord Yahweh declares.

Now, pay attention! I have clapped my hands together to show how grieved I am about the profit that these local officials have extorted and about the people whom they have murdered among you, citizens of Jerusalem.
You will not be so brave, nor will you remain calm when I deal with you. I, Yahweh, have said this, and I will certainly do it.
I will forcibly disperse you among many nations in many different territories, and I will make you once again fit to worship me.
The people of other nations will see you bring disgrace upon yourselves. When that happens, you will finally understand exactly who I am and what I am like—I am Yahweh!”’”
Yahweh gave me another message. He said,

“Human, I consider the Israelite people to be like slag. All of them are like the bronze, tin, iron, and lead that people throw into a furnace in order to purify silver. They have become like the slag that remains after metalworkers purify silver.
So this is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say: ‘All of you are like slag. So, pay attention to what I am about to do! I am going to gather all of you together inside Jerusalem.

People gather metals like silver, bronze, iron, lead, and tin into a smelter in order to melt them by the blast of the smelter’s heat. In the same way, in my fierce anger against you, I will gather you together inside Jerusalem. I will deposit you there, and you will suffer things that will feel as though I am melting you.
Yes, I will gather you together, and because I am furiously angry with you, it will be as though I am blasting you with a hot fire. You will feel as though I am melting you inside that city.
Just as a metalworker melts silver in his smelter, so I will melt you inside that city. At that time, you will understand that I, Yahweh, have vented my fierce anger against you.’”
Yahweh gave me another message. He said,
“Human, tell the Israelite people, ‘You live in a land that remains in need of ritual cleansing. As long as I am indignantly angry with you, there will be no rain.

The prophets in the city of Jerusalem are conspiring! They murder people, acting just like vicious, prowling lions. Moreover, they seize people’s money and their valuables, and they murder so many men that many women in Jerusalem have become widows.

The priests in Jerusalem abuse my laws! They disrespect and disregard the spaces and items that belong to me, Yahweh. They do not make any distinction between holy spaces or things and ordinary, common ones, nor do they teach people the difference between what is ritually impure and what is ritually pure! They deliberately ignore my Sabbath days. By doing all these things, they publicly dishonor me among the citizens of Jerusalem.

Jerusalem’s local officials savagely harm the people who live in the city, as though they were vicious wolves. They harm people and even kill them in order to use violence to make a profit for themselves.

Your prophets intentionally deceive the people. They claim that I, Yahweh, give them visions, but their visions never happen! They tell lies when they claim to possess divine insight into a situation. They say, “This is what the Lord Yahweh says,” even though I never spoke to them!
Everyone else in Israel extorts one another and robs them. They violently harm people who are poor and destitute, and they unjustly treat the foreigners who live among them.

I searched among all the Israelite people for someone who would defend the land and plead with me on its behalf, as if they were repairing a broken wall. If I found that person, I would not destroy the territories of Israel. However, I did not find anyone like that.

So I have vented my indignant anger against them. Because I was furiously mad, I have destroyed them. I have made them suffer the consequences that their behavior deserves. That is what I, the Lord Yahweh, declare.’”
Yahweh gave me another message. He said,
“Human, {listen to this story.} There once were two sisters.
While they lived in Egypt, they engaged in prostitution. Even though they were young, they acted like prostitutes. Their lovers fondled their breasts there in Egypt and caressed their virgin nipples.

The older sister’s name was Oholah, and her sister’s name was Oholibah. I married them, and they gave birth to sons and daughters. Oholah represents the city of Samaria, and Oholibah represents the city of Jerusalem.
However, Oholah acted like a prostitute while she was still my wife. She desired other lovers, including the Assyrians. They were warriors
who wore extravagant blue clothing. They were governors and commanders—all of them handsome young men who rode horses.
She acted like a prostitute with all of them, the most desirable men of Assyria. She also worshiped all the ritual statues of the men she so desired, and so she made herself unacceptable to me.

She never ceased acting like a prostitute in Egypt, where men had previously had sexual relations with her when she was young. They caressed her virgin nipples and freely satisfied their own promiscuous desires with her.
So I let her lovers, the Assyrians, whom she had desired so much, dominate her.

Her Assyrian lovers stripped her naked and publicly shamed her. They apprehended her children and murdered her with a sword. Her lovers executed such judgment on her that women everywhere talked about her.
Her sister Oholibah witnessed all of this. Nonetheless, her illicit desires grew even greater than her sister Oholah’s. She acted even more like a prostitute than her sister had!
She desired the Assyrian men—those governors, commanders, and warriors who wore opulent uniforms and rode on horses, all of them handsome young men.
I observed that she had made herself unacceptable to me; both sisters behaved in the same way!
Oholibah increasingly acted like a prostitute. She saw depictions of men that someone had carved onto a wall—engravings of Babylonian men that an artist had outlined in bright red.
The engravings depicted men wearing belts around their waists and flowing turbans on their heads. They all looked like Babylonian officers native to Chaldea.
As soon as she saw them, she desired those men. So she sent messengers to them in Chaldea.
The Babylonian men came to her and had sexual relations with her. Their promiscuity made her unacceptable to me. After she had done this, she became disgusted with them and rejected them.
She openly flaunted her promiscuous behavior and shamelessly exhibited her naked body. So, I became disgusted with her and rejected her, just as I had become disgusted with and rejected her sister.
Yet she increasingly acted like a prostitute, recalling the days when she was young, when she acted like a prostitute in Egypt.
There, she desired her Egyptian lovers, men whose genitalia were like those of donkeys and whose seminal emissions were like those of horses.
So you, Oholibah, longed to behave as obscenely as you did when you were young—when the Egyptians caressed your nipples and fondled your young breasts.

For this reason, Oholibah, this is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say: ‘Pay attention to what I am about to do! I am about to incite your lovers to attack you—the very men you became disgusted with and turned away from. I will bring against you all of those who surround you:

the Babylonians and all the people of Chaldea, along with the men of Pekod and Shoa and Koa, and all the Assyrians with them. They are all handsome young men—governors and commanders, chariot officers and famous men, all of them riding on horses.

They will attack you with their weapons, riding chariots and wagons, and with a huge army. They will surround you, arraying large infantry shields and smaller shields against you and wearing their war helmets. I will let them decide what you deserve, and they will treat you according to their own customs.

I will act toward you in my zealous love for you. As a result, your lovers will treat you cruelly. They will cut off your noses and your ears, and those of you who survive will die by the sword. Your lovers will take away your children, and fire will destroy those of you who yet survive.
They will strip off your clothing and take away your beautiful jewelry.

So I will put an end to your obscene behavior and to the promiscuous ways that you began in Egypt. You will no longer expect help from the Egyptians or any of your other lovers, nor will you think about Egypt anymore.’
This is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say: ‘Pay attention to what I am about to do! I am about to let the people you hate dominate you, the ones you became disgusted with and turned away from.

They will treat you hatefully and take away everything that you worked hard to gain. They will leave you completely naked, so that everyone will see plainly how promiscuous and obscene you have behaved.
They will treat you this way because this is what your promiscuous behavior toward the nations deserves! You made yourself unacceptable to me by worshiping their idols.
You have behaved just as your sister behaved! As a result, I will make you suffer the same punishment that she suffered.’

This is what the Lord Yahweh has to say: ‘You will suffer just as your sister suffered—as if I forced you to drink from a deep and wide cup. Your cup will contain so much that people will laugh at you and deride you.

You will suffer so much, drinking deeply from this cup, that your sorrow will overcome you as if it made you drunk. You will suffer the horrifying punishment that your sister Samaria suffered when I destroyed her land.

You will experience all of your punishment, as though I forced you to drink your cup down to the very last of it and eat the broken pieces of the cup. You will suffer such agony that you will tear at your own body. I, Yahweh, have said this!’ That is what the Lord Yahweh declares.

So this is what the Lord Yahweh says: ‘You have forgotten about me and completely rejected me! As a result, you yourself must suffer the consequences that your obscene and promiscuous behavior deserves.’”
Yahweh gave me another message. He said, “Human, you must pronounce my verdict against Oholah and Oholibah. Tell them about the disgusting and illict things that they have done.

This is because they have committed adultery, and they are guilty of murdering people. They have been unfaithful to me by worshiping the ritual statues of other gods. They have even sacrificed the children that they bore for me by burning them alive and offering them to their idols as food.
They have even done this to me: On that same day, they desecrated my temple, and they dishonored my Sabbath days.

On the very same day that they butchered their children as sacrifices to their idols, they entered into my temple so that they could dishonor it! Moreover—pay attention!—they did this right inside my temple.
They even dispatched messengers to invite people who lived far away—and, look!—they came! For them, you bathed yourself, applied your makeup, and put on your jewelry.
You sat on a splendid couch. In front of it, someone had set a table on which you placed the incense and the olive oil that belonged to me.

A noisy, carefree crowd surrounded her. Along with the ordinary men in that crowd, people brought in drunken men from the desert wilderness. The two sisters, Oholah and Oholibah, put bracelets on their wrists and beautiful crowns on their heads.
Then I said about that woman, who had exhausted herself with her many adulteries, ‘Now one of these men will treat her as a prostitute—even her!’
Then one man had sexual relations with her as men do with a prostitute. That is how they treated both Oholah and Oholibah, those women who do obscene things.

However, virtuous men will condemn Oholah and Oholibah. They will sentence them the way people sentence women who commit adultery and women who murder people. After all, these women both have committed adultery and are guilty of murder.
This is what the Lord Yahweh says: ‘I will incite a mob against them, and I will let that mob terrify them and ransack their possessions.
That mob will publicly execute them by throwing stones at them and slashing them with their swords. They will kill their children and burn down their houses.
In this way, I will put an end to obscene behavior in the territories of Israel. Your punishment will warn all the other women, so that they will not behave as obscenely as you have behaved.

You, people of Israel, will suffer the consequences of your obscene behavior; you will accept the punishment for the sins that you committed by worshiping idols. At that time, you will know exactly who I am and what I am like—I am the Lord Yahweh!’”
In the ninth year after the Babylonians took us people of Israel away to Babylonia, on the tenth day of the tenth month, Yahweh gave me a message. He said,
“Human, write down today’s date, the exact date. Do this because, on this very day, the king of Babylon has besieged the city of Jerusalem with his army.
Quote a proverb to these rebellious people. You must tell them, ‘This is what the Lord Yahweh says: “Put a cooking pot on the fire; do it! Pour water into it also.
Put pieces of meat into the pot, all the best pieces— the thigh and the shoulder. Fill up the pot with the best bones!
Take the best sheep from the flock, and pile logs under the pot for fuel. Boil the meat thoroughly, until you have simmered the bones in the pot as well.”

So then, this is what the Lord Yahweh says: “How terrible it will be for Jerusalem, the city where people murder one another! That city is like the proverbial pot, whose rust stays inside it and never comes off. Take the pieces of meat out of the pot one piece at a time; do not throw lots to decide which pieces to take out.

Do this because the blood of the people whom the citizens of Jerusalem murdered, remains inside the city. They spilled that blood on bare rock; they did not even show respect for it by pouring it out on the ground and covering it over with dirt.
I will spill her own blood on the bare rock, where no one will cover it up in respect. I will do this so that I can rouse my anger and redress the citizens of Jerusalem.”

So this is what the Lord Yahweh says: “How terrible it will be for Jerusalem, that city in which people murder one another! I myself will increase my punishment against it, as though I were piling the firewood high under that pot.
Pile on more wood and light the fire! Cook the meat until it is done; Stir in the appropriate mixture of spices, and char the bones for the stock.
Then set the empty pot on the coals until it becomes very hot and its bronze glows red. Then the fire will melt away everything that is filthy inside it and destroy all its rust.
That city has worn itself out with all its efforts, but its thick rust still would not come off, not even when the fire burned it.

Jerusalem, the rust in that pot represents the shameful things that you have done. I tried to make you stop sinning, but you refused to stop. So you will remain sinful until I have finished punishing you in my anger.

I, Yahweh, have spoken. The time when I will punish you is coming, and I will certainly do what I have said. I will not hold back, I will not pity you, and I will not change my mind. I will punish you as you deserve for the way you have lived and for the things that you have done. That is what I, the Lord Yahweh, declare.’”
Then Yahweh gave me another message. He said,

Human, pay attention to what I am about to do! I am about to take away from you your wife, the one whom you love to look at. She will die suddenly. However, you must not mourn for her or weep, and you must not let your tears flow.

Groan quietly; do not mourn out loud for your dead wife. Keep your turban wrapped on your head and your sandals on your feet, and do not cover the lower part of your face, as mourners do. Do not eat the food that friends bring to those who are mourning.”
So one morning I spoke to the people, and that evening my wife died. The next morning I did what Yahweh had commanded me to do.
Then the people said to me, “Tell us what these things mean for us, the things that you are doing.”
So I said to them, “Yahweh gave me this message.

He told me to say to you people of Israel that this is what he, the Lord Yahweh, says: ‘I am about to allow enemies to destroy my temple and make it unholy, the building that you are so proud of, the building that you love to look at and that you cherish deeply. Also, the sons and daughters whom you left behind in Jerusalem will die in battle.
Then you will do what Ezekiel has done: you will not cover the lower part of your faces, and you will not eat the food that friends bring to those who are mourning.

You will keep your turbans on your heads and your sandals on your feet. You will not mourn or weep, but you will slowly weaken and die because of the sins that you have committed, and you will groan to one another.
Ezekiel is a warning to you; you will do everything that he has done. When all this happens, you will know that I am the Lord Yahweh.’”

{Yahweh also said to me}, “As for you, human, on the day when I take away from those people the temple that made them feel safe and strong, the beautiful building that made them rejoice, the building that they delighted to look at and longed for, I will also take away their sons and their daughters.
On that day, someone who escapes from Jerusalem will come to you and tell you what has happened there.

At that time I will enable you to speak again; you will talk with that man, and you will no longer remain silent. In this way you will be a warning to your people, and they will know that I am Yahweh.”
Yahweh gave me another message. He said,
“Human, turn toward the land where the people of Ammon live and prophesy against them.

Tell them that they must listen to my message. This is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say: ‘You shouted in triumph when the Babylonians defiled my temple, when they ruined the land of Israel, and when they took the people of Judah away to Babylonia.

So I am about to let the peoples who live in the desert east of you conquer you. They will set up their tents in your territory and live in your land. They will eat the fruit that grows in your land, and they will drink the milk from your herds.
I will turn your capital city, Rabbah, into a pasture for camels, and I will turn the rest of the land of Ammon into a resting place for sheep. Then you will know that I am Yahweh.’
This is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say: ‘You clapped your hands and stamped your feet to celebrate, and you gloated because you utterly despised the land of Israel and everyone who lived there.

So I am about to use my power to punish you. I will let other nations carry you off as plunder. I will destroy you completely, so that you no longer exist as a people in any land. Then you will know that I am Yahweh.’
This is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say: ‘The people of Moab and the people of Seir said that the people of Judah were no different from all the other nations.
So I am about to leave Moab’s frontier defenseless. The cities that guard its border, the finest cities in that land: Beth Jeshimoth, Baal Meon, and Kiriathaim,

I will give to the peoples who live in the desert to the east. They will possess it along with the land of the people of Ammon. I will do this so that the nations will no longer remember that the people of Ammon ever existed.
I will also punish the people of Moab. Then they will know that I am Yahweh.’

This is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say: ‘The people of Edom hurt the people of Judah because of what Judah did in the past. Because they hurt them so cruelly for what they did, the people of Edom sinned greatly.’

So this is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say: ‘I will use my power to punish the people of Edom. I will destroy both the people and the animals that live there. I will ruin their land completely, from Teman all the way to Dedan, and their enemies will kill them with swords.

I will use my people Israel to punish the people of Edom. My people will treat Edom in a way that shows how extremely angry I am. Then the people of Edom will know that I am the one punishing them.’ That is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say.

This is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say: ‘The Philistines attacked the people of Judah because of what Judah did in the past. Because they utterly despised my people, they tried to destroy them completely because of what Judah did in the past, for they had hated my people for a very long time.’

So this is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say: ‘Because they did that I am about to use my power to punish the Philistines. I will destroy the Cherethites, and I will kill everyone who still lives along the seacoast.
I will punish them again and again because I am very angry about what they did in the past. When I punish them for what they did, they will know that I am Yahweh.’”
In the eleventh year after the Babylonians took us people of Israel away to Babylonia, on the first day of the month, Yahweh gave me a message. He said,

“Human, the people of Tyre gloated over the city of Jerusalem. They said, ‘Aha! Jerusalem was the city that controlled the trade of all the peoples, but now enemies have destroyed her! The trade that used to pass through her has turned toward us instead. Now that Jerusalem lies in ruins, we will grow rich!’
Therefore this is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say: ‘Listen, Tyre! I am now your enemy. I will cause many nations to attack you continuously, one after another.
Their armies will destroy the walls of Tyre and tear down her towers. I will scrape away even the soil of that city until nothing remains there but bare rock.

The sea will surround the place where the city was and become a place where fishermen do nothing but spread out their nets {to dry}. I myself have said this. That is what I, the Lord Yahweh, declare. The soldiers of those nations will carry off everything valuable that she owns.
Enemy soldiers will attack the villages on the mainland that depend on Tyre, and they will kill the people who live there in battle. Then the people of Tyre will know that I am Yahweh.’

This is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say: ‘I am about to bring King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon to attack Tyre. He is the greatest king of all, and he will march against you from the north with horses, chariots, horsemen, and a huge army of soldiers.

He will kill the people who live in your villages on the mainland. He will build a wall of earth all around your city to shut everyone inside, he will pile up a ramp of earth against your city wall so that his soldiers can climb up it, and he will set up large shields to protect his soldiers as they attack.
He will bring up heavy beams and pound them against your walls to smash them, and he will tear down your towers with iron tools.

He will have so many horses that when they charge in, the dust that their hooves stir up will settle over your whole city. Your walls will shake from the thundering noise of his horsemen and his wagons and his chariots when he rides in through your gates after his soldiers have broken through your walls.

His horses will trample every one of your streets with their hooves. His soldiers will kill your people with their swords, and the sacred stone pillars that you were so proud of will crash to the ground.

His soldiers will carry off your wealth and the goods that your merchants sell. They will break down your walls and demolish the beautiful houses that you love. Then they will throw your stones and your timbers and your rubble into the sea.
I will put an end to the noise of your singing, and no one will hear anyone playing your harps ever again.
I will make you nothing but bare rock, a place where fishermen spread out their nets. No one will ever rebuild you, because I, Yahweh, have spoken.’ That is what I, the Lord Yahweh, declare.

This is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say to Tyre: ‘When you fall, the people who live along the coasts will certainly tremble, because they will hear your dying people groaning and your enemies slaughtering people all through your city.

Then all the rulers of {the nations along} the sea will step down from their thrones. They will take off their royal robes and strip off their embroidered clothes {to show that they are mourning}. Instead they will tremble with fear. They will sit on the ground, shuddering over and over, and they will shake with horror at what has happened to you.

Then they will sing a funeral song about you. They will sing, “How completely you have perished, you city where seafarers lived! Everyone praised you, and you were powerful out on the sea, you and the people who lived in you. You terrified everyone who lived along the coast!
Now, on the day when you fall, the people along the coasts tremble; the people on the islands in the sea shake with terror because you are gone.”’

This is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say: ‘I will make your city a ruin, like the cities where no one lives anymore. I will overwhelm you completely with disaster, as though the deep sea had risen up and its vast waters had covered you.

Then I will send you down to join the people who died long ago and went down into the grave. I will make you stay in the world far below the earth, among places that have lain in ruins since ancient times, together with everyone else who has gone down into the grave. You will never again have a place among living people. However, I will give glory to the land where living people dwell.
I will bring you to a horrifying end, and you will exist no longer. People will search for you, but they will never find you again.’ That is what I, the Lord Yahweh, declare.”
Yahweh gave me a message. He said,
“As for you, human, sing a funeral song about the city of Tyre.

Say this to Tyre, the city that is where ships come in from the sea, the city full of people that trade with peoples who live along many coasts. This is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say: ‘People of Tyre, you yourself boasted that you were perfectly beautiful.
Your territory lies out in the middle of the sea; the ones who built you made you completely beautiful.
You were like a magnificent ship. Your builders made all your planks out of cypress trees from Senir; they took a cedar tree from Lebanon to make your mast.
They made your oars out of oak trees from Bashan; they made your deck out of pine wood from the coasts of Kittim, and they set ivory into it.
They made your sail out of fine embroidered linen from Egypt, so that people far away could tell that it was you; they made your awning out of blue and purple cloth from the coasts of Elishah.
Men from Sidon and Arvad rowed you; your own skilled men, Tyre, were on board, and they sailed you.
The elders of Gebal and that city’s skilled workers were on board to seal up your leaking seams. Sailors from every ship that sailed the sea came to you to trade for your goods.
Men from Persia, Lud, and Put served as soldiers in your army. They hung their shields, helmets{, and all their other armor} inside your city; they are the ones who made you look magnificent.

Men from Arvad and your own soldiers stood guard on your walls all around, and men from Gammad guarded your towers. They hung their shields all around on your walls; they are the ones who made you completely beautiful.
Merchants from Tarshish traded with you because you had such an enormous amount of goods. They gave you silver, iron, tin, and lead in exchange for your wares.
Merchants from Javan, Tubal, and Meshech traded with you. They gave you slaves and bronze objects in exchange for your goods.
Men from Beth Togarmah gave you workhorses, warhorses, and mules in exchange for your wares.
Men from Dedan traded with you, and you controlled the trade of the people who lived along many coasts. Those people brought you ivory tusks and ebony{, a valuable black wood,} as payment.
Merchants from Aram traded with you because you produced so many things. They gave you emeralds, purple cloth, embroidered cloth, fine linen, coral, and rubies in exchange for your wares.
Men from Judah and from the land of Israel traded with you. They gave you wheat from Minnith, a food called pannag, honey, olive oil, and balm in exchange for your goods.
Merchants from Damascus traded with you because you produced so many things and had such great wealth. They brought you wine from Helbon and white wool.
Men from Vedan and from Javan near Uzal also traded with you. They brought wrought iron and the spices cassia and sweet cane.
Merchants from Dedan traded with you. They brought saddle blankets that people put on horses before riding them.
Merchants from Arabia and all the rulers of Kedar traded with you. They gave you lambs and rams and male goats in exchange for your goods.
Merchants from Sheba and Raamah traded with you. They gave you the finest of all the spices, all kinds of precious stones, and gold in exchange for your wares.
Merchants from Haran, Kanneh, Eden, Sheba, Assyria, and Kilmad also traded with you.
In your marketplace those merchants sold you fine clothing, cloaks of blue cloth and embroidered cloth, and multicolored rugs that they had rolled up and tied tightly with cords.
Ships from Tarshish carried your goods from place to place. People loaded you full of cargo, and you rode very low in the water far out in the middle of the sea.
Your rowers took you out into deep water, but a wind from the east will break you apart far out in the middle of the sea.

On the day when you sink, all of these will go down into the middle of the sea: your wealth, your wares, and your merchandise, your sailors and your pilots and the men who repair your leaking seams, the merchants who trade your goods, all your soldiers who are on board, and the whole crowd of people who are in you.
When your pilots cry out, the people who live along the shore will tremble with fear.
All the men who row will come down from their ships; the sailors and all the pilots who sail the sea will stand on the shore.
They will cry out loudly about you and weep bitterly; they will throw dust on their heads and roll in ashes {to show how deeply they grieve}.

They will shave their heads completely bald and put on rough sackcloth, to show that they are mourning for you; they will weep for you because they feel terrible sorrow, and they will grieve for you very deeply.
As they wail, they will sing a funeral song for you. They will sing, “No city was ever like Tyre; now she {has perished, and she} lies silent in the middle of the sea.”
When your goods went out across the seas, you gave many peoples everything that they wanted. With your great wealth and all your merchandise you made kings all over the earth rich.
Now you will break apart far out at sea and sink into deep water; all your merchandise and the whole crowd of people in you will go down with you.
All the people who live along the coasts shake with horror at what has happened to you; their kings shudder violently, and their faces show how terrified they are.
Merchants among the nations hiss at you to show their scorn and horror. What has happened to you will horrify people everywhere, and you will never exist again.’”
Yahweh gave me another message. He said,

“Human, say to the ruler of the city of Tyre that this is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say, ‘You have become very proud, and you have boasted that you are a god and that you sit on a god’s throne out in the middle of the sea. Yet you are only a human being; you are not a god, even though you think that you are as wise as a god.
You think that you are wiser than Daniel was and that no one can keep any secret hidden from you.
Because you are so wise and understand so much, you have made yourself wealthy; you have acquired gold and silver and stored them in your treasuries.
You have traded very skillfully because you are so wise, and so you have become even wealthier. Now, because you are so wealthy, you have become very proud.’
Therefore, this is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say, ‘Because you think that you are as wise as a god,

I am about to bring foreigners to attack you, soldiers from the nations that are the most ruthless of all. They will destroy the beautiful things that you created by being so wise with their swords, and they will make everything that made you look magnificent ugly.
They will bring you down to the grave. You will die violently, the way soldiers die in battle, there in your city out in the middle of the sea.

When the men who are about to kill you come to you, you will certainly not claim that you are a god. You are only a human being, not a god, and the men who stab you will have you completely in their power.
Foreigners will kill you, and you will die a shameful death like people who do not belong to God. This will surely happen because I myself have said it.’ That is what I, the Lord Yahweh, declare.”
Yahweh gave me another message. He said,
“Human, sing a funeral song about the king of the city of Tyre. Say to him that this is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say, ‘You were perfect in every way. You were completely wise and perfectly handsome.

It was as though you lived in Eden, the garden of God. You wore precious stones of every kind: ruby, topaz, and diamond, beryl, onyx, and jasper, sapphire, emerald, and garnet. Craftsmen mounted those stones in settings of gold. I prepared all of them for you on the day when I created you.
I anointed you and appointed you as a winged creature who guards. I placed you on my own holy mountain, and you walked about there among the glowing stones.
Everything that you did was perfect from the day when I created you, until you began to do wicked things.

Because you traded on such a huge scale, your merchants acted violently everywhere in your city, and you sinned. So I treated you as something unclean and drove you away from my mountain. You winged creature who guards, I destroyed you and removed you from among the glowing stones.

You became very proud because you were so handsome. Because you loved your own splendor, you ruined the wisdom that you had. So I brought you down and disgraced you completely; I put you on display in front of other kings, and they all stared at you.

Because you sinned so many times and traded so dishonestly, you made your own temples unholy. So I caused a fire to break out inside your city, and it burned you up completely. I reduced you to ashes lying on the ground, and everyone who was watching saw it happen.
All the peoples who knew you shake with horror at what has happened to you. You have come to a terrifying end, and you will never exist again.’”
Yahweh gave me another message. He said,
“Human, turn toward the city of Sidon and prophesy against it.

Say that this is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say, ‘You people of Sidon, I am your enemy! By what I do among you I will show how glorious I am. When I punish you and show that I am holy, then people will know that I am Yahweh.

I will send a deadly disease among you, and enemy soldiers will kill people in your streets. They will attack you from every direction, and they will kill your people inside your city. Then people will know that I am Yahweh.
The nations all around the people of Israel despise them, but those nations will no longer hurt them or cause them pain. Then the people of Israel will know that I am the Lord Yahweh.’

This is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say, ‘I will gather the people of Israel from the peoples among whom I scattered them, and by what I do for them I will show the nations that I am holy. After that, they will live in their own land, the soil that I gave to my servant Jacob.

They will live there safely. They will build houses and plant vineyards. They will live safely when I punish all the nations around them that despise them. Then they will know that I am Yahweh their God.’”
In the tenth year after the Babylonians took us people of Israel away to Babylonia, on the twelfth day of the tenth month, Yahweh gave me a message. He said,
“Human, turn toward Pharaoh, the king of Egypt and prophesy against him and against everyone who lives in the land of Egypt.

Tell him that this is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say, ‘Listen, Pharaoh, king of Egypt! I am now your enemy. You think that you are powerful and safe, like a huge monster that lies among the channels of the Nile River. You boast that the Nile River belongs to you and that you made it for your own benefit.

So I will capture you. It will be as though I put hooks in your jaws and made all the fish in your channels stick fast to your scales, and then dragged you up out of the middle of your channels with all those fish still clinging to you.

I will throw you out into the desert, you and all {your people who are like} the fish from your channels. You will fall on the open ground, and no one will pick up your body or bury it. I will give your body to the wild animals and the birds for them to eat.
Then everyone who lives in Egypt will know that I am Yahweh. I will punish you because you Egyptians failed the people of Israel when they relied on you to support them.
When the Israelites asked you for help, you failed them, and you wounded them badly. When they depended on you to hold them up, you could not, and you left them too weak to stand.’
Therefore, this is what I, the Lord Yahweh, say, ‘I am about to bring an army to attack you with swords, and those soldiers will kill both your people and your animals.
